# PRODUCT_DEBT.md — Known Inconsistencies & Target States

> The register of **known product/UX inconsistencies** — where the product diverges from the [Design System](../design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md), the [architecture rules](../../AGENTS.md#9-architecture-philosophy), or the [product principles](PRODUCT_PRINCIPLES.md) — and the target state for each.
>
> **Context.** DalyHub V2 is a redevelopment of a prompt-driven V1. Much of the debt below is *inherited* from V1's patterns and is precisely what the V2 [roadmap](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md) exists to resolve. As V2 is built greenfield on the shared foundation, resolving an item usually means "build the shared pattern instead of the legacy one." New debt discovered during V2 work is logged here too.

---

## How to use this register

- **Every entry links to a [ROADMAP_V2](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md) item** that resolves it. Debt without a roadmap home is a signal the roadmap is incomplete — add the item.
- **When you touch code carrying debt,** either resolve it (and check the box) or update the entry with what you learned ([campsite rule](../../AGENTS.md#12-development-workflow)).
- **Found new debt?** Add it with the [template](#entry-template) rather than leaving it undocumented. Undocumented divergence is the worst kind.
- **Priority:** `P1` (actively harms coherence/trust), `P2` (notable friction), `P3` (cleanup).
- **Status:** ☐ open · ◐ in progress · ☑ resolved.
- **IDs are unique and stable.** Never reuse a retired number; never issue a number twice. The next free ID is **DEBT-243** *(advanced 2026-09-04 by [the post-V2.8 product-strategy pass](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_9.md), which raised **DEBT-238 … DEBT-242** — the five concrete gaps its re-measurement of `main` at `6b4d4a8` produced that no entry named: a kernel Activity contract with no window read, an Analytics range vocabulary capped by an inherited eight, an obligation that cannot exist without an Asset or carry an amount, 447 broken local documentation links with no check to catch them, and no workspace-deletion path — and gave every entry it touched a dated V2.9 disposition. Previously advanced 2026-08-30 by [the V2.7 roadmap decision](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_7.md), which raised **DEBT-222 … DEBT-235** — the fourteen numbered findings of the RECALL programme definition, every one re-measured against `main` at `0d08cd6` rather than copied from the 2026-08-29 post-V2.6 audit, which had deliberately left its findings unnumbered for this pass; seven are scheduled as RECALL-00 and the rest one-per-item, and the same pass **corrected two of that audit's claims** — Review snapshots ARE compared (only multi-snapshot trend is unread), and `/today/waiting` HAS a palette command — so neither became debt. Previously advanced 2026-08-29 by [V2.6 FIND-02 + FIND-03 + FIND-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_6.md#-find-02--one-tag-vocabulary--delivered-2026-08-29), which **closed DEBT-182 and DEBT-48** — the two entries the retrieval theme was deferred *whole* for, twice — and raised **DEBT-217**, **DEBT-218**, **DEBT-219**, **DEBT-220** and **DEBT-221**, all five about surfaces it does not own — the last of them a journey that went red on 2026-08-29 because a seeded obligation's due date passed, MEASURED against the database and proven untouched by this branch. With them **V2.6 is complete**, and the programme closed every entry it took. DEBT-182 is worth reading for the MODEL question it left open and how it was settled: a tag is a workspace vocabulary row plus a polymorphic attachment, and the two rejected candidates are recorded with reasons rather than dismissed — an EntityLink type over a tag entity would have acquired a record page, a timeline, Activity and Search presence, every one an ADR-112 non-goal; a read-time aggregate over the three existing columns cannot give two spellings one identity, so rename stays unreachable and the entry stays open. The CASE rule is the decision with a user-visible consequence, and it is stated rather than assumed: identity is the **ASCII** case-folded key, because SQLite's `lower()` folds ASCII only and three engines have to compute the same value, so `Café` and `café` remain two tags — the failure that can be undone. The migration was proven the way this programme's own acceptance boundary demands, by seeding all three legacy columns through the OLD schema and reading the new one, and FALSIFICATION removed `asset_details` from it and watched three tests fail. DEBT-48's own prediction — *"almost certainly"* a kernel primitive rather than a Task-only field — is confirmed as fact, and its TASKS-04 warning held: no `label` field was added. FIND-04's recorded decision is the one worth carrying forward, because it is the one the parser's own philosophy did NOT settle: an unknown `#tag` is **offered** in the preview, never created silently and not left as literal words, because that rule is about phrases the grammar cannot recognise and `#` is an explicit marker it recognises perfectly. The offline answer is a test rather than a comment: a FROZEN pre-FIND-04 queue record replayed through the real route arrives as the words the owner typed, with no tag and no vocabulary created behind their back. Previously advanced 2026-08-29 by [V2.6 FIND-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_6.md#-find-01--search-answers-before-you-type--delivered-2026-08-29), which **closed DEBT-195** — the theme's only P2, open since DHDS-13 measured it, deferred by V2.4 and again by V2.5 — and raised exactly one entry, **DEBT-216**. **DEBT-214 and DEBT-215 were left to V2.5 STEER-05 rather than taken here**, while that branch was still open: taking 214 would have re-created the very collision its merge had just resolved. It has since merged and holds both, so the numbering is continuous and nothing was skipped. A gap would have been free; a number issued twice is not, and this register has already paid for that once with DEBT-45. DEBT-195 is worth reading for what the AUDIT changed about the recorded plan: the entry and ADR-112 both preferred deriving recency from the Activity stream, and the audit AGREED but for a reason neither had — `entities.updated_at`, the obvious cheaper authority, is maintained inconsistently across the detail tables (`d1-area-repository.ts` already carries an `EFFECTIVE_PROJECT_UPDATED_AT_EXPR` to compensate), so it would have silently under-reported every detail-only edit. The audit also found a SECOND empty state nobody had documented — a device-local `localStorage` list of results the owner had clicked inside Search, which had existed the whole time this P2 was open and is the evidence it did not close it. And the tie-break was found by FALSIFICATION rather than by reasoning: breaking ties on entity id alone is stable but arbitrary to a human, ties are the common case (creating a Task inside a Project touches both at one instant), and the kernel test was flaky across runs until `createdAt` broke the tie first. DEBT-216 is the one thing this pass found and deliberately did not do: a command-palette test still asserting that Goals have no creation command, which STEER-01 gave them — the product is right and the assertion is stale. Previously advanced 2026-08-28 by [V2.5 STEER-05](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-05--the-weeks-door--delivered-2026-08-28), which **closed DEBT-34** — the last entry of the Steering programme, and the one that had been open since REVIEWS-01 — and raised **DEBT-214** (which it also closed) and **DEBT-215** (which it deliberately did not). DEBT-34 is worth reading for what it did with the clause it could NOT meet: the entry's closing condition demanded Today's query count be *unchanged*, and nothing Today reads touches `review_details`, so the existence read had no statement to ride. The cost was measured (20 → 21, one bounded statement, identical in all three door states), pinned by a counting database so a second Reviews read fails the suite, and put back to the entry with the measurement — ADR-110 decision 7's posture applied to a budget instead of to storage. The read itself is creation's OWN idempotency lookup exposed on the repository contract, sharing one predicate with it, so "is there one?" and "there already is one" cannot become two rules. Its composition question — *which of Today's finite surfaces gives up space?* — was answered by MEASUREMENT rather than by taste: the six-column pairing was built first and rejected because at 1440 the foot row was already full, so the door is a band and no surface gave up anything. DEBT-214 is the reason the campsite rule is in `AGENTS.md`: measuring Today once, in its final shape, found TWO **serious** `axe` target-size violations on the same page — STEER-04's next-action link, floored only inside `@media (pointer: coarse)`, and the row title, floored nowhere at all — which were already failing `today-focus.spec.ts` and `goal-measurement.spec.ts` on `main`, both reproduced on a clean tree with a fresh database before any of this item's code existed. **Two further pre-existing `main` failures were found and deliberately NOT taken**, and they are recorded as **DEBT-215** rather than absorbed: three assertions in `goals.spec.ts` and `areas.spec.ts` still address the Area record's Goals tab as the `role="article"` Card that STEER-03 replaced with the shared `GoalStoryRow`. That is a different item's surface and a different pass's repair; fixing it inside a feature branch is how a branch stops being reviewable, which is V2.4-GATE-01's own recorded reason for the same choice. **Both of STEER-05's entries were RENUMBERED on merge, and the rule that says so is the one directly above it.** They were authored as DEBT-213 and DEBT-214 on a branch cut from `1ce1e75`; while that branch was open, the V2.6 roadmap decision merged and issued its OWN **DEBT-213** for the AI model and pricing registry. Two different subjects held one number, which *"never issue a number twice"* forbids. `main` keeps 213 because it is the merged and cross-referenced one — five links in `ROADMAP_V2_6.md`, one in `AI_PLATFORM.md` and one in ADR-112 — and STEER-05's pair moved up to **DEBT-214** and **DEBT-215**, whose only references were inside its own unmerged branch. This is deliberately NOT the DEBT-45 treatment: that collision kept one number twice because renumbering would have broken cross-references that already existed, and here the cheaper side had none. A collision caught while renumbering is still free is renumbered; one caught after is recorded. Previously advanced 2026-08-28 by the [V2.6 roadmap decision](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_6.md), which raised exactly one entry — **DEBT-213**, the AI model and pricing registry pinned to a single dated reading with nothing scheduling its re-verification — and closed nothing: a roadmap pass closes no debt, it gives debt a home. What it DID do is worth reading for the METHOD, because the decision it was asked to take and the decision the evidence supported were not the same one. The working hypothesis put to it was that V2.6 should be AI-first with *"one narrow, explainable assistant capability built on existing product-derived facts"*; the audit found that capability **already shipped on 2026-08-05** — ~9,800 lines across `app/kernel/ai`, `app/platform/ai`, `app/modules/ai` and `app/shared/ai`, four closed features including the Weekly Review assistant, an operational ledger holding no content, 29 E2E journeys, and [ADR-073](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-073-the-controlled-ai-platform--provider-independence-proposal-only-writes-application-enforced-budgets-and-an-evidence-contract) already stating every principle the hypothesis proposed adopting, several of them more strictly. So the question was never *"is AI ready"*. It is that **nothing in this repository has ever contacted a provider**, the credential is owner-held, and this repository is **0 for 3** on owner-held blockers clearing (a provider key open since 2026-08-05, DEBT-198 since 2026-08-22, `verify:production` since 2026-08-22). The decision turned on asymmetry rather than readiness: retrieval work makes the AI programme cheaper — a tag vocabulary and a recency source are inputs to the retrieval service DEBT-93 describes — while an assistant does nothing for search, so the dependency runs one way. It took the twice-deferred retrieval theme whole (DEBT-195 P2, DEBT-182, DEBT-48) into a four-item sequence, deferred AI with its **blocker named exactly** and its gate and sequence written down in advance rather than as the word "later", and **deliberately did not take** DEBT-102 (adjacent, and a kernel decision of its own) or DEBT-91 (a P3 off-theme, which is how a programme becomes a grab-bag). Two findings are worth carrying forward. **DEBT-91 was amended, not renumbered**: V2.5 made it simultaneously cheaper to close (`loadGoalStories` already IS the bounded fact block it asks for) and worse to leave (the block has no field for the owner's `set_aside` condition, so an assistant that ran would describe a Goal the owner deliberately put down as neglected — an untruth about the owner's own recorded judgement, arriving through the one surface they cannot correct by looking beside it). And the pass corrected a **premise it was handed**: V2.5 was described as complete, and [STEER-05](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-05--the-weeks-door--delivered-2026-08-28) is still ☐ — so DEBT-34's Today half is not closed, is not V2.6's, and V2.6 does not begin until V2.5 finishes. The pattern is now frequent enough to be worth naming: **two branches open at once will both reach for the next free number, and the file cannot stop them — only the merge can.** Take the next free ID as late as you can, and re-check it when you rebase.
- **Close only on evidence.** An entry moves to ☑ when the source code *and* its tests prove it, cited in the entry. "It should be fixed by now" is not evidence.
- **Resolving an entry changes its heading, and therefore its anchor — repair the links in the same PR.** Every entry here is linked by id from roadmaps, ADRs and module docs, and the anchor is computed from the *whole* heading text, so appending `— **RESOLVED 2026-09-04**` breaks every existing link to it. Repair each link to the new anchor; **never rename the heading back**, because the resolution is the record. `pnpm run docs:links:check` finds them all and `Static` fails on the first one that is left ([AGENTS.md §12](../../AGENTS.md#12-development-workflow), V2.9 INS-00). This is not a nicety: before the check existed, 254 anchors had drifted this exact way and 115 of the failures were links into this file.

## V2 release closure review — 2026-08-01

Every open entry was re-read against the code on `main` for the
[V2 release closure](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#change-log-for-this-roadmap). The
question asked of each was narrow and specific: **does this block the V2 release?**
An entry blocks only if it is a release blocker, a data-integrity risk, a security
or workspace-isolation risk, a broken primary workflow, a materially misleading
user-facing behaviour, or a consistently failing required test. Nothing else was
touched — a release closure is not a licence to refactor.

**Verdict: no open debt item blocks the V2 release.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Blocks V2** | **None.** Two release blockers were found during the closure and both are fixed; both were E2E-gate defects, recorded under [DEBT-41](#-debt-41--the-e2e-suite-is-unreliable-on-main-so-ci-is-green-claims-are-unverifiable--p1--resolved-2026-08-02). |
| **Closed by this review (7)** | [DEBT-04](#-debt-04--filter-inconsistencies-across-lists--p2--resolved-2026-08-01), [DEBT-05](#-debt-05--legacy-modals-instead-of-the-drawer--p2--resolved-2026-08-01), [DEBT-06](#-debt-06--navigation-inconsistencies--lost-context--p2--resolved-2026-08-01), [DEBT-09](#-debt-09--legacy-pages--old-layouts-outside-the-design-system--p2--resolved-2026-08-01), [DEBT-10](#-debt-10--inconsistent-emptyloadingerror-states--p3--resolved-2026-08-01), [DEBT-11](#-debt-11--accessibility-gaps-in-legacy-ui--p1--resolved-2026-08-01), [DEBT-12](#-debt-12--inconsistent-markdown-handling--p3--resolved-2026-08-01) — all seven are **V1-inherited** entries describing screens that do not exist in this repository. V2 was built greenfield on the shared foundation, so the roadmap item each one named as its resolution has shipped and the divergence each one described has no code left to be true of. Each entry now carries its resolution and its evidence. Where a *narrower*, genuinely-V2 concern survives, it is named and stays open — that is not the same entry, and it was not folded in to make a count look better. |
| **Retained, genuine, not blocking (39)** | Everything else still marked ☐/◐ below (30 ☐ and 9 ◐, counted from the entry headings). [DEBT-63](#-debt-63--load-more-could-silently-drop-a-page--p1--resolved-2026-08-01), raised and then RESOLVED by this closure, is not among them — it turned out to be a P1 product defect rather than the P3 test curiosity it was first filed as. All are P2 or P3 after the two reclassifications above — **the register now carries no open P1 except [DEBT-41](#-debt-41--the-e2e-suite-is-unreliable-on-main-so-ci-is-green-claims-are-unverifiable--p1--resolved-2026-08-02)**, which is deliberately held open until `main` is green after this merges *(that condition was met and DEBT-41 closed on 2026-08-02, and the register carried **no open P1** from then until 2026-08-08, when [DEBT-106](#-debt-106--mains-e2e-suite-is-broadly-red-36-journeys-across-19-spec-files-fail-for-reasons-unrelated-to-the-change-that-found-them--p1--resolved-2026-08-09) was raised P2 → P1 on the same evidence DEBT-41 was closed for)*. None of the 39 touches data integrity, workspace isolation, or a primary workflow. |
| **Severity changes** | [DEBT-01](#-debt-01--duplicate-card-implementations-per-module--p2) and [DEBT-02](#-debt-02--inconsistent-record-headerslayouts--p2) drop **P1 → P2**. Both were P1 when the product had a bespoke card and a bespoke header per module. Today the shared Card and the shared Record Layout are what every collection and every canonical record composes, and what remains of each entry is **one deliberate, documented Diary exception** with a stated reason. A single accepted exception is friction, not a coherence failure — and calling it P1 alongside genuine P1s devalues the label. |

**Target releases.** Every open entry is targeted at **V2.1 or later** and is reachable
from the roadmap item that owns it. The mapping that matters for the release:

- **V2.1, because a named V2.1 roadmap item resolves them:**

## Debt register

### ☑ UIX-06 — whole-application convergence (page origin, control baseline, count line, task-row columns, D1) — **RESOLVED 2026-08-11**

- **Current issue (was).** Five module-at-a-time redesigns left the product coherent within each module and divergent between them. A single BEFORE suite — every index, every detail family and the shared overlays, captured in one run at the same widths in both appearances — showed seven classes of drift: **three page origins** at 1280 (a collection's title 40px right of Today's and Analytics' behind an entity badge; Settings' 16px left of both, at a title rung six points smaller); a **control baseline that was the size and shape of nothing else** (36px on 4px corners against `.dh-btn`'s 45px on `--app-shape-control`), with the user-agent select chevron shipping in four collection headers; **five conventions for one subtitle** across nine collections, one of which showed the current view's NAME instead of a count and two of which said "1 notes loaded"; **D18's two trailing columns never actually aligned** (six consecutive Project marks at x = 630, 510, 724, 672, 638, 670, with titles ellipsised beside 200px of empty row); **two differently-drawn control rails on the Goals screen**; **three card treatments against D1's one**; and a **dark appearance that had not been reviewed as first-class** — the top bar's search field had no visible container at all in dark, because `card-subtle` and `app-bar` generate to the same value.
- **Resolved by.** One control baseline in `base.css` for every native control, which also draws the select chevron (D31) and let three module-local copies be deleted; `PaneHeader` no longer resolving a glyph from `entityType`, so all thirteen page origins agree (D30); one shared `collectionCountLabel`; a real trailing TRACK on the task row (`.dh-card__support` → `display: contents`, a fixed date column, no auto margins, and the low tier off the row per D32) measured to one Project x and one date right edge at every width from 320 to 1920; the Goals status rail moved into the filter band; D1 extended to `.dh-card`, `.dh-region-card`, the empty state and the Settings group; and `surface-sunken` under the top bar's search.
- **Also fixed.** A 1:1 contrast failure the not-found work surfaced — `.page a` / `.dh-pane-body a` repainted an `<a class="dh-btn">` in the link colour, so a filled button's label was the same colour as its container, in both appearances. And the not-found route itself, which was still the framework template's "404" on a bare canvas with no way back.
- **Related roadmap item.** [UIX-06](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_2.md); record in [`UIX_06_WHOLE_APP_CONVERGENCE_2026_08.md`](../design/UIX_06_WHOLE_APP_CONVERGENCE_2026_08.md).

### ☑ UIQ-013 / UIQ-014 / UIQ-021 — collection view switchers, the Reviews primary action, and overflow-menu viewport placement — **RESOLVED 2026-08-07 (#130)**

- **Current issue (was).** Three findings the August 2026 UI quality audit recorded rather than fixed, because each needed a shared change too broad for an audit PR. **UIQ-013**: view switchers rendered four ways — the shared segmented control (Projects/Goals/Notes/Tasks), pill tabs under the header (People), pill rows inside the pane header (Assets/Reviews) and loose segment links in a content toolbar (Meetings) — three selected-state treatments, two corner radii, and three of the four below the 44px target. **UIQ-014**: "New Review" rendered beside the view pills instead of the shared primary slot. **UIQ-021**: the one shared menu always opened below its trigger with no max-height and no flip, so a ~713px Tasks row menu opened low on an 800px viewport ran past the bottom.
- **Resolved by.** One documented [collection-header anatomy](../design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md#the-collection-header-anatomy-uiq-013uiq-014) with fixed semantic ownership of its slots; ONE [view switcher](../design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md#the-view-switcher-uiq-013) (`~/shared/view-switcher`) that eight collections and Diary now render, with the `SegmentedFilter` wrapper kept for genuine in-content filters; the primary action in the shared slot on every collection, with an intentional two-row narrow composition instead of accidental wrapping; and viewport-aware flip/clamp/scroll placement in the one shared menu, with the decision logic as a pure, unit-tested function.
- **Also removed.** A `projects.css` rule that turned EVERY `.dh-segmented` in the product into a two-column grid below 30rem — a module stylesheet deciding how a shared primitive degrades, and the reason the four Review scopes rendered as a 2×2 block with the container's rounded ends mid-row.
- **Not done here.** UIQ-011 and UIQ-012 remained open. **UIQ-011 was then resolved by [#131](../design/RECORD_SCREEN_CONVERGENCE_2026_08.md)** — see immediately below; UIQ-012 is still open.

### ☑ UIQ-011 — Person record exposes eight equally-weighted actions — P3 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-08 (#131)**

- **Original issue.** The Person record's Summary carried eight tonal pills at one weight (Call, Email, New Task, Diary entry, New Meeting, New Note, Copy email, Copy phone), where the Quick Actions contract says a curated two or three live on the surface and the tail lives in the overflow and the Command Palette. A greyed-out Call on a person with no phone number was also a control that could never do anything.
- **Resolved (#131).** **Call and Email are the primary actions**, plus **Message** where the person has a mobile (`sms:` needs a mobile, not any phone — so someone with only a work number gets two actions, not a third that would text a landline). Each is rendered **only where the data behind it exists**: the sparse Person fixture renders no action group at all rather than a row of disabled buttons. The four capture actions and the two clipboard actions moved into the record header's shared DS-12 overflow, still carrying this Person's capture context (ADR-060) — nothing was removed from the product, and the copy entries are themselves omitted when there is nothing to copy.
- **And the surface around them.** The Summary had been restating the record header — the name, the pronouns, and "Site foreman · Whitfield Building Co." — so it read as a contact row with a button bar. Each of those facts is now stated once, in the header's context line, and the Summary keeps what the header cannot show: the person's face, their preferred name, and the relationship word. The stay-in-touch pill likewise appears once (the context line) with the panel explaining it rather than repeating it.
- **Evidence.** `e2e/record-anatomy.spec.ts` → "the Person action hierarchy (UIQ-011)": asserts exactly three exposed contact links on the full fixture, none on the sparse one, and every demoted action reachable in the overflow. Before/after captures in `assets/record-2026-08/` (captured, not committed; [`RECORD_SCREEN_CONVERGENCE_2026_08.md`](../design/RECORD_SCREEN_CONVERGENCE_2026_08.md) records what each showed).

### ☐ UIQ-012 — the Goal status "Open" reads as a command, not a state — P3 — **retained, with the reason**

- **Current issue.** A Goal card's status chip says "Open", which sits where every other card shows its ⋯ menu and reads as *"Open this record"* rather than as a state.
- **Investigated, and deliberately not renamed.** "Open" is not Goals-only vocabulary. It is the shared spine word for "not yet completed", used by the Goal chip (`goalStateLabel`), the Area's equivalent, the Goal search projection, and — decisively — by **Projects**, where `open` is a real `ProjectStateFilter` value in the repository, a documented segment (`All / Open / Completed / Archived`) and a **URL parameter** (`?state=open`) that is shareable and bookmarkable.
- **Why that settles it.** Renaming only the Goal chip would replace one inconsistency with a worse one: two different words for the same binary state on two sibling spine entities. Renaming both coherently means changing a domain filter value, a URL contract, the repository's typed state filter, the segment labels, the tests and the docs together — a vocabulary migration with a persistence-visible surface, which is exactly what this PR was told not to fold in. The audit's own instruction was to leave it recorded rather than guess.
- **Desired future state.** If the product decides "Active" is the clearer DalyHub-wide word, change it as one vocabulary change across Goals AND Projects — chip, filter value, URL parameter (with the old value still accepted), forms, accessibility labels, tests and documentation — not as incidental cleanup. **This needs the owner's decision, not an implementer's.**
- **Impact.** One word on one chip, in the one position on a card where the owner expects a control. It costs a beat of hesitation on a Goal card and nothing else: the state is never carried by that chip alone (the card also shows progress, and the record states its condition in prose), and no action is mis-fired, because the chip is not interactive.
- **Why it remains open.** It is a **product vocabulary decision the owner has not made**, and every implementation of it is worse than leaving it: renaming the Goal chip alone puts two words on one binary state across two sibling spine entities, and renaming both means changing a repository state filter, a shareable `?state=open` URL contract, the segment labels and their tests together.
- **Closing condition.** Either an ADR recording that `open` stays as the shared spine word for "not yet completed" (which closes this without a code change), or one vocabulary change landing Goals AND Projects together — chip, `ProjectStateFilter` value, URL parameter with the old value still accepted, forms, accessibility labels, tests and docs — with `?state=open` links from before the change still resolving.
- **Related roadmap item.** [DALYHUB_UI_QUALITY_AUDIT_2026_08.md](../design/DALYHUB_UI_QUALITY_AUDIT_2026_08.md) (UIQ-012, raised there); tracked with [DEBT-107](#-debt-107--eleven-recorded-not-fixed-findings-from-the-august-2026-ui-quality-audit--p3).

### ☐ RECORD-02 — Two records have no Settings tab, so their paperwork has nowhere to be demoted to — P3

- **Current issue.** [RECORD-01](../design/RECORD_SCREEN_CONVERGENCE_2026_08.md) gives every record's administrative metadata (Created, Updated, raw State) one home: a shared `RecordDetails` list in the record's **Settings** tab. Seven records have one. **Goals and Notes do not.** The Goal's timestamps are therefore demoted to the trailing `facts` line of its summary band, and the Note's "Created" relies on its Activity tab's `entity.created` event plus the print byline. Both are the contract's permitted "later in the record" fallback, and both are correct — they are simply not the same answer the other seven give.
- **Why it was not done here.** Adding a Settings tab to a module changes that module's information architecture, which PR #131 was explicitly scoped out of. Adding one purely to host two dates would also be a tab that is almost empty on arrival.
- **Desired future state.** Goals and Notes gain a Settings tab when they have a second reason to (a Goal's icon, a Note's default tags), and their Record details move into it. Until then the fallback is documented rather than silently inconsistent.
- **Impact.** Small and one-directional: the information is present on all nine records, but an owner who has learned *"administrative detail lives in Settings"* on seven of them has to look somewhere else on the other two. Nothing is missing and nothing is wrong — what is inconsistent is where the answer is.
- **Why it remains open.** It is **evidence-triggered, not blocked**. RECORD-01's own contract permits the fallback these two use, so there is no defect to repair; adding a tab purely to host two dates would ship a tab that is almost empty, which is a worse answer than the documented fallback. The trigger is a **second** reason for the tab to exist.
- **Closing condition.** A Goal and a Note each carry a Settings tab hosting the shared `RecordDetails` list, added in the change that gives that tab its second occupant — not before. Alternatively, an explicit decision that the summary-band fallback is the contract for records with no administrative surface, recorded in `RECORD_SCREEN_CONVERGENCE_2026_08.md`, which closes it with no code change.
- **Related roadmap item.** [RECORD-01](../design/RECORD_SCREEN_CONVERGENCE_2026_08.md); DS-02 (the shared Record Layout).

### ◐ RECORD-03 — A Goal record is still tall on a phone — P3
> **Reframed by UIX-03 (2026-08-10).** The cause has changed, so the entry has.

- **What UIX-03 changed.** The Goal's measurement section is no longer inside the summary band: it is the record's own top-level `feature` region ABOVE it, so the band is back to the definition of done, the contribution meter and the alignment state alone. That removed one level of container nesting and put the answer to "am I getting there?" first at every width — on a phone the metric strip, the bar and the state now sit above the fold instead of below the prose.
- **What remains.** The record is still tall, and not only on a phone. At 1280×800 the Goal's **tabs** start ~1300px down: the header (124px), the progress workspace (~290px unmeasured, more when measured) and the summary band (~740px — the definition of done, the contribution meter, the alignment state, its reasons, the contribution evidence and the timestamps) stack above them. Measured on `main` before this change it was 1360px, so UIX-03 did not cause it and improved it slightly; it did not fix it either.
- **What the fold anchor now measures.** `record-anatomy.spec.ts` asserts the top of the record's WORKING region, and UIX-03 taught it to prefer a declared `feature` region over the first tab panel. On the Goal that is a genuine improvement rather than a relaxation — the owner now lands on the metric strip, the bar and the status at 236px instead of on a definition of done — but it means the assertion no longer covers the total height above the tabs, which is what this entry is about.
- **Why it is recorded rather than fixed.** The fold anchor is specified at 1280×800 and phone layouts are permitted to recompose. The honest remaining fix is progressive disclosure for the history list (and possibly the pace facts) on narrow widths, which is a shared decision about record composition rather than a Goals one.
- **Desired future state.** A decision on progressive disclosure for long record content, applied through the shared Record Layout rather than per module. For the Goal specifically the likeliest answer is that the summary band's contribution EVIDENCE and the workspace's measurement HISTORY both belong in tabs — the brief's own suggested IA (Overview / Progress / Milestones / Projects) puts them there — which is an information-architecture change this pass was scoped out of.
- **Current issue, restated after the reframe.** A Goal record stacks a header, a progress workspace and a summary band above its tabs. MEASURED at 1280×800: the tabs start ~1300px down (1360px on `main` before UIX-03, so that pass improved it by ~60px and did not fix it). On a phone the same content recomposes rather than shrinking, so the tail is longer still.
- **Impact.** The Goal is the one record whose tabs an owner has to scroll to find, so its Projects and Milestones are effectively second-class on the record that exists to relate them. It is a *finding* cost rather than a correctness one — nothing is unreachable, and UIX-03 put the answer to "am I getting there?" first at every width, which is the half that mattered most.
- **Why it remains open.** It needs a **shared decision about record composition** — which regions may be disclosed progressively, in the shared Record Layout rather than per module — and the Goal-specific answer is an information-architecture change (evidence and measurement history into tabs). Taking it inside a cleanup pass would set a product-wide precedent from one module's symptom.
- **Closing condition.** `record-anatomy.spec.ts` asserts the Goal's TABS — not only its working region — begin above a stated fold anchor at 1280×800 and at 393px, with the rule that gets them there expressed in the shared Record Layout and applied to at least one other record, so it is a composition rule rather than a Goals patch.
- **Related roadmap item.** [UIX-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_2.md); [RECORD-01](../design/RECORD_SCREEN_CONVERGENCE_2026_08.md); DS-02.

### ◐ DEBT-01 — Duplicate card implementations per module — P2
> **P1 → P2 (V2 release closure, 2026-08-01).** The shared DS-04 Card is what every
> collection composes; UX-01 retired the last bespoke collection card (Meetings).
> What remains is ONE deliberate, documented exception — the Diary timeline node,
> split out as [DEBT-46](#-debt-46--diarys-timeline-node-is-still-not-the-shared-card--p3-deliberately-downgraded).
> An accepted exception with a stated reason is friction, not a coherence failure.
> **Target release:** V2.1 or later, with DEBT-46.

- **Partly resolved by UX-01 (2026-07-28).** Meetings no longer uses the bespoke
  `dh-meeting-card` collection; `/meetings` now composes `CollectionLayout`,
  `CardCollection` and the shared DS-04 `Card` with bounded search/sort/pagination.
  Diary's timeline treatment and any remaining specialised cards keep this debt
  open until audited separately.
- **Current issue.** V1 grew a bespoke card per module; the same entity looks and behaves differently in different places.
- **Desired future state.** One configurable shared [Card](../design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md#cards); every entity renders through it.
- **Progress (2026-07-27 audit).** [DS-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-04--shared-cards) shipped the one entity-agnostic Card ([`app/shared/card`](../../app/shared/card)) and Areas, Assets, Goals, Notes, People, Projects, Reviews, Tasks and Today all render through it. **Two V2 forks remain:** the Diary timeline node is a hand-rolled `dh-diary-entry` element ([`app/modules/diary`](../../app/modules/diary)) and the Meetings collection renders a hand-rolled `dh-meeting-card` anchor ([`MeetingsCollection.tsx`](../../app/modules/meetings/MeetingsCollection.tsx)) — neither imports `~/shared/card`, so neither inherits selection, quick actions, density, swipe or the shared a11y behaviour. Kept ◐ rather than resolved: the shared Card exists and is dominant, but the product is not yet card-uniform.
- **Update 2026-07-28 (PX-06).** The **Diary timeline node stays a deliberate, documented fork** rather than being forced into a Card variant. It is the strongest scanning surface in the product (subtype icon + badge + timestamp on a chronological spine), and every variant shape considered lost some of that for no user-visible gain — so PX-06 preserved the visual exactly and instead pulled Diary onto the shared pieces that *do* fit: the shared subtype-icon registry, the shared overflow menu and lifecycle, the shared create-label convention and one primary entry point per viewport. Meetings' bespoke settings section was retired onto the shared DS-10b surface in the same change. This entry stays ◐ for the Diary card itself, now as an **accepted exception with a stated reason** rather than an untracked divergence.
- **Impact.** One presentation, on one surface, with a stated reason. Nothing about the OBJECT differs — a Diary entry opens the same Inspector, carries the same activity and the same links wherever it is reached from — so what remains is a second visual grammar for a chronological spine, not a second answer to "what is this record?".
- **Re-verified 2026-08-25, and the shape of the residual has changed.** The premise *"one configurable shared Card; every entity renders through it"* is no longer the architecture: DS-08 replaced the single Card with a shared card FAMILY of five (`DashboardCard`, `MetricTile`, `RecordRow`, `EntityCard`, `TimelineItem`, in [`card-family.css`](../../app/styles/card-family.css)), precisely because one Card was the wrong object for four other jobs the product does constantly. The V1 defect this entry names — a bespoke card per module — is gone; what is left is that **Diary composes neither the Card nor the family's own `TimelineItem`**, which is [DEBT-46](#-debt-46--diarys-timeline-node-is-still-not-the-shared-card--p3-deliberately-downgraded) and is now a bounded adoption rather than an open design question.
- **Why it remains open.** It is a **container** for DEBT-46 and holds no work of its own. It closes when DEBT-46 does, and it is deliberately not merged into it so the V1-inheritance story stays traceable.
- **Closing condition.** Every collection surface in the product composes a member of the shared card family, with `DiaryTimelineBody` the last conversion, and no module stylesheet defines a card anatomy of its own — asserted the way the state-layer ratchet is, over the stylesheets rather than by inspection.
- **Related roadmap item.** [DS-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-04--shared-cards) (the shared Card) and [PX-06](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-px-06--cross-module-polish--copy-convention) (retiring the Diary/Meetings forks); tracked alongside [DEBT-31](#-debt-31--cross-module-presentation-drift-todaydiary-forks-terminology-and-capitalisation--p2--presentation-half-resolved-2026-07-28).

### ◐ DEBT-02 — Inconsistent record headers/layouts — P2
> **P1 → P2 (V2 release closure, 2026-08-01).** Every canonical record composes the
> shared DS-02 Record Layout — verified at closure across Areas, Goals, Projects,
> Tasks, Notes, People, Meetings, Assets and Reviews. The single exception is the
> Diary entry, presented through the DS-10 Inspector, which is a deliberate
> interaction choice for a chronological capture surface rather than an ad-hoc
> layout. **Target release:** V2.1, with [DIARY-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-diary-02--day-context-links).
- **Current issue.** Tasks, projects, notes, and people each have ad-hoc top-of-record layouts; no shared header.
- **Desired future state.** Universal [Record Layout](../design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md#record-header) (header + summary + tabs) across all entities.
- **Progress (2026-07-27 audit).** [DS-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-02--shared-record-layout-header--summary--tabs) shipped the entity-agnostic Record Layout and **every canonical record now composes it** — Areas, Goals, Projects, Notes, People, Meetings, Assets, Reviews and the shared Task record Drawer ([`TaskRecordDrawer.tsx`](../../app/shared/task-record/TaskRecordDrawer.tsx)) all import `~/shared/record-layout`. **The one exception is the Diary entry**, which is presented through the DS-10 Inspector rather than a Record Layout; that is a deliberate, documented interaction choice for a chronological capture surface, but it means a Diary entry has no record header, tabs or Activity tab like every other entity. Kept ◐ until [DIARY-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-diary-02--day-context-links)/[PX-06](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-px-06--cross-module-polish--copy-convention) confirm the Diary treatment as an accepted variant or converge it.
- **Impact.** None on any canonical record: the V1 defect this entry names — Tasks, Projects, Notes and People each with an ad-hoc top-of-record layout — does not exist in this repository. The one exception is a Diary ENTRY, which opens in the DS-10 Inspector rather than as a record page. That is an interaction choice for a capture surface, made deliberately and documented, not a layout that drifted.
- **Re-verified 2026-08-25.** Nine record types compose the shared Record Layout, and eight of the nine now also mount the shared `LinkedItemsTab` on it. Nothing has regressed since the 2026-08-01 closure audit; the entry's own closing statement is still true.
- **Why it remains open.** For ONE reason, and it is a decision rather than work: whether a Diary entry should become a record page (and therefore compose the Record Layout) is a [DIARY-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-diary-02--day-context-links) question about what a Diary entry IS, not a layout convergence. Until that is answered the exception is accepted, which makes this friction rather than a coherence failure — which is why it was re-rated P1 → P2 at the V2 release closure.
- **Closing condition.** Either a Diary entry composes the shared Record Layout, or an ADR records that a chronological capture surface is presented through the Inspector by design — which closes this entry with no code change. **A decision either way closes it; the absence of one is what keeps it ◐.**
- **Related roadmap item.** [DS-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-02--shared-record-layout-header--summary--tabs); Diary convergence under [PX-06](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-px-06--cross-module-polish--copy-convention).

### ☑ DEBT-03 — Multiple save patterns (autosave vs. explicit vs. modal) — P1
- **Current issue.** Different forms save differently; users can't predict whether edits persist. Erodes [trust](PRODUCT_PRINCIPLES.md#how-users-should-feel).
- **Desired future state.** One [Forms](../design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md#forms) system with a predictable save model per field type.
- **Resolution.** [DS-06](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-06--shared-forms--field-controls) delivers ONE shared [forms system](../design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md#shared-forms--field-controls-ds-06) in which the save mode is a **declared, visible part of the component contract**, never inferred: `useForm` for explicit Save/Cancel (dirty tracking, duplicate-submit prevention, draft preservation on failure, unsaved-navigation interception) and `useAutosaveField` for calm, deterministic autosave (`Unsaved`/`Saving`/`Saved`/`Couldn’t save`, stale-response-safe, retry). No modal-save pattern is introduced. The predictable model now exists design-system-wide; each product create/edit surface simply adopts it (there are no product forms today that still diverge).
- **Related roadmap item.** [DS-06](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-06--shared-forms--field-controls).

### ☑ DEBT-04 — Filter inconsistencies across lists — P2 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-01**
- **Current issue.** Each list built its own filtering; syntax, chips, and saved-view behaviour differ.
- **Desired future state.** One [Filters](../design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md#filters) system used everywhere, URL-reflected, with saved views.
- **Resolved (V2 release closure, 2026-08-01).** This entry described V1 lists that each grew their own filtering. No such list exists here. [DS-07](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-07--shared-filters) shipped the one entity-agnostic filter system ([`app/shared/filters`](../../app/shared/filters)) with a typed definition model, a bounded AND/OR expression, a pure evaluator and a versioned URL contract; [TASKS-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-tasks-03--tasks-collection-experience-filtering-sorting-grouping-and-saved-views) added persisted saved views over a validated declarative configuration ([ADR-059](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-059-the-tasks-collection-contract--one-declarative-view-configuration-server-side-filtering-and-grouping-and-saved-views-as-validated-configuration)); [MOBILE-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-mobile-01--fast-mobile-first-daily-experience) gave every collection one shared filter/sort/view sheet. **Evidence:** `test/unit/filters/`, `e2e/cards-filters.spec.ts`, `e2e/tasks-collection.spec.ts`.
- **The narrower V2 concern that survives is NOT this entry, and stays open.** Filter *depth* is still uneven between collections ([DEBT-20](#-debt-20--no-health-specific-project-filter-yet-ds-07-clause-builder-still-deferred--p3)) and two filter MODELS coexist ([DEBT-49](#-debt-49--two-filter-models-coexist-ds-07-expressions-and-the-tasks-declarative-configuration--p3--resolved-2026-08-08-x-02)). Both are P3, both are owned by [X-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-x-02--saved-views--cross-module-filters), and neither is "each list built its own filtering".
- **Related roadmap item.** [DS-07](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-07--shared-filters); successors under [X-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-x-02--saved-views--cross-module-filters).

### ☑ DEBT-05 — Legacy modals instead of the Drawer — P2 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-01**
- **Current issue.** V1 opened records in modals that lose context and can't stack or deep-link.
- **Desired future state.** Records open in the shared [Drawer](../design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md#drawer); modals reserved for true interruptions only.
- **Resolved (V2 release closure, 2026-08-01).** No record in V2 opens in a modal. [DS-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-03--shared-drawer) is the record surface everywhere: URL-backed (so it deep-links), history-correct (so Back works), focus-managed and stackable, and [MOBILE-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-mobile-01--fast-mobile-first-daily-experience) made it the whole screen on a phone using the same implementation and the same URL/history/focus contract. The modal machinery is reused only for true interruptions — confirmation dialogs, the command palette, the Inspector sheet — which is exactly the target state this entry named. **Evidence:** `e2e/drawer.spec.ts`, `e2e/record-lifecycle.spec.ts`, `e2e/task-drawer.spec.ts` (deep-link, Back/Forward, Escape and focus restoration).
- **Related roadmap item.** [DS-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-03--shared-drawer).

### ☑ DEBT-06 — Navigation inconsistencies / lost context — P2 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-01**
- **Current issue.** Navigating between modules discards scroll/selection/place; "back" is unreliable.
- **Desired future state.** Context-preserving navigation and restored state ([UX philosophy](../../AGENTS.md#6-ux-philosophy)).
- **Resolved (V2 release closure, 2026-08-01).** The three specific failures this entry named are each closed by a shared mechanism, not by per-module care: opening a record no longer replaces the page (DS-03's URL-backed Drawer over the collection), Back is reliable (the Drawer's close is a history pop, made idempotent per history entry when [DEBT-41](#-debt-41--the-e2e-suite-is-unreliable-on-main-so-ci-is-green-claims-are-unverifiable--p1--resolved-2026-08-02) traced a double-Escape carrying the user off the record), and a paginated collection keeps the owner's place ([UX-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ux-01--daily-driver-ux-ui-and-product-polish) replaced six near-identical paginators and two page-REPLACING links with the one [`useKeysetPagination`](../../app/shared/load-more/useKeysetPagination.ts)). UX-01 also fixed the rail and the phone bar disagreeing about the current module, through one shared rule ([`navigation-active.ts`](../../app/shared/shell/navigation-active.ts)). **Evidence:** `e2e/drawer.spec.ts`, `e2e/ux-01-daily-driver.spec.ts`, `e2e/px-03-navigation.spec.ts`, `test/unit/load-more/useKeysetPagination.test.tsx`.
- **Related roadmap item.** [FND-09](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-fnd-09--app-shell-routing--auth) + [DS-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-03--shared-drawer) + [UX-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ux-01--daily-driver-ux-ui-and-product-polish).

### ◐ DEBT-07 — Fragmented activity/history — P2
- **Current issue.** History (where it exists) is per-module and inconsistent; no unified timeline or audit trail.
- **Desired future state.** One [shared Activity model](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-005-shared-activity-model) rendered as Timeline/Activity Feed everywhere.
- **Progress.** FND-05 + DS-05 established the one event model and the one renderer, and Tasks, Areas, Goals, Projects, Meetings, Assets and People each adopted it rather than forking a per-module history. [PEOPLE-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-people-02--relationship-timeline) is the first surface to prove the harder half — a **unified, cross-record** history — without fragmenting anything: the Person Timeline reads the ONE Activity stream across the Person AND their linked records, through an additive kernel multi-anchor read, with cross-module event labels taken from the FND-06 module registry. No second timeline, relationship-event store or copied content was introduced, and [ADR-052](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-052-the-unified-people-relationship-timeline--a-derived-multi-anchor-projection-over-the-one-activity-stream) records the pattern any future cross-record history should reuse. **[MEET-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-meet-03--people--history-integration) (2026-07-28) is the first real test of that seam, and it held.** Meetings contributed genuine interaction history to the Person timeline through ONE manifest line and a multi-subject `meeting.held` event — no Meetings tab on the Person record, no interactions table, no `lastContactAt` column, no copied meeting summaries, and no People-module change at all (asserted by an architectural test). It also **removed** a small fragmentation the audit had not caught: the Person timeline was hand-rolling a Task-only entity destination, so linked Notes, Assets, Meetings and Reviews rendered as inert text; every reference now resolves through the ONE shared `entityDestination` helper. See [ADR-055](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-055-a-meetings-occurrence-is-a-durable-write-once-fact-and-attendee-history-is-one-multi-subject-activity-event). **Still open:** modules that render no Timeline at all; the workspace-wide Activity Feed has no product surface yet (only the dev fixture); and the seven other module Activity routes still carry the same hand-rolled Task-only destination the People route just shed — each is a one-line change to the shared helper, deliberately left out of MEET-03's scope rather than bundled into it.
- **Impact.** Low and shrinking. Seven record types already read one event model through one renderer, so "what happened to this?" has the same answer and the same shape almost everywhere. What remains is coverage, not divergence — a module that records nothing is silent, which is honest; it is not a module that records the same thing differently.
- **Why it remains open.** Two named gaps, both evidence-triggered rather than blocked: [DEBT-33](#-debt-33--settings-changes-are-not-yet-represented-in-activity--p3--resolved-2026-08-25) (a preference change writes no event) and [DEBT-103](#-debt-103--the-workspace-wide-activity-feed-endpoint-has-no-ui-consumer--p3) (the workspace-wide feed the model supports has no surface reading it). Neither is a second history model; both are the one model not yet reaching somewhere.
- **Closing condition.** Every module that records history reads `activity.listForEntity` through the shared feed — no module-local history table, no second renderer — and the two named gaps are closed or explicitly accepted in their own entries. An architectural test asserting no module owns a history table would close it structurally rather than by audit.
- **Related roadmap item.** [FND-05](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-fnd-05--shared-activity-model) + [DS-05](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-05--shared-timeline--activity-feed) + [PEOPLE-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-people-02--relationship-timeline) + [MEET-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-meet-03--people--history-integration).

### ◐ DEBT-08 — Ad-hoc cross-entity links — P2
- **Current issue.** Relationships were modelled per-feature; links aren't bidirectional or universally visible.
- **Desired future state.** Kernel [EntityLinks](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-002-entitylinks) with a shared link picker and backlinks.
- **Progress.** The kernel half is done: [FND-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-fnd-04--entitylinks) provides typed, bidirectional EntityLinks stored once, and [DS-06](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-06--shared-forms--field-controls) adds the ONE shared, entity-agnostic **link picker** that creates/removes real EntityLinks through that kernel (proven bidirectionally in an integration test). **First product adoption:** [TODAY-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-today-02--task-drawer) ([ADR-028](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-028-task-drawer-persistence-and-composition--the-additive-task-detail-slice)) — the Task Drawer's Links tab renders the task's real project/goal/area relationships and uses the picker to create/remove `task.relates_to` links through the policy-enforced, workspace-isolated server service. **Still open:** a shared **backlinks** surface, and broader adoption across modules; relationships are not yet universally visible in the UI. Left as in-progress rather than resolved; it completes when a backlinks view ships and more modules adopt the picker.
- **Backlinks half now done (NOTES-05 knowledge completion, 2026-08-01).** The shared `~/shared/references` surface reads the FND-04 graph directionally for ANY module, and the Note record's Backlinks tab presents it with a count, module-family grouping and a module filter. `dalyhub://` record links add a second way to CREATE a relationship from prose that resolves by stable id, and the shared `/links` endpoint gained `op=record-link` so a second picker reuses the same bounded, workspace-scoped search rather than inventing one. **Still open:** the backlinks surface is currently composed only by the Note record — other record types can consume it unchanged but do not yet.
- **Impact, corrected 2026-08-25.** The entry says *"relationships are not yet universally visible in the UI"*. **That is no longer true and has not been for some time.** Nine record types — Areas, Assets, Goals, Habits, Meetings, Notes, People, Reviews and the Goals workspace pane — mount the shared `LinkedItemsTab`, which reads the FND-04 graph from EITHER endpoint, so a relationship created anywhere is visible from both of its ends. There is one relationship model, one store and one picker.
- **What genuinely remains, stated narrowly.** The **prose-reference backlinks** surface (`~/shared/references`, `dalyhub://` links resolved by stable id) is composed only by the Note record. Other record types can consume it unchanged and do not. That is a reach question about ONE presentation, not an ad-hoc relationship model — the defect this entry was raised for.
- **Why it remains open.** Because a record that can be *written about* in prose should be able to show who wrote about it, and eight record types cannot. It is bounded adoption, not a decision: the surface exists, is entity-agnostic, and needs a tab per record type.
- **Closing condition.** At least one non-Note record type composes `~/shared/references` unchanged — proving the surface is genuinely entity-agnostic rather than Note-shaped — and a test asserts that no module creates a relationship outside `entity_links`.
- **Related roadmap item.** [FND-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-fnd-04--entitylinks) + [DS-06](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-06--shared-forms--field-controls).

### ☑ DEBT-09 — Legacy pages / old layouts outside the design system — P2 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-01**
- **Current issue.** Some V1 screens predate any shared system and don't match current patterns.
- **Desired future state.** All surfaces composed from [Design System](../design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md) patterns; legacy pages retired module-by-module.
- **Resolved (V2 release closure, 2026-08-01).** There are no V1 screens in this repository — V2 is a greenfield redevelopment, and every surface is composed from Design System patterns. Audited at closure: `ModuleComingSoon`, the PX-03 placeholder this entry's successors were measured against, is rendered by **exactly one** route — `/ai` — which is honestly deferred and says so. Every other module route renders real, shared-pattern product. **Evidence:** the only `ModuleComingSoon` import in `app/modules/` is `app/modules/ai/routes/index.tsx`; the two other files that mention it do so in a comment recording that they replaced it.
- **Related roadmap item.** The per-module Phase 2–13 items in [ROADMAP_V2](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md), all ☑.

### ☑ DEBT-10 — Inconsistent empty/loading/error states — P3 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-01**
- **Current issue.** Some screens dead-end when empty, spinner-block while loading, or show raw errors.
- **Desired future state.** Shared [Empty](../design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md#empty-states)/[Loading](../design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md#loading)/[Error](../design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md#error-feedback) patterns everywhere.
- **Resolved (V2 release closure, 2026-08-01).** The shared `EmptyState`, skeleton loading and error patterns exist and are what modules compose; [PX-06](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-px-06--cross-module-polish--copy-convention) swept the last forked/inert empty states off Today and made the copy convention *executable* rather than written down ([`app/shared/entity/copy.ts`](../../app/shared/entity/copy.ts) derives every empty-collection title and count label from the one identity map, so a module structurally cannot drift). Nothing spinner-blocks a blank screen and no surface shows a raw error. **Evidence:** `test/unit/empty-state/`, `test/unit/skeleton/`, `test/unit/feedback/`, `e2e/feedback.spec.ts`.
- **Related roadmap item.** [DS-10](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-10--inspector-settings-and-feedback-states) + [PX-06](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-px-06--cross-module-polish--copy-convention).

### ☑ DEBT-11 — Accessibility gaps in legacy UI — P1 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-01**
- **Current issue.** Legacy screens have keyboard traps, missing labels, and insufficient contrast.
- **Desired future state.** WCAG 2.2 AA across shared components and every module ([accessibility](../../AGENTS.md#15-accessibility-requirements)).
- **Resolved (V2 release closure, 2026-08-01).** There is no legacy UI to have gaps in. [DS-11](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-11--accessibility--responsive-baseline) established a three-layer strategy — `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y`, component/contrast unit tests, and an axe-core Playwright gate over real surfaces — and it is enforced, not aspirational: the WCAG 2.2 AA contrast of all five themes is asserted per theme rather than sampled ([THEME-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-theme-01--the-curated-theme-system)), and the gate has repeatedly caught genuine violations before release (the `aria-prohibited-attr` on the shared activity viewport, the duplicate `main` landmark on two create routes, the read-only sheet with no tab stop). **Evidence:** `e2e/accessibility.spec.ts`, `e2e/keyboard.spec.ts`, `e2e/touch-targets.spec.ts`, `e2e/themes.spec.ts`, `test/unit/tokens/`, and the per-module axe scans in light and dark.
- **The narrower V2 concerns that survive are named individually and stay open**, each P3 and each with a stated reason: [DEBT-14](#-debt-14--grouped-rolefeed-interleaves-non-article-children--p3), [DEBT-15](#-debt-15--listbox-options-wrap-a-focusable-result-control--p3), [DEBT-26](#-debt-26--rendered-gfm-task-list-checkboxes-have-no-accessible-label--p3--resolved-2026-08-25), [DEBT-50](#-debt-50--card-quick-actions-are-28px-on-a-narrow-viewport-with-a-mouse--p3--resolved-2026-08-25), [DEBT-54](#-debt-54--border-strong-is-still-below-31-where-it-is-a-decorative-border--p3) and [DEBT-56](#-debt-56--axe-reports-label-title-only-for-one-shared-selectfield-in-the-tasks-drawer-and-the-dom-says-otherwise--p3). They are specific, known and non-blocking — which is a categorically different state from "legacy screens have keyboard traps".
- **Related roadmap item.** [DS-11](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-11--accessibility--responsive-baseline).

### ☑ DEBT-12 — Inconsistent Markdown handling — P3 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-01**
- **Current issue.** Text stored/rendered differently across features; some paths risk unsafe HTML.
- **Desired future state.** One [Markdown pipeline](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-006-markdown-strategy) with a single sanitising renderer.
- **Resolved (V2 release closure, 2026-08-01).** [FND-08](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-fnd-08--markdown-pipeline) ([ADR-015](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-015-markdown-source-and-safe-rendering-pipeline)) is the ONE pipeline: Markdown is stored as a validated, branded `MarkdownSource` and rendered through one deterministic `unified` chain that drops raw HTML before it can become DOM and sanitises against a single frozen allowlist. The "some paths risk unsafe HTML" half is closed structurally, not by review — `app/shared/markdown/MarkdownContent` is the **only** `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in `app/`, it accepts only the branded output, and **a repository test fails if a second one appears**. Notes, Diary, descriptions, Reviews and the export all consume it. **Evidence:** `test/unit/markdown-boundary.test.ts` (the one-sink rule), `test/unit/markdown-url-policy.test.ts`, `test/kernel/markdown-render.test.ts` (the XSS corpus, in the Workers runtime).
- **Related roadmap item.** [FND-08](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-fnd-08--markdown-pipeline).

### ☐ DEBT-13 — Reserved-spine-type guard lives in the D1 adapter — P3
- **Current issue.** The FND-07 reservation that stops the generic Entity/EntityLink repositories from mutating spine types/links ([ADR-014](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-014-spine-hierarchy-completion-and-rollup-semantics)) is enforced inside the D1 adapters (`d1-entity-repository`, `d1-entity-link-repository`) against a shared kernel identifier set. D1 is the only adapter today, but a second storage adapter would have to replicate the guard to stay safe.
- **Desired future state.** If a second adapter is ever added, lift the reserved-mutation check to a shared, storage-independent layer (e.g. a small guarded base or a kernel-level decorator) so no adapter can forget it — without coupling generic persistence to a mutable registry.
- **Impact.** **None today, by construction.** There is exactly one adapter, so there is exactly one place the guard can be forgotten and it is not forgotten. The cost is entirely prospective: the rule lives one layer below where it is decided, so a second adapter would inherit the obligation and not the enforcement.
- **Why it remains open.** **Evidence-triggered, and deliberately so.** Lifting the check now means coupling generic persistence to a mutable type registry to defend against an adapter nobody has proposed — which is the shape of speculative generality `AGENTS.md` §9.1 rules out. The trigger is a second adapter, not a date.
- **Closing condition.** Either a non-D1 adapter is proposed, at which point the reserved-mutation check moves to a storage-independent guard both adapters pass through and a kernel test proves a bare adapter cannot mutate a spine type; or an ADR records that D1 is the only adapter DalyHub will have, which closes this with no code change.
- **Related roadmap item.** [FND-07](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-fnd-07--area--goal--project--task-hierarchy) (revisit when a non-D1 adapter is proposed).

### ☐ DEBT-14 — Grouped `role="feed"` interleaves non-article children — P3
- **Current issue.** The DS-05 Timeline/Activity Feed ([ADR-021](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-021-the-shared-timeline--activity-feed--one-renderer-one-presentation-view-model-in-house-virtualisation)) renders a grouped, virtualised `role="feed"` whose direct subtree interleaves day-heading elements (and a load-more control) with the `role="article"` events. This is keyboard- and screen-reader navigable (semantic day headings, `aria-posinset`/`aria-setsize` on articles), but does not satisfy the strict ARIA `feed`→`article`-only child requirement, so the DS-11 axe gate disables `aria-required-children` (documented in `e2e/helpers.ts`).
- **Desired future state.** Revisit the grouped-feed structure so the `role="feed"` owns only articles (e.g. day labels carried inside each day's first article, load-more outside the feed) while preserving virtualisation, grouping and the reading experience — then re-enable `aria-required-children` in the axe gate.
- **Impact.** A screen reader in feed mode sees day headings and a load-more control as siblings of the articles rather than as part of them — so "next article" can land on a label. It is a navigation nuisance rather than a loss: every heading and control is still reachable, announced and operable, and the reading order is correct. The measurable cost is that `aria-required-children` is disabled in the shared axe scan, which means a genuinely broken feed elsewhere would not be caught.
- **Why it remains open.** The structure and the fix are in tension: the day grouping and the in-house virtualisation both need the headings to be siblings in the scroll container, and carrying a heading INSIDE each day's first article changes what an article is. It needs a DS-05 hardening pass with the virtualiser in scope, not a markup tweak.
- **Closing condition.** `aria-required-children` is removed from `GLOBALLY_DISABLED_RULES` in `e2e/helpers.ts` and the whole suite is axe-clean without it — which is the one measurement that proves the feed's children are what the role promises, and cannot be faked by rearranging one feed.
- **Related roadmap item.** [DS-05](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-05--shared-timeline--activity-feed) (revisit in a DS-05 hardening pass).

### ☐ DEBT-15 — Listbox options wrap a focusable result control — P3
- **Current issue.** DS-08 Search and DS-09 Command Palette ([ADR-023](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-023-shared-search--registry-driven-providers-runtime-orchestration-and-safe-navigation)/[ADR-024](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-024-command-palette--quick-actions--command-kinds-trusted-catalogue-authenticated-execution-and-one-shared-action)) render each `role="option"` around a real, focusable result control (a `tabindex="-1"` link so a record result stays middle-clickable / open-in-new-tab, or a button). Selection is driven by `aria-activedescendant`, so the inner control is never a tab stop, but axe's `nested-interactive` flags the nested focusable, so the DS-11 axe gate disables that rule (documented in `e2e/helpers.ts`).
- **Desired future state.** Revisit the option anatomy so the option element itself is the single interactive/link target (preserving middle-click, shareable navigation and keyboard activation) with no nested focusable — then re-enable `nested-interactive` in the axe gate.
- **Impact.** Small for a keyboard or screen-reader user — the listbox's own roving focus is what drives selection, and the nested link is never reached by Tab while the listbox owns the keyboard — and it costs the suite the `nested-interactive` rule, disabled globally. The nested anchor is what makes a result middle-clickable and its URL copyable, which is a real capability, so the anatomy is a trade rather than a mistake.
- **Why it remains open.** Removing the nested focusable means the option element itself becomes the link, which changes how the listbox activates a result and how the palette runs an ACTION (which has no URL at all). That is a search/palette anatomy decision, and doing it inside a cleanup pass would trade a proven navigation capability for a lint rule.
- **Closing condition.** `nested-interactive` is removed from `GLOBALLY_DISABLED_RULES` and the suite is axe-clean without it, with middle-click, copy-link and keyboard activation each still asserted on a search result — because the rule is only worth re-enabling if nothing was lost to it.
- **Related roadmap item.** [DS-08](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-08--shared-search) / [DS-09](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-09--command-palette--quick-actions) (revisit in a search/palette hardening pass).

### ☑ DEBT-16 — Minimal task-detail model (richer workflow status deferred) — P3
- **Current issue.** [TODAY-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-today-02--task-drawer) ([ADR-028](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-028-task-drawer-persistence-and-composition--the-additive-task-detail-slice)) added only the smallest honest task-detail slice: a two-value workflow `status` (`todo`/`in_progress`, with "done" derived from spine completion), a three-value `priority`, due/scheduled dates and a Markdown description. A richer workflow status (planned/active/on-hold/cancelled) was **not** modelled.
- **Partially resolved (TODAY-03).** The Waiting/blocking relationship was modelled by [TODAY-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-today-03--waiting) ([ADR-029](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-029-task-waiting--additive-state-a-reserved-entitylink-and-a-derived-first-class-display-state)) — exactly as intended, by extending the same `task_details` + EntityLink foundation (two additive columns + a reserved `task.waiting_on` link) rather than a parallel store.
- **Resolved (2026-07-25, verified 2026-07-27).** [TASKS-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-tasks-01--first-class-tasks-module) ([ADR-043](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-043--the-first-class-tasks-module-the-four-question-planning-model-time-sectors-somedaymaybe-and-derived-display-state)) closed this exactly as the entry required — by **extending `task_details`, not forking a parallel store**. Migration `0012_extend_task_planning.sql` widens `priority` to `p1..p4`, widens the workflow status set to `todo` / `in_progress` / `on_hold` / `cancelled` ([`app/kernel/tasks/task.ts`](../../app/kernel/tasks/task.ts), CHECK-constrained and validated in [`task-validation.ts`](../../app/kernel/tasks/task-validation.ts)), and adds `time_sector`, `commitment_state` (Active vs Someday/Maybe) and delegation columns. One shared pure evaluator, `taskDisplayState` ([`task-view.ts`](../../app/shared/task-record/task-view.ts)), resolves the precedence Deleted → Completed → Cancelled → Waiting → On hold → Someday/Maybe → In progress → Planned → Inbox. Proven by `test/unit/tasks/task-display-state.test.ts`, `test/kernel/task-repository.test.ts` and `test/kernel/task-planning.test.ts` (all green locally, 2026-07-27).
- **Follow-on.** One surface has not caught up with the widened vocabulary — Today does not exclude or label `on_hold`. Tracked separately as [DEBT-37](#-debt-37--on-hold-tasks-appear-on-today-but-are-excluded-from-tasks-active-planning-views--p2) rather than left inside this entry.
- **Related roadmap item.** [TASKS-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-tasks-01--first-class-tasks-module).

### ☑ DEBT-17 — Today search provider is fixture-backed, not over real records — P1
- **Original issue.** TODAY-02 made the Today *focus* section read real workspace-scoped tasks, but the DS-08 search provider (`app/modules/today/search.ts`, since removed) still built its candidates from the TODAY-01 fixtures (matching the seeded ids), because a search provider's `ModuleRuntimeContext` exposed the workspace context but not a repository/D1 handle. A search result for a fixture id that was not a real record opened the calm not-found Drawer.
- **Task half resolved (2026-07-25).** [TASKS-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-tasks-01--first-class-tasks-module) added a **real, repository-backed** Tasks search provider ([`app/modules/tasks/search.ts`](../../app/modules/tasks/search.ts)) that resolves live workspace tasks through the trusted `searchLinkTargets` seam, and the Today provider's `buildCandidates()` no longer contributes task results. There is now exactly one trustworthy task search.
- **Escalation before resolution.** The Today provider still contributed **fixture** `upcoming:<id>`, `project:<id>` and `note:<id>` results after real Projects, Notes, Meetings and Diary records existed, so global Search mixed **fabricated results with real ones** and a fixture hit opened a placeholder Drawer over `/today` instead of the canonical record. Presenting invented records as real search results violated [AGENTS.md §8 "fail honest"](../../AGENTS.md#8-ai-philosophy) and the [product principles](PRODUCT_PRINCIPLES.md). This was the same root cause as [DEBT-19](#-debt-19--projects-search-still-opens-the-fixture-project-drawer--p3) and was compounded by the missing real providers in [DEBT-36](#-debt-36--global-search-coverage-is-incomplete-several-shipped-modules-register-no-provider--p2).
- **Desired state.** Retire the fixture provider entirely once Projects, Notes and Meetings/Diary each register a real repository-backed provider; no shipped surface should return an id that does not resolve to a real record.
- **Related roadmap item.** [DS-08](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-08--shared-search) and [X-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-x-01--global-search-maturity).
- **TODAY-08 historical note.** The command-centre landing retired the calendar/notes/timeline *widget* fixtures and wired those widgets to real reads, but the Today **search provider** was out of scope for that item and remained fixture-backed until X-01. The Today recent-notes widget reads the TRUE newest notes via the dedicated `EntityRepository.listRecentByType` projection (newest-first, bounded) — not the oldest `entities.list` page re-sorted — so it is correct at any workspace size.
- **Resolved (2026-07-29).** X-01 removed the Today provider entirely:
  [`app/modules/today/module.ts`](../../app/modules/today/module.ts) now registers
  routes and commands only, and `app/modules/today/search.ts`
  no longer exists. Today remains a derived dashboard reachable through navigation
  and command-palette commands; it manufactures no records for Search. Production
  registry tests (`test/unit/today/search.test.ts`,
  `test/unit/module-registry/discovery.test.ts`) fail if `today.search` or any
  Today-owned Search provider is registered, and the real `/search` route test
  asserts the payload contains no `today.search`.

### ◐ DEBT-18 — Reserved cross-app keyboard vocabulary + a few Today actions lack a dedicated palette command — P3 — **the `?` half RESOLVED 2026-08-01**
- **Current issue.** TODAY-05 implemented the Today execution shortcuts (Arrow/Home/End/Enter/Space roving, `P`/`Shift+P`/`C`, `?`, `Escape`) but the broader reserved keyboard vocabulary documented in [`PRODUCT_EXPERIENCE.md` Part IV](../design/PRODUCT_EXPERIENCE.md) — the `g`+letter go-to chords, `j/k` movement aliases, `x` select, `o`/`e` open/primary-action, and `[` sidebar — is still reserved-but-unbuilt at the app level, and the keyboard reference is Today-scoped (a `help:shortcuts` Drawer key), not a global `?` overlay. Separately, four Today actions are keyboard-operable only through their visible controls, not yet a dedicated palette command: **mark waiting** and **change waiting subject** (the Drawer waiting editor — needs typed input), **choose a custom planning date** (the Drawer/bulk-bar date inputs), and **open Task Activity** (the RecordTabs tablist). Each is fully reachable by keyboard today (ADR-031 §31.5b) — the gap is only palette discoverability, not accessibility.
- **Desired future state.** A cross-app pass implements the remaining reserved vocabulary through the SAME one shared dispatcher (never per-surface listeners), promotes the shortcuts reference to a global overlay reusing the shared modal machinery, and adds dedicated commands for the four Today actions (e.g. a command that opens the waiting editor / activity tab / a date prompt) — extending, never forking, the DS-09 command system.
- **The global `?` half is done (2026-08-01, UX-01).** This was worse than the entry recorded: the reference's own first group was titled **"Anywhere"** and listed `?` as showing it — a claim that was false on every route but `/today`. The catalogue now lives once in [`app/shared/commands/shortcut-reference.ts`](../../app/shared/commands/shortcut-reference.ts), one shared renderer serves both hosts, and `AppShell` registers `?` through the SAME one dispatcher as a new **fallback** binding tier (appended after contextual and registered bindings), so it opens the reference in the shared `Sheet` everywhere without taking the key from a surface that owns it.
  - **Today keeps its Drawer host by decision, not by omission.** There the reference belongs inside the drawer STACK — that is what makes a task drawer beneath it stop owning the task shortcuts (`isTop`, ADR-031 §31.5b) — and a sheet sits outside that stack. The fallback tier exists precisely so Today's contextual `?` still wins there. Converging the two hosts is what remains of this half.
  - **It also surfaced a latent shared-component gap**: every Sheet built before this held focusable content, so a READ-ONLY sheet's scroll container had no tab stop (WCAG 2.1.1). Fixed in `Sheet` via an opt-in `bodyFocusable`.
- **Impact.** A documented vocabulary the product does not implement is worse than no vocabulary: an owner who reads `PRODUCT_EXPERIENCE.md` Part IV and presses `g` then `t` gets nothing, and cannot tell whether they mis-remembered or the product is broken. The `?` half — a reference that CLAIMED to work "Anywhere" and worked on one route — was the same defect and is fixed.
- **Why it remains open.** The remaining chords need a shared multi-key dispatcher (a `g`-prefixed chord is a state machine, not a key handler), and every one of them must not fire while a text field has focus. That is one shared mechanism, built once, with its own tests — not a per-surface listener, which is exactly what the entry forbids.
- **Closing condition.** Every shortcut `PRODUCT_EXPERIENCE.md` Part IV declares is either implemented through the one shared dispatcher or struck from the document, with a test that reads the documented table and asserts each row — so the reference and the product cannot disagree again.
