- **Still open:** the `g`+letter go-to chords, `j/k`, `x`, `o`/`e` and `[`; and the four Today actions without a dedicated palette command.
- **Related roadmap item.** [UX-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ux-01--daily-driver-ux-ui-and-product-polish) (the `?` half); a future cross-cutting keyboard item (post-[TODAY-05](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-today-05--keyboard-workflow)); the vocabulary stays reserved in the interim so nothing else claims those keys.

### ☑ DEBT-19 — Projects: search still opens the fixture project drawer — P3
- **Current issue.** PROJ-01 replaced the Today "Continue working" seam with the real project read model (navigating to `/projects/:id`), but the DS-08 Today **search** provider (`app/modules/today/search.ts`, since removed) still indexes fixture projects and opens a fixture `project:<id>` Drawer (the same fixture-search limitation as [DEBT-17](#-debt-17--today-search-provider-is-fixture-backed-not-over-real-records--p1)), so a project *found via search* opens a placeholder rather than the real record route now that real projects exist.
- **Resolved (2026-07-22).** The collection-pagination half of this debt is **fixed**: the Projects collection AND the Project Tasks tab are now fully **cursor-paginated** (versioned, scope-bound cursors mirroring the spine/EntityLink pattern, keyset ordering with a deterministic `id` tiebreaker, `nextCursor` on the kernel contract, and an accessible shared "Load more" affordance), so **every** matching project and task is reachable — not just the first bounded page. See [ADR-034](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-034-the-projects-module--a-read-only-projection-over-the-spine-no-second-project-model) and [PROJECTS_MODULE.md](../development/PROJECTS_MODULE.md). Only the fixture-search issue above remains open under this debt.
- **Desired future state.** Search resolves real projects and targets the canonical `/projects/:id` route (folded into the DEBT-17 real-search work). This does not block PROJ-01's calm single-owner surface. *(Today's "Continue working" already selects the most-recently-updated projects at the database via `orderBy: "recent"`, so the earlier loader-side recency approximation is resolved.)*
- **Related roadmap item.** [PROJ-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-proj-01--overview); [DS-08](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-08--shared-search); [PROJ-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md) (richer project filtering reuses the DS-07 clause-builder the state segment defers).
- **Resolved (2026-07-29).** X-01 retired the Today fixture provider and added the
  real Projects provider (`app/modules/projects/search.ts`) backed by
  `ProjectRepository.searchProjects`. Results target canonical `/projects/:id`
  routes and carry Area/Goal context plus Task progress. The actual `/search`
  Workers route test seeds a real Project and proves it is returned from
  `projects.search`, not Today.

### ☐ DEBT-20 — No health-specific project filter yet (DS-07 clause-builder still deferred) — P3
- **Current issue.** PROJ-02 surfaces project health on every collection card and explains it on the record, but the `/projects` collection still filters only by the restrained Open/Completed/All URL segment ([`SegmentedFilter`](../../app/shared/segmented-filter/SegmentedFilter.tsx)). There is no way to filter the collection to *just* at-risk / blocked / stale projects. Health is derived (not a stored column), so a health filter must be applied server-side over the same bounded facts, not a client re-sort of one page.
- **Assessment.** For a single-owner workspace the expected outcome — *recognise which open projects need attention without opening every record* — is met by the always-visible health cue on each card plus normal scanning; a dedicated filter is a refinement, not a requirement. The audit deliberately did **not** invent a second filtering system.
- **Desired future state.** A health **enum** dimension evaluated server-side over the bounded PROJ-02 facts — never replacing the Open/Completed/All state control.
- **Partly delivered 2026-08-08 by [X-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-x-02--saved-views--cross-module-filters--delivered-2026-08-08), and the desired future state changed.** A health filter now EXISTS and is server-evaluated over PROJ-02's own bounded facts: `project.health` is a typed module dimension of the shared cross-module view configuration, so `/views?show=project&p.health=at_risk` is a real, savable answer to "which Projects need attention", and the built-in **Needs attention** view includes at-risk / stale / blocked Projects across modules. The DS-07 clause-builder route this entry pointed at is NOT the path taken and should not be revived — [DEBT-49](#-debt-49--two-filter-models-coexist-ds-07-expressions-and-the-tasks-declarative-configuration--p3--resolved-2026-08-08-x-02) records why.
- **What genuinely remains.** The `/projects` COLLECTION itself still offers only the Open/Completed/All segmented control; adopting the shared view configuration inside that collection's own header is the remaining work, and it is now an adoption task rather than a design question.
- **Impact.** Low, and narrower than when it was raised. The health filter EXISTS and is server-evaluated; what the `/projects` collection header offers is the older Open/Completed/All segmented control, so the capability is reachable through a saved view and not through the collection's own chrome. The owner can answer *"which projects need attention?"* — by scanning health cues, which for a single-owner workspace is the expected path.
- **Why it remains open.** It is **adoption, not design**: `/projects` has not moved to the shared view configuration its header would need. Doing that changes the collection's URL vocabulary and its saved-view semantics, which is an X-02 adoption task with its own tests, not a filter to bolt on.
- **Closing condition.** `/projects` composes the shared view configuration in its own header, with `project.health` selectable there, and the Open/Completed/All control preserved as a scope rather than replaced — asserted by a journey that filters to `at_risk` from the collection and shares the resulting URL.
- **Related roadmap item.** [PROJ-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-proj-02--health); [X-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-x-02--saved-views--cross-module-filters--delivered-2026-08-08).

### ☑ DEBT-21 — Bare project record page has a pre-existing heading-order gap — P3
- **Current issue.** PROJ-02's record axe scan surfaced (did not cause) a pre-existing PROJ-01 condition: the bare `/projects/:id` record page jumped from the record `h1` straight to the Tasks tab's task cards at `h4`, with no intervening `h2`/`h3` — an axe `heading-order` (WCAG best-practice) violation. It was never caught because the only prior record axe gate scanned the record with the shared Task Drawer **open** (which inerts the background and hides its headings). PROJ-02 matched that established gate for its own record scan rather than performing a drive-by heading-hierarchy refactor.
- **Desired future state.** The bare project record page has a correct, non-skipping heading outline so it is axe-clean without the Drawer open.
- **Resolved (2026-07-22).** Fixed in PROJ-04, whose work directly touched and tested the Project Record Layout. Each project tab now opens with a visually-hidden **section `h2`** (Tasks / Key links / Activity), the Tasks tab's cards render at `h3` (was `h4`), and the new Activity tab's DS-05 Timeline day headings are `h3` — giving every tab a non-skipping outline (record `h1` → section `h2` → content `h3`). The fix stayed local to the Projects module tabs (no broad DS-02 redesign). A new **bare-record** axe gate (`/projects/pr-website` in the `e2e/accessibility.spec.ts` light + dark sweep, plus a bare-record + Activity-tab scan in `e2e/project-activity.spec.ts`) is the regression guard, so the record is no longer covered only by the Drawer-open scan. See [ADR-036](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-036-the-project-activity-tab--the-shared-timeline-over-the-project-subject-events) and [PROJECTS_MODULE.md](../development/PROJECTS_MODULE.md).
- **Remaining.** The generic DS-02 `RecordTabs` composition still has no built-in per-panel section heading, so a future record type could reintroduce the gap; giving DS-02 a shared section-heading affordance is a small optional enhancement, no longer blocking any project record.
- **Related roadmap item.** [PROJ-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-proj-02--health) (surfaced); [PROJ-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-proj-04--activity) (fixed).

### ☑ DEBT-22 — Goal record's Projects tab has no interactive "Load more" — P3
- **Current issue.** AREA-02's canonical `/goals/:goalId` record showed a single bounded first page (50) of Projects advancing the Goal, with only a static "more Projects exist" note when a `nextCursor` was present — so a Goal with more than 50 linked Projects could not reach the remainder from the record itself, and the note could silently imply the first page was the full set.
- **Resolved (2026-07-25).** Added the `GET /goals/:goalId/projects` bounded resource route ([`app/modules/goals/routes/projects.tsx`](../../app/modules/goals/routes/projects.tsx)) and a real interactive "Load more" on the Projects tab, following the EXACT pattern `ProjectTasksTab`/`/projects/:projectId/tasks` already established: the new [`GoalProjectsTab`](../../app/modules/goals/GoalProjectsTab.tsx) accumulates keyset pages via `useFetcher().load` (no navigation, so `?tab=`/`?drawer=` state, scroll and focus are untouched), de-duplicates by id (a Project on a page boundary appears once), and reconciles the accumulation from the fresh first page on a mutation revalidation while ignoring a drawer-only change. It reuses the EXISTING scope-bound, versioned `goal-cursor.ts` (workspace + goal), fails closed for missing/deleted/wrong-kind/cross-workspace Goal ids (calm `404`) and rejects a tampered/cross-scope cursor calmly (`400 invalid_cursor`). The tab badge stays the EXACT complete `getGoalProjectContribution.total`, never the loaded page length; the empty state means the complete result is empty. Proven by `test/kernel/goals-route.test.ts` (one page / multi-page reach-all with no dup or gap / `nextCursor=null` at exhaustion / malformed + cross-scope cursor `400` / missing-wrong-kind-cross-workspace `404`) and `test/unit/goals/GoalProjectsTab.test.tsx` (append + de-dupe + exhaust + empty + retry, no navigation).
- **Related roadmap item.** [AREA-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-area-02--goals).

### ☑ DEBT-23 — Alignment priority ordering does not span pages — P3
- **Current issue.** AREA-03's `/goals` Alignment collection fetched one bounded, creation-order-keyset page of Goals, computed each Goal's alignment from the COMPLETE underlying facts (always exactly correct), then sorted only THAT page by state precedence for display — so a neglected Goal on page 2 was never promoted above an active Goal on page 1. The "most in need of a look" ordering was per-page, not workspace-wide, and the sort ran in React.
- **Resolved (2026-07-25).** The Alignment order is now established WORKSPACE-WIDE, in the repository, BEFORE pagination. A new `GoalRepository.listGoalsByAlignment` ([`d1-goal-repository.ts`](../../app/platform/storage/d1/d1-goal-repository.ts)) computes each Goal's display rank in ONE workspace-scoped SQL statement — two grouped CTEs gather the complete Project-contribution facts (total/archived) and the most-recent qualifying two-hop Task activity (the SAME structural links, `MEANINGFUL_HEALTH_ACTIVITY_TYPES` vocabulary and `recentWindowStartIso` bound the pure evaluator's facts reads use), and a `CASE` assigns the exact `GOAL_ALIGNMENT_DISPLAY_RANK` (the ONE source of truth in [`goal-alignment.ts`](../../app/kernel/alignment/goal-alignment.ts), from which the display comparator also derives). It then keyset-paginates over `(displayRank, createdAt, id)` — ending in the immutable id — via a NEW versioned cursor ([`goal-alignment-cursor.ts`](../../app/kernel/goals/goal-alignment-cursor.ts)) bound to workspace + sort semantics (`alignment`), so a creation-order or cross-workspace cursor is rejected calmly (reset to first page). The client no longer re-sorts; it renders the authoritative server order. Alignment stays DERIVED (no persisted score, no cached classification column, no second algorithm) — a parity test proves the SQL order agrees with `evaluateGoalAlignment` for every state. The read is bounded per page and scans only the workspace's own Goals (no cross-workspace scan), N+1-free. Proven by `test/kernel/alignment.test.ts` (global order not creation order / SQL↔evaluator parity across all five states / a high-priority Goal never stranded on a later page / no dup or gap across boundaries / `nextCursor=null` at exhaustion / malformed + cross-scope + wrong-sort cursor rejection / workspace isolation).
- **Deferred at the time, delivered since.** Alignment *history* (a time series of a Goal's alignment over time) was out of scope here — a genuinely different, `REVIEW-03`-shaped feature, tracked below as DEBT-24 rather than invented here without evidenced need. REVIEW-03 built it as a **derived** reflection surface (2026-08-08); this live Alignment read is unchanged.
- **Related roadmap item.** [AREA-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-area-03--alignment-view).

### ☑ DEBT-24 — No Alignment history / trend is stored — P3 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-08 (REVIEW-03)**
- **Current issue.** Alignment is recomputed live on every read (ADR-040's "derived, never cached" ethos, matching PROJ-02/AREA-01/AREA-02); no history of a Goal's alignment over time is stored, so "was this Goal neglected last week too" cannot be answered from the Alignment view itself. (Split out of DEBT-23, whose cross-page-ordering half is now resolved.)
- **Assessment.** Alignment history is a genuinely different feature (a time series, not a snapshot). Deferring it avoids inventing a second persisted analytics model without evidenced need, and keeps Alignment derived. Owner: whoever picks up REVIEW-03. Impact: low — the current snapshot answers "which Goals need a look now", which is the property that matters for trust.
- **Desired future state.** Alignment trend/history, if ever wanted, is a `REVIEW-03`-shaped concern (a derived reflection surface over the Activity stream), not a change to the live Alignment read.
- **Resolved 2026-08-08 by [REVIEW-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-review-03--insights--alignment--delivered-2026-08-08), exactly as this entry predicted — and the live Alignment read is unchanged.** The Review evidence surface answers "did this Goal receive contribution this period, and how is that changing" without storing an alignment score anywhere: the **trend** is derived from the append-only Activity stream over recent completed Reviews of the same type (no storage at all, and truthful for periods that predate the feature), and the only persisted artefact is one small per-Review snapshot of what could not be reconstructed — ids, states and counts, never titles, never a score, never read by the Alignment view. `/goals` still recomputes on every read exactly as ADR-040 requires. The Goal-contribution rule introduces **no new threshold**: it reads completed work rolled up through the spine plus AREA-03's own live alignment state, and distinguishes "no contribution path" from "no recent movement" so a Goal with no Project is never described as neglected. See [ADR-079](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-079-review-insights--three-kinds-of-truth-one-persisted-snapshot-and-no-score) and [`REVIEWS_MODULE.md → Review evidence`](../development/REVIEWS_MODULE.md#review-evidence-review-03).
- **Bounded limitation, recorded rather than papered over.** A snapshot exists only from the first Review completed after REVIEW-03 shipped, so *health-change and carry-over comparison* start there; the surface says so instead of inventing a comparison. The trend has no such limitation.
- **Related roadmap item.** [REVIEW-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-review-03--insights--alignment--delivered-2026-08-08) ☑.

### ☐ DEBT-25 — Today "Continue working" Project card's Area context is not navigable — P3
- **Current issue.** On `/today`, a real Project card in "Continue working" shows its parent Area as an inert label (`RecentProjectItem.areaLabel` is a resolved title only; no Area id crosses to the card), so — unlike the Project's own title (a real link) and unlike the Area card's parent-Goal context (fixed in this PR) — the Area context cannot be activated. The relationship-navigation deliverable made every OTHER displayed Area/Goal/Project/Task relationship navigable; this one row is the sole remaining inert structural relationship, because wiring it needs the Today read model to also project the Area id.
- **Assessment.** Not a correctness or safety gap — the card already opens the Project, and the Area is reachable from there. Deliberately left for a small Today read-model follow-up rather than widening this PR's Today surface (the audit boundary kept Today changes minimal).
- **Desired future state.** Project the parent Area id in the Today recent-projects read model and render the card's `context` with an `EntityLink`/`href` to `/areas/:id`, reusing the shared `entityDestination` helper this PR added.
- **Impact.** One dead-end label on one card. The Area is reachable in two clicks (open the Project, follow its parent), and the card's own title is a real link — so nothing is unreachable and nothing is mislabelled. What it costs is consistency: everywhere else in the product a record's parent context is navigable, and here it looks navigable and is not.
- **Why it remains open.** It needs the parent Area **id** projected into Today's recent-projects read model, and Today's loader is the most-visited query in the product — the change is one join and a field, but the surface it lands on is the one where a careless read is most expensive. It has waited for a Today read-model change to travel with rather than for a decision.
- **Closing condition.** The card's Area context renders as an `EntityLink` to `/areas/:id` through the shared `entityDestination` helper, with Today's route query COUNT unchanged — asserted, because the point is that the id travels in the existing read rather than in a second one.
- **Related roadmap item.** [PROJ-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-proj-01--overview) (Today integration) / a future Today refinement.
- **V2.5 disposition — WEIGHED and NOT TAKEN (2026-08-28, STEER-04), against this entry's own bar.** [STEER-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-04--from-signal-to-step--delivered-2026-08-28) was told to take this *"only if the id travels in the existing statement, which is that entry's own bar"*. It does not. The statement STEER-04 added is about TASKS, partitioned by Project (`listProjectNextActions`), and it carries no Area — the Area context on a card comes from the PROJECT read (`readActiveProjects` → `listProjects`), which STEER-04 did not touch. Closing this would therefore have meant widening a different read on the most-visited route in the product to satisfy a P3, which is exactly the trade this entry has declined twice. It stays open, unchanged, with its bar intact and one fewer excuse: the next Today read-model change to touch `listProjects` should carry the id.

### ☑ DEBT-26 — Rendered GFM task-list checkboxes have no accessible label — P3 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-25**
- **Current issue.** The shared FND-08 renderer (`app/platform/markdown`, sanitised by the one frozen allowlist and rendered by the single `MarkdownContent` sink) emits a GFM task-list item `- [ ]` as a `<input type="checkbox" disabled>` with **no associated label** — no wrapping/explicit `<label>`, `aria-label`, or `title`. axe (`label`, WCAG 2.2 AA, critical) flags each such checkbox. NOTES-04 surfaced this when a Note whose Markdown contains a checklist is previewed; it was latent before because no prior preview axe scan rendered task-list content. The checkbox text sits in the sibling list-item content, so a screen-reader user still hears the item, but the input itself is unlabelled.
- **Assessment.** This is a **shared Markdown-pipeline** concern, not a Notes concern — the same output appears anywhere Markdown with a task list is rendered (Notes preview, Diary, descriptions). NOTES-04 is scoped to Notes and must not modify the one authoritative pipeline or its frozen sanitisation allowlist (which would touch shared infrastructure and risk the concurrent TASKS-01 work), so it recorded the gap rather than fixing it, and scopes its own editor axe gate to the Source surface (the toolbar it actually adds) while keeping the preview's functional/safety assertions.
- **Desired future state.** The shared renderer associates each display-only task-list checkbox with its item text — e.g. `aria-label` derived from the item content, or `aria-hidden` on the purely-decorative input since the checked/unchecked state is already conveyable in the item text — inside the one FND-08 pipeline and its allowlist, with a `test/kernel/markdown-*` regression and the axe scan re-enabled over rendered task lists.
- **Related roadmap item.** [FND-08](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-fnd-08--markdown-pipeline); [DS-11](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-11--accessibility--responsive-baseline).
- **RESOLVED 2026-08-25 by the [all-open-debt pass](PRODUCT_DEBT_CLOSURE_2026_08.md), in the ONE pipeline, by the first of the two routes this entry offered.**
  - The renderer NAMES each task-list checkbox with its own item's text, in the hast transform that already runs before sanitisation — so the attribute is subject to the same frozen allowlist as everything else, and `ariaLabel` was added to the schema's `input` entry for exactly this and nothing else.
  - **Not `aria-hidden`, and the reason matters.** The item's text says what the step IS; only the checkbox says whether it is DONE. Removing the input from the accessibility tree would satisfy the checker and take the one fact it carries with it — a screen-reader user would hear "Book the venue" for a ticked step and an unticked one alike.
  - **The axe scan now looks at the thing.** `label` has never been in the globally-disabled set, so nothing was re-enabled: the gap was that no scan had ever rendered task-list content, exactly as this entry says. `e2e/notes.spec.ts` → *"a rendered task list is axe-clean, and each checkbox is named"* writes a real checklist, renders it through Read mode (the shared FND-08 render), and scans the whole page in both appearances.
  - **Closing condition, met and falsified twice.** Five of seven new assertions in [`test/kernel/markdown-render.test.ts`](../../test/kernel/markdown-render.test.ts) fail against the previous pipeline; and with the naming removed the E2E scan reports the violation verbatim — `"id": "label"`, `"impact": "critical"`, *"aria-label attribute does not exist or is empty"*, twice.
### ☑ DEBT-27 — Task overdue urgency is signalled by colour alone — P1
- **Current issue.** An overdue task's due date renders as "Due &lt;date&gt;" in the danger tone (red) with **no textual "Overdue" cue**; a future due date renders the same "Due &lt;date&gt;" string in a neutral tone. The only difference is colour ([`taskDateLabel`](../../app/shared/task-record/task-view.ts) sets `tone: "danger"` with no marker word; duplicated inline in [`TasksWorkspace.tsx`](../../app/modules/tasks/TasksWorkspace.tsx) and `TodayDashboard.tsx` (now [`day/TodayScreen.tsx`](../../app/modules/today/day/TodayScreen.tsx))). This directly contradicts the product's own "never rely on colour alone" contract ([ACCESSIBILITY_RESPONSIVE.md](../development/ACCESSIBILITY_RESPONSIVE.md)). Confirmed visually in the 2026-07 audit (the July 2026 audit's light-appearance capture of the Task drawer (not committed)). Separately, a task due **today** (`due == today`) is not distinguished at all — it falls through to the neutral label, identical to a due date months away.
- **Desired future state.** A shared task urgency signal carries an explicit label ("Overdue", "Due today", "Scheduled today") — icon + word — with colour as reinforcement only, per the §6 grammar in [`UI_UX_COHERENCE_AUDIT_2026_07.md`](UI_UX_COHERENCE_AUDIT_2026_07.md). Overdue detection is computed once in the shared derivation, not re-derived inline per surface.
- **Resolved (2026-07-26).** Fixed in [TASKS-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-tasks-02--shared-task-signal-presentation). Overdue/due-today/scheduled-today detection is computed once in the canonical `taskUrgency(task, todayIso)` evaluator ([`task-view.ts`](../../app/shared/task-record/task-view.ts)) and rendered by the ONE shared `UrgencyChip` component ([`UrgencyChip.tsx`](../../app/shared/task-record/UrgencyChip.tsx)) on every task-bearing surface (Today, Projects, `/tasks`, the Drawer) — icon **+ WORD**, colour as reinforcement only. The inline per-surface date logic was removed; `taskDateLabel` now delegates to `taskUrgency` so the string-slot Waiting list carries the words too. The Drawer resolves urgency against the owner's server-derived calendar day (`TaskDetailData.todayIso`, ADR-022), never browser-local. A real-D1 Playwright test asserts the "Overdue" word on a card; component/unit tests cover every kind and the colour-not-only contract.

### ☑ DEBT-28 — Task priority is invisible where triage happens, and status resolves three different ways — P2
- **Current issue.** Priority (P1–P4) is a colour-free grey metadata chip in the Tasks module ([`TasksWorkspace.tsx`](../../app/modules/tasks/TasksWorkspace.tsx)) and is **not rendered at all** on Today cards (the `planning-view` (since removed) projection omits it), Project task cards (data is on the wire but unrendered — [`ProjectTasksTab.tsx`](../../app/modules/projects/ProjectTasksTab.tsx)), or Search results ([`search.ts`](../../app/modules/tasks/search.ts)). A P1 and a P4 look identical while planning the day or working a project. Separately, task **status** resolves through two functions with different vocabularies — the 8-state [`taskDisplayState`](../../app/shared/task-record/task-view.ts) on Tasks/Drawer versus the legacy 3-state `taskDisplayStatus` on Projects (which has no case for On hold / Cancelled / Someday, so those silently read as "To do") — so the same task shows a different status depending on the surface. Confirmed in the 2026-07 audit.
- **Desired future state.** A shared `PriorityIndicator` renders on every task-bearing Card (Today/Projects/Tasks/Search), driven by the canonical `taskPriorityTag`; the Today projection and Tasks search payload carry priority; `taskDisplayStatus` is retired so every surface uses the single `taskDisplayState`. See §6 of the 2026-07 audit.
- **Resolved (2026-07-26; Search follow-up completed 2026-07-29).** Fixed first in [TASKS-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-tasks-02--shared-task-signal-presentation) for Today, Projects, Tasks and the Drawer. X-01/TASKS-02b completed the deferred Search surface: `SearchResultItem.signals` carries generic serialisable facts, `tasks.search` reads priority/due/scheduled/completion fields from one bounded projection, and the Search surface renders them with the shared `PriorityIndicator`/`UrgencyChip`. The legacy `taskDisplayStatus` remains retired; Search no longer has the priority/urgency exception.

### ☑ DEBT-29 — Record removal is inconsistent and undiscoverable; no shared overflow menu exists — P1 — **RESOLVED 2026-07-28**
- **Current issue.** There is **no overflow (⋯) menu anywhere in the product** — [`RecordHeader`](../../app/shared/record-layout/RecordHeader.tsx) renders only inline primary/secondary buttons, and the Card's built-in `overflowAction` slot is passed by none of the seven modules — so there is no conventional home for secondary/destructive actions. As a result removal is scattered across four placements plus three absences: Notes = record-header "Delete" + Deleted filter (the good pattern, ADR-042); Project = archive/restore **buried in the Settings sub-tab** with no header or collection entry ([`ProjectSettingsTab.tsx`](../../app/modules/projects/ProjectSettingsTab.tsx)); Task = cancel via a drawer status `<select>`; **Area, Goal and Diary entries have no removal UI at all** despite the spine/entity kernel supporting soft-delete ([`spine-repository.ts`](../../app/kernel/spine/spine-repository.ts), [`entity-repository.ts`](../../app/kernel/entities/entity-repository.ts); mutate routes reject every non-rename intent). "How do I delete this Project or Area?" has no good answer. Confirmed in the 2026-07 audit (the July 2026 audit's Area record capture (not committed), its Project record capture (not committed)).
- **Re-audited 2026-07-27 — the shape has changed, the debt has not.** Verified against `main` at `b1a2f65`:
  - **Still no overflow menu anywhere.** `RecordHeader` renders only inline primary/secondary buttons, and a repository-wide search finds `overflowAction` referenced *only* in [`Card.tsx`](../../app/shared/card/Card.tsx)/[`card/types.ts`](../../app/shared/card/types.ts) — **no module passes it**. [DS-12](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-12--record-header-overflow-menu--card-overflow-action) remains unstarted, so [PX-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-px-04--lifecycle--destructive-action-consistency) is still blocked.
  - **A de-facto convention emerged without the primitive.** Five modules now house lifecycle in a record **Settings tab**: Projects, Areas ([AREA-05](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-area-05--area-archive--safe-deletion-lifecycle)), People, Assets and Reviews (`*SettingsTab.tsx` / `ReviewRecord.tsx`). That is more consistent than the four-way scatter the original entry described, but it is convention by imitation, not a shared component — and it is still not where a user looks first.
  - **Three placements still disagree.** Notes = record-header "Delete" + a Deleted filter (ADR-042); Meetings = an inline "Archive meeting"/"Restore meeting" button in the record body ([`meetings/routes/detail.tsx`](../../app/modules/meetings/routes/detail.tsx)); Task = cancel via a Drawer status `<select>`.
  - **Two absences remain.** **Goals and Diary entries still have no removal UI at all**, though the kernel supports soft-delete. Areas gained theirs in AREA-05, so the original "Area, Goal and Diary" list is now "Goal and Diary".
- **Desired future state.** Implement the documented Record Header overflow (⋯) slot and adopt the Card `overflowAction`; house one shared lifecycle action set (Archive/Delete/Restore) there, consistently across modules; converge the five Settings-tab implementations and the Notes/Meetings/Task placements onto it; add the missing Goal and Diary lifecycle; gate hierarchy deletes on the existing `SpineHasActiveChildrenError` with an explanatory confirm. See §7 of the 2026-07 audit. **Reversible removal first** — permanent deletion stays behind the shared exact-title dangerous-action dialog, never a cascade.
- **Resolved 2026-07-28 by [DS-12](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-12--record-header-overflow-menu--card-overflow-action) + [PX-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-px-04--lifecycle--destructive-action-consistency)** ([ADR-053](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-053-the-shared-overflow-menu-and-one-record-lifecycle-vocabulary)). The structural hole is closed: ONE shared overflow (⋯) menu ([`app/shared/overflow-menu`](../../app/shared/overflow-menu)) renders on both the Record Header and the Card, and every record's lifecycle actions live there. The wording is **derived** from `ENTITY_IDENTITY` ([`app/shared/record-lifecycle`](../../app/shared/record-lifecycle)), so the five Settings-tab implementations, the Notes header flow and the Meetings inline button now say the same words and drive the same handlers. **Both absences are closed with no migration**: Goals gained reversible delete/restore plus a `?state=deleted` view, and Diary entries gained the same. Meetings' bespoke settings section became the shared DS-10b surface. Task removal stays **Cancel** by explicit decision (ADR-053 §8), documented rather than silently omitted.
- **Related roadmap item.** [DS-12](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-12--record-header-overflow-menu--card-overflow-action) (the shared overflow primitive) and [PX-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-px-04--lifecycle--destructive-action-consistency) (the lifecycle adoption that depends on it).

### ☑ DEBT-30 — Shared EntityLink renders no entity icon, so related-record identity drifts — P2 — **RESOLVED 2026-07-28**
- **Current issue.** The one shared relationship component, [`EntityLink`](../../app/shared/entity/EntityLink.tsx), renders title text only — no `EntityIcon`/accent (identity is only in its `aria-label`). Consumers therefore drift: the Task/Project Links tabs hand-compose an `EntityIcon` beside it, but the Project overview summary rows show bare text Area/Goal links ([`ProjectOverview.tsx`](../../app/modules/projects/ProjectOverview.tsx)). The same "linked record" concept looks iconned in one place and generic in another — undercutting "the value is in the links."
- **Re-audited 2026-07-27 — the predicted collision has now happened, and the fork has doubled.** `EntityLink.tsx` still contains no icon reference at all. Entity identity itself is complete — [`identity.ts`](../../app/shared/entity/identity.ts) maps all ten entity types (`area`, `goal`, `project`, `task`, `note`, `meeting`, `person`, `asset`, `diary`, `review`) to one frozen icon + accent. But **subtype** icons have forked twice, not once: Diary's [`diary-icons.tsx`](../../app/modules/diary/diary-icons.tsx) and Assets' [`asset-icons.tsx`](../../app/modules/assets/asset-icons.tsx) each maintain a private module-local map (the Assets file explicitly cites Diary as its precedent). And the collision the original entry only *predicted* is now real: `diary-icons.tsx` maps the `meeting` **subtype** to `MeetingIcon`, which since [MEET-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-meet-01--meeting-record) is the **Meeting entity glyph** — so a Diary entry of subtype "meeting" is visually indistinguishable from a Meeting record.
- **Desired future state.** `EntityLink` gains an optional leading `EntityIcon` (default on); hand-composed icons are removed. A shared **subtype-icon registry** (distinct from entity identity) is promoted alongside `ENTITY_IDENTITY`, with Diary and Assets migrated onto it as its first two consumers, so subtype icons never fork or collide with entity icons — and the Diary `meeting` subtype is given a glyph distinct from the Meeting entity. See §5 of the 2026-07 audit.
- **Resolved 2026-07-28 by [PX-05](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-px-05--identity-adoption-entitylink-icon--subtype-icon-registry).** `EntityLink` now carries its leading `EntityIcon` by default (opt-out only where the surrounding row already shows the type); the hand-composed icons are gone, and the two byte-identical relationship rows collapsed into one shared `EntityRelationshipRow`. A shared subtype-icon registry ([`app/shared/entity/subtype-icons.tsx`](../../app/shared/entity/subtype-icons.tsx)) replaced the two private maps, and the collision was fixed **at its root** rather than reassigned: the shared icon set gained dedicated subtype glyphs so **no** subtype wears an entity glyph, enforced by a test.
- **Related roadmap item.** [PX-05](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-px-05--identity-adoption-entitylink-icon--subtype-icon-registry).

### ◐ DEBT-31 — Cross-module presentation drift: Today/Diary forks, terminology and capitalisation — P2 — **presentation half RESOLVED 2026-07-28**
- **Current issue.** Today does not use the shared [`EmptyState`](../../app/shared/empty-state/EmptyState.tsx) (each section renders a bare inline `<p>` with no icon or CTA — `TodayDashboard.tsx` (now [`day/TodayScreen.tsx`](../../app/modules/today/day/TodayScreen.tsx))) and its primary "Quick capture" action is a bespoke, currently-inert button rather than the shared create pattern. Diary ships **two** primary entry points (header button + a floating FAB), forks the shared Card (a hand-rolled `dh-diary-entry` timeline node) and uses the Inspector rather than the shared Record Layout. Create labels and count nouns drift in capitalisation ("New Area"/"New Goal" title-case vs "New project"/"New task"/"New note" lower-case vs "Quick capture"/"New entry"), empty-title copy drifts ("No tasks here" vs "No projects yet" vs "Your diary is empty"), the Links tab is "Key links" on Projects but "Links" on Tasks, and Diary uses a curly apostrophe where others use ASCII. Confirmed across the 2026-07 audit's collection screenshots.
- **Re-audited 2026-07-27 — Today is now the sole `EmptyState` holdout.** Every other product surface has adopted the shared component: Areas, Assets, Diary, Goals, Meetings, Notes, People, Projects, Reviews and Tasks all import `~/shared/empty-state`, and `/today/waiting` does too — but `TodayDashboard.tsx` and `landing/widgets.tsx` contain **zero** `EmptyState` references. Quick Capture is also confirmed still inert: `onCapture` sets the notice *"Quick Capture is not connected yet. Your draft has not been saved."* and writes nothing (`TodayDashboard.tsx` (now [`day/TodayScreen.tsx`](../../app/modules/today/day/TodayScreen.tsx))). That message is honest — it is not a lying CTA — but the app's most prominent primary action still does not create a record.
- **Desired future state.** Today adopts the shared `EmptyState` and create pattern (and Quick Capture is wired to real creation); Diary keeps its excellent timeline visual but reduces to one primary entry point per viewport and, where feasible, expresses the timeline node as a Card variant so it inherits shared behaviour; a copy/capitalisation convention is added to [`DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`](../design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md) and swept across all collections; tab labels converge ("Links"). See §8–§10 of the 2026-07 audit.
- **Resolved 2026-07-28 by [PX-06](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-px-06--cross-module-polish--copy-convention), except the two items that were never in its scope.** Today adopted the shared `EmptyState` (a new `size="compact"` variant sized for a widget) — it was the last holdout. The copy convention is now **executable**: create/empty/count labels derive from `ENTITY_IDENTITY` ([`app/shared/entity/copy.ts`](../../app/shared/entity/copy.ts)), so drift is structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged; the written rule lives in `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` and every collection was swept to it, apostrophes included. Diary dropped its `+` glyph and now shows exactly one primary entry point per viewport. Tab labels converged on `Linked`, and the Person record's `Timeline` became `Activity` in its correct position. **Still open, by design:** Quick Capture remains inert pending [TODAY-07](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-today-07--quick-capture-wiring), and the Diary timeline node remains a **deliberate, documented fork** — expressing it as a Card variant risked losing the best scanning surface in the product for no user-visible gain, so the visual was preserved intact.
- **Today's half was re-decided by the 2026-08 Today redesign, and the files named above no longer exist.** Today does not render the shared `EmptyState` any more, deliberately: on a screen whose whole point is a short quiet day, an icon + headline + description + button makes "nothing is due" the largest object on the page. Its two empty cases are now single lines — "Nothing planned today. Capture anything new with the + button." and the rail's "All clear" — and that rule is written into [`DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` → The Today screen](../design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md#the-today-screen). Quick Capture is likewise gone from Today: the global `+` is the one capture affordance, which is what TODAY-07 was asking for. The Diary timeline-node fork is what remains of this entry.
- **Impact.** Effectively nil today, and the entry's own record explains why: the presentation half was resolved by PX-06, and Today's half was then RE-DECIDED — a screen whose whole subject is *what is left to do* says "nothing left" in its own words rather than through a shared empty state, which is a deliberate difference, not drift. What is left is terminology and capitalisation, which no test enforces.
- **Why it remains open.** ONE unenforced half: the copy convention is executable for empty-collection titles and count labels (`app/shared/entity/copy.ts` derives them from the identity map) and is a convention everywhere else. Nothing stops a module writing "Task" where the product says "task", and nothing has, which is why this sits at ◐ with no defect to point at.
- **Closing condition.** The copy convention is derived rather than written down for every owner-facing noun — the way empty-collection titles already are — so a module structurally cannot capitalise an entity differently; or an ADR records that the remaining surface is prose and is reviewed rather than tested, which closes it with no code change.
- **Related roadmap item.** [PX-06](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-px-06--cross-module-polish--copy-convention) (empty-state, copy, Diary entry-point and tab-label polish) and [TODAY-07](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-today-07--quick-capture-wiring) (making Quick Capture functional).

### ☐ DEBT-32 — Today personalisation is per-device, not synced — P3
- **Current issue.** TODAY-08 remembers the Today widget arrangement (hide/move/pin/collapse) in `localStorage`, so it is per-device and does not follow the owner across devices. This is a deliberate first cut ([ADR-045](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-045-today-as-the-command-centre--the-personalisable-widget-landing-surface-over-real-cross-module-reads) §2): the arrangement is a cosmetic UI preference with no entity content, so it was kept out of the server-derived workspace rather than over-coupling a nicety to the security boundary.
- **Desired future state.** When a workspace/user preference store exists (SET-01 territory), a synced arrangement can adopt the SAME pure `landing/layout.ts` model unchanged — only the persistence seam (`useTodayLayout`) swaps from `localStorage` to the preference store. No widget or model change required.
- **Related roadmap item.** A future Settings/preferences item (SET-01 and beyond).
- **SET-01 note.** SETTINGS-01A introduced the owner/workspace preference store but deliberately did **not** migrate Today arrangement into it; the device-local boundary remains a product decision until synced widget layout is explicitly prioritised.
- **THEME-01 note (2026-07-31).** The theme preference has now moved INTO that store for exactly the reason this entry defers: a personal choice that does not follow the owner between devices is a broken one. That makes the device-local arrangement newly inconsistent rather than merely deferred — recorded as [DEBT-55](#-debt-55--today-widget-arrangement-is-still-device-local-while-the-theme-is-not--p3), which also notes that THEME-01 has proven the migration shape end to end.
- **Impact.** **None — there is nothing to sync.** Re-verified 2026-08-25: `rg "useTodayLayout" app` returns **nothing**. The widget arrangement this entry is about was removed with the 2026-08-07 Today redesign, so no owner has a per-device arrangement to be frustrated by. The entry now describes a *capability the product deliberately dropped*, which is a different subject from the one it was raised about.
- **Why it remains open.** Because closing it would assert that the persistence question was answered, and it was not — it was **removed**. If Today ever regains personalisation, whether that arrangement syncs is a live question and this entry is where the reasoning already is (THEME-01 proved the migration shape end to end). Deleting it would throw that away; marking it resolved would be false.
- **Closing condition.** Either Today gains a personalisation system as its own roadmap item AND its arrangement lives in the owner/workspace preference store from the first commit — with [DEBT-55](#-debt-55--today-widget-arrangement-is-still-device-local-while-the-theme-is-not--p3) closing at the same moment, since they are one question — or an ADR records that Today is deliberately not personalisable, which closes both with no code change.
- **⚠ The code this entry describes no longer exists (verified 2026-08-16 by [TODAY-11](../design/TODAY_11_COMMAND_CENTRE_2026_08.md)).** The 2026-08-07 Today redesign removed the widget system outright — `useTodayLayout` and `landing/layout.ts` are gone, and `grep -rn "useTodayLayout" app` returns nothing. There is no arrangement in `localStorage`, because there is no arrangement. This entry and DEBT-55 both now describe a *capability the product deliberately dropped* rather than a persistence seam waiting to be swapped, and the two must be re-decided together: **either** Today regains a personalisation system (a feature, with its own roadmap item, not a seam swap) **and** it is synced from the start, **or** both entries close as "not applicable — Today is one composed screen". TODAY-11 deliberately did neither: rebuilding Today to `MOCKUP 5.png` is a composition change, and inventing a widget registry inside it would have been exactly the creep that pass was told to avoid.

### ☑ DEBT-33 — Settings changes are not yet represented in Activity — P3 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-25**
- **Original issue.** SET-01 persists owner/workspace preferences, but preference mutations do not append Activity rows. The accepted Activity model is entity-subject based, and forcing Settings into a fake entity subject would pollute the audit model. Preference values can also be sensitive or identifying, so arbitrary before/after payloads are not acceptable.
- **The blocking half is resolved (2026-08-08, with SET-03).** The "deliberate workspace/owner-scoped audit shape for non-entity system changes" this entry asked for now exists, and it is not a second audit log: `buildWorkspaceActivityWriteModel` validates a SUBJECT-LESS event, `WorkspaceEventRecorder` appends it to the SAME `activities` table with the same trusted actor, and it surfaces in the workspace feed while appearing in no record's Timeline. `buildActivityWriteModel`'s "at least one subject" rule is untouched, so a subject-less event has to be asked for by name. Payloads carry structural metadata only — counts and enumerated literals — exactly as this entry required. See [`ACTIVITY_TIMELINE.md → Workspace-scoped events`](../development/ACTIVITY_TIMELINE.md#workspace-scoped-events-set-03-2026-08-08).
- **What remains.** Only the adoption: `security.signed_out` and `security.local_data_cleared` are recorded, and ORDINARY preference changes (timezone, date format, navigation visibility, module defaults, AI policy) still are not. That is now a small, mechanical extension rather than a modelling problem.
- **Impact.** An owner reading their own history could see that they signed out and not that they had changed **where their captured work goes**, which timezone their day is computed in, or which modules they had hidden. Those are the changes most likely to make the product behave unexpectedly a week later, and the history — the one place a person goes to ask *"what did I change?"* — could not answer.
- **Closing condition.** A representative preference change appends a structural workspace-scoped event, with a kernel test proving the payload carries no preference VALUE that could identify the owner.
- **RESOLVED 2026-08-25 by the [all-open-debt pass](PRODUCT_DEBT_CLOSURE_2026_08.md).** Both halves of the closing condition, and the entry's own constraint was the design.
  - **It was smaller than this entry said, and the reason is worth recording.** The type already existed — `APP_PREFERENCES_CHANGED` (`"settings.preferences_changed"`) in `app-preferences.ts` — and it already had a line in the workspace feed's descriptor map. **It had never once been written.** So the gap was not a type, a descriptor or a model; it was a payload contract and a call site. A second constant was deliberately NOT introduced: one type string with two names is the duplicate vocabulary the architecture rules forbid.
  - **The payload is a set of FIELD NAMES, never values**, which is exactly the constraint this entry gave for why it had not been taken: *"preference values can also be sensitive or identifying"*. [`app/kernel/preferences/preference-events.ts`](../../app/kernel/preferences/preference-events.ts) reads only the KEYS of a patch, keeps only those on a declared allowlist, sorts and de-duplicates them, and returns `null` when nothing recordable changed — so no event is written for a change that is not one. A timezone is a location; a default capture parent is a record id; a default view id names a filter the owner wrote. None of them reaches the stream.
  - **The allowlist is the safety property, not tidiness.** A future preference key whose NAME carries something identifying cannot reach the payload by being added to the preferences type — it has to be added to `RECORDABLE_PREFERENCE_FIELDS`, deliberately, and a test asserts an undeclared key is dropped rather than trusted.
  - **No branch can forget it.** The settings action had six `appPreferences.update` call sites; all six now go through one `updatePreferences` helper that writes and then records. Recording is best-effort **at the call site**, as SET-03's seam requires: failing to write history must never fail the owner's actual change, which is already durable by then.
  - **The feed says what changed in the owner's own words.** The descriptor previously rendered a fixed *"changed application preferences"*; it now reads the bounded field names and renders *"changed your timezone and date format"*, mapping through the same labels the settings screen uses. An unmapped name degrades to *"their settings"* rather than showing a raw key.
  - **Evidence, and it is against REAL D1** ([`test/kernel/settings-preference-events.test.ts`](../../test/kernel/settings-preference-events.test.ts)) — because the claim is about what is actually stored, and a payload assertion against an in-memory object would not see a serialiser that kept more than it was given. Four tests: the event lands subject-less in the one `activities` table with the bound actor; the stored `payload_json` **text** contains none of five identifying values (asserted over the text, not a parsed shape, because a value nested in a structure a future payload grew would still be a leak); an undeclared key is dropped; and a patch that changes no preference records nothing.
  - **FALSIFIED.** `preferencesChangedPayload` was changed to return `{ fields, ...patch }` — the before/after payload this entry says is not acceptable — and **three of the four tests went red**, the payload test naming the leaked value outright: *"the stored payload contains the preference VALUE `Pacific/Kiritimati`"*. Restored, and green.
- **Related roadmap item.** A future Settings hardening item building on [SET-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-set-01--app--workspace-settings--core-preferences). **Related ADR.** [ADR-082](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-082-a-nonce-based-content-security-policy-one-header-authority-and-a-security-surface-that-refuses-to-overclaim) decision 9.

### ☑ DEBT-34 — Reviews period context and Today integration are bounded first cuts — P2 — resolved 2026-08-28 (V2.5 STEER-05)
- **Current issue.** REVIEWS-01 presents bounded live Tasks/Diary/Meetings context through existing repositories and ships the clean Reviews module seam, but it does not yet provide a complete unbounded period aggregation service, immutable source-record snapshots, Projects-updated-in-period facts, or a Today card for "Start/Continue current weekly Review." The Review remains correct and durable because authored reflection and links are stored, but context is a live helper rather than a complete historical snapshot.
- **Desired future state.** Add a dedicated Reviews period-context service that composes source repositories with explicit pagination/summary semantics for Tasks, Projects, Diary and Meetings; add a modest Today contribution that shows the active current-period Review or Start weekly review action; and, if the owner needs historical source labels frozen, design a small snapshot mechanism rather than copying entire source records into Review tables.
- **V2.4 disposition — NARROWED.** [FOLLOW-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-follow-01--did-the-week-hold--delivered-2026-08-26) adds the period account this entry's "bounded first cut" is missing on the Review side. The Today-integration half is untouched and stays open.
- **ADVANCED 2026-08-26 by [V2.4 FOLLOW-01](V2_4_FOLLOW_01_WEEK_ACCOUNT_2026_08.md), and still OPEN on its own closing condition.** The Review half is delivered: the evidence surface now accounts for the period's PLAN — what it held, what kept its day, what moved and how often, what was cleared, what was left unfinished and what was done without being planned — from a bounded derivation over the append-only Activity stream, plus routine consistency for the same period (DEBT-156). That is the last thing REVIEW-03's period context was missing, so this entry is no longer about the Review at all. **What remains is exactly what the closing condition names and nothing else: Today still offers no "Start/Continue this week's Review".** That is a Today composition decision — which of the day's finite surfaces gives up space for a once-a-week prompt — and FOLLOW-01 deliberately touched no Today surface.
- **Related roadmap item.** [REVIEW-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-review-03--insights--alignment) for derived period facts/snapshots and a future Today refinement for the current-week entry point.
- **Partially resolved 2026-08-05 by [REVIEW-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-review-02--weekly-review--delivered-2026-08-05), with evidence.** The named gap "**Projects-updated-in-period facts**" is closed: the guided flow adds a bounded Project review projection over `ProjectRepository` + PROJ-02's `ProjectHealthRepository` (Area/Goal context, workflow status, derived health, open/overdue/waiting counts, Tasks completed in the period, last activity, a deterministic next action), with a documented selection and ordering rule, an ASSERTED per-step query budget measured against real D1, and two tests proving the counts are flat with respect to workspace size. The context also stopped being unbounded-or-silent: where a list is bounded the surface states the truth ("4+") and links to the canonical destination, and the Inbox total is the authoritative grouped aggregate rather than "how many were loaded". See [`REVIEWS_MODULE.md → Project review projection`](../development/REVIEWS_MODULE.md#project-review-projection) and [ADR-072](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-072-the-guided-weekly-review--one-review-two-presentations-a-canonical-step-model-and-the-smallest-possible-persisted-workflow-state) decisions 7 and 8.
- **Narrowed again 2026-08-08 by [REVIEW-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-review-03--insights--alignment--delivered-2026-08-08), with evidence.** The named gap "**derived period facts**" is closed: the Review now derives, from the owner's own canonical data, what completed in the period (exact, from the append-only Activity stream, for **any** period past or present), where that completed work landed by Project / Goal / Area, what was already outstanding when the period began, how Project health moved since the previous Review, and a bounded trend over recent Reviews of the same type. A **small explicit snapshot mechanism** was designed rather than avoided — but deliberately NOT the "immutable source-record snapshot" this entry originally imagined: `review_insight_snapshots` stores **derived facts only** (ids, states, counts), never a copy of a record body, precisely so a renamed Project still renders under its live title. Every read is a bounded, grouped aggregate under an **asserted 14-statement budget** proven flat with respect to workspace size, so "a complete unbounded period aggregation service" is no longer the desired state — an unbounded aggregation is the thing the budget exists to prevent.
- **Impact.** Narrow and shrinking: REVIEW-02 closed the Projects-in-period facts and REVIEW-03 closed the derived period facts, so the Review itself is no longer a "bounded first cut" in the sense this entry raised. What is left is a **discoverability** cost — the weekly Review has no entry point on the screen the owner opens every day, so starting one is something they must remember rather than something the product offers.
- **Why it remains open.** The Review half is [FOLLOW-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-follow-01--did-the-week-hold--delivered-2026-08-26)'s and is scheduled; the Today half is a Today composition decision — which of the day's finite surfaces gives up space for a once-a-week prompt — and belongs to a Today refinement, not to Reviews.
- **Closing condition.** Today offers the current period's Review as a real entry point (start it if none exists, continue it if one does), reading the SAME `currentReviewPeriod` authority the Reviews module uses so the two cannot disagree about which week it is — with Today's route query count unchanged.
- **Deliberately still open in this entry.** The Today "Start/Continue this week's Review" card. REVIEW-02 built the *flow* and REVIEW-03 built the *evidence*; neither touched Today, and a Today entry point is a Today read-model change rather than a Reviews one. Immutable source-record snapshots stay out of scope on purpose: the REVIEW-03 audit concluded that freezing source labels would make a Review disagree with the records it points at, which is worse than a label moving.
- **V2.5 disposition — TAKEN.** [STEER-05](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-05--the-weeks-door--delivered-2026-08-28) delivers exactly the remaining half, against this entry's own closing condition: Today offers the current period's Review (start or continue), reading the same `currentReviewPeriod` authority, with the query-count clause honoured or its cost stated and put to this entry rather than absorbed.
- **RESOLVED 2026-08-28 by [STEER-05](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-05--the-weeks-door--delivered-2026-08-28), with evidence — and with the query-count clause ANSWERED rather than met.** The closing condition is delivered: Today's foot carries a full-width band, *"This week's Review"*, that offers **Start** when the owner's week has no Review, **Continue** into the guided flow when one is underway, and a quiet **"This week's Review is done."** with a link back to the record when it is finished. It reads `currentReviewPeriod` from `~/kernel/reviews` — the same function `NewReviewForm` calls — and labels it with `reviewPeriodLabel`, which moved into the same kernel module in this pass so the door and the Reviews collection cannot print two names for one week. Today **links**: `/reviews/new`, `/reviews/:id/guide` and `/reviews/:id` are all the Reviews module's, and Today mutates nothing.
  - **The query-count clause could not be honoured, and this is the recorded cost.** This entry asked for Today's route query count to be UNCHANGED. Nothing Today already reads touches `review_details`, so there was no existing statement for the existence read to ride on, and the honest answer is that the day costs **one more bounded statement**: MEASURED at **20 → 21** on an empty workspace, in the existing parallel block, and identical in all three door states. Both numbers are pinned by a counting database in [`today-review-door.test.ts`](../../test/kernel/today-review-door.test.ts), so a second Reviews read — or one that varies with the door's state — fails the suite rather than passing unnoticed. This is [ADR-110](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-110-follow-through-is-derived-from-the-activity-stream-never-stored--one-period-account-no-adherence-score-and-no-snapshot-table-for-a-plan-or-a-goal) decision 7's posture applied to a budget instead of to storage: recorded and put to the entry, never absorbed in a PR description.
  - **The read is creation's own lookup, not a second one.** `ReviewRepository.findPeriodEntry` is the period lookup `create` already performs to stay idempotent, exposed on the contract and sharing one `PERIOD_MATCH` predicate with it — so "is there one for this week?" and "there already is one" are the same question. It answers with a small `ReviewPeriodEntry` (id, title, period, status, archived) rather than a `Review`, which is what makes it ONE statement: a `Review` would carry ten section bodies and cost a second.
  - **The composition decision this entry asked for, with its measurement.** The entry framed the open half as *"which of the day's finite surfaces gives up space for a once-a-week prompt"*. The measured answer is **none of them**: the door is a full-width band at the very foot, below the day's work, its schedule, its routine, its Goals and its reflection. The six-column alternative was built first and rejected on a measurement — at 1440 the foot row already holds `Continue working` (x 264, w 560) and `Daily reflection` (x 840, w 560), so a third six-column cell wrapped and left 560px of empty grid, conditionally on whether the owner had a project with open work. Nothing above the first task moved: the first actionable row stays at 461 / 497 / 597 / 646 px at 1440 / 820 / 393 / 320.
  - **Calm, and asserted as such.** No badge, no count, no urgency colour, no notification and no streak of completed Reviews. A week the owner never reviews is never called overdue, missed or late — a vocabulary guard over the rendered band asserts it in all three states, which is ADR-110 decision 5's spirit applied to a ritual instead of to a figure.
  - **Evidence.** [`today-review-door.test.ts`](../../test/kernel/today-review-door.test.ts) (real D1: the three states through the actual loader, agreement with `create` across every lifecycle state, workspace and period isolation, both `firstDayOfWeek` preferences, the degraded read, and the budget); [`review-door.test.ts`](../../test/unit/today/review-door.test.ts) (the pure state rule, including the archived-Review case); [`review-door-authority.test.ts`](../../test/unit/today/review-door-authority.test.ts) (the one-import-path guard, FALSIFIED against a `planningWeekStart` re-derivation that agrees on every value); [`steer-week-door.spec.ts`](../../e2e/steer-week-door.spec.ts) (start → create → continue → resume → complete in a real browser, both appearances, four widths, `axe` clean with no rule disabled).
  - **What stays out, by the decision this entry already recorded.** Immutable source-record snapshots remain out of scope — REVIEW-03's audit concluded that freezing source labels makes a Review disagree with the records it points at — and nothing here adds Review machinery, a second period authority, or any change to the Review's content or steps.

### ☐ DEBT-35 — Assets: deferred capabilities (attachments, reminders, logbooks, ingestion, AI) — P3
- **Current issue.** ASSET-01 ships a deliberately complete-but-bounded first version: no real file attachments, no external object storage (R2), no OCR, no barcode/QR scanning, no recurring reminders or automated warranty/renewal alerts, no service-history logbook, no depreciation/tax or insurance-claims workflow, no receipt/email ingestion, no external subscription sync, no AI extraction, and no household sharing beyond current workspace rules. These are intentionally absent (no dead UI ships for any of them), but they are the natural next capabilities users will expect. The kernel already stores the queryable warranty/renewal/service dates and exposes `AssetRepository.list({ view: "expiring" | "service_due" })` as the bounded read seam a future Today widget / reminder engine will consume.
- **Desired future state.** ASSET-02 adds history & renewals (maintenance log, value-over-time, calm renewal reminders reading the existing dates) and a Today "expiring soon / service due" widget over the existing read seam; a later attachments story adds real object storage (R2) with OCR/barcode as optional enrichment — all reusing the shared seams, never a bespoke fork, and each documented with an ADR where it introduces a genuine new decision.
- **V2.8 disposition — NOT TAKEN (2026-09-02).** The smallest legitimate attachment capability and its prerequisites — one private R2 bucket bound to the application Worker, an `attachment` entity linked by EntityLink, an authenticated same-origin route, byte budgets before the body is read, inherited privacy class, a binary vault collection, and a backup/restore rehearsal for the second store BEFORE any owner file is accepted — are recorded in [`ROADMAP_V2_8.md`](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#attachments-assessed-step-4) so the next decision pass does not re-derive them. On `main` at `036d3da` the application Worker still has no R2 binding by written policy (`wrangler.jsonc`), and the export manifest still says in code that DalyHub stores no files (`app/platform/export/manifest.ts:118`).
- **V2.9 disposition — RE-HOMED, in two halves (2026-09-04).** Re-measured on `6b4d4a8`: unchanged (no R2 binding; `manifest.ts:118` and `build-vault.ts:1419` still record the absence). The **attachments** half — R2, the `attachment` entity, budgets, export, backup and restore of a second store, the phone picker and camera — is [V2.11 EVIDENCE](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_9.md#v211--evidence-planned), with the D1+R2 restore rehearsal as its first item. The **renewals and reminders for things that are not Assets** half is [V2.10 LIFE ADMIN](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_9.md#v210--life-admin-planned), through the shared Obligation model ([DEBT-240](#-debt-240--an-obligation-cannot-exist-without-an-asset-parent-and-carries-no-amount--p3)). OCR, barcode scanning, receipt or email ingestion, depreciation/tax and subscription sync stay here and are refused for V2 ([the V3 boundary](DALYHUB_POST_V2_8_PRODUCT_STRATEGY.md#12-the-v3-boundary)). The entry still closes empty, not resolved.
- **Related roadmap item.** [ASSET-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-asset-02--history--renewals--done); [ASSET-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-asset-03--mobile).
- **Still open after [ASSET-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-asset-03--mobile-assets--delivered-2026-08-08) (2026-08-08).** ASSET-03 made creating an Asset from a phone fast — the global `+` offers Asset and the type picker became a phone control — and deliberately added **none** of the capabilities in this entry. No scanning, no OCR, no lookup, no attachments, no AI classification, no reminders: a phone camera next to a capture form is exactly where those would have crept in, and they stay recorded here rather than half-built.
- **Impact.** None on any promise the product makes. Every item here is a capability ASSET-01 deliberately did not ship, stated as such, with no placeholder reserving space for it and no copy claiming it — the discipline [DEBT-53](#-debt-53--weather-and-calendar-on-today-were-removed-not-implemented--p3) records. What it costs is that an Asset's paperwork (a receipt, a warranty PDF) lives outside DalyHub.
- **Why it remains open.** It is a **future-feature entry, not implementation debt**, and it is kept open so the deferral stays visible rather than being rediscovered as an omission. Attachments in particular need R2, a size and retention policy, export coverage and a deletion story — a programme, not a field.
- **Closing condition.** Each named capability is either delivered under its own roadmap item or struck from this entry with a recorded decision that DalyHub does not do it — so the list shrinks by decision rather than by drift. **This entry closes empty, not resolved.**
- **Scope boundary (2026-07-27).** OCR, barcode/QR scanning, receipt or email ingestion, financial depreciation/tax workflows and external subscription sync stay in **this** entry as future debt. They are explicitly **not** part of [ASSET-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-asset-02--history--renewals--done), whose scope is service/maintenance history, warranty and renewal tracking, value changes, calm due/expiry surfacing and the Today read seam.

### ☑ DEBT-36 — Global search coverage is incomplete: several shipped modules register no provider — P2
- **Original issue.** DS-08 discovered search providers from the module registry, but only **five** manifests contributed one: Assets, Meetings, People, Reviews and Tasks (plus the fixture-backed Today provider). **Notes, Projects, Areas, Goals and Diary declared no `searchProviders` at all**, even though all five shipped real, workspace-scoped records. Global search therefore could not find a note, a project, an area, a goal or a diary entry by title — while simultaneously returning **fabricated** project/note/meeting hits from the Today fixture provider ([DEBT-17](#-debt-17--today-search-provider-is-fixture-backed-not-over-real-records--p1)). Command-palette coverage remains separate: `commands.ts` exists for Assets, Meetings, People, Reviews, Settings, Tasks and Today, but **Areas, Goals, Projects, Notes and Diary register no commands**, so there is no "Open Notes" or "New project" anywhere in the palette.
- **Impact before resolution.** The product's central promise — one searchable, cross-linked model — was not met for half the shipped modules, and the results a user *did* get were partly invented. This was the single largest gap between what DalyHub claimed and what a user could do in Search.
- **Desired state.** Each shipped module registers a real, repository-backed search provider returning canonical record targets (following the [`tasks/search.ts`](../../app/modules/tasks/search.ts) and [`reviews/search.ts`](../../app/modules/reviews/search.ts) precedent). The Today fixture provider is retired once nothing depends on it. No new search architecture — the registry seam already exists.
- **Narrowed (2026-07-28, NOTES-03) — the Notes half closed first.** Notes registered a real, repository-backed provider over **title, full Markdown body, headings and tags** (the first provider that searches a record's *body*, not just its header fields), plus five navigation commands. Each result states where it matched and shows a readable, syntax-free excerpt. The remaining gap before X-01 was Projects, Areas, Goals and Diary, plus the still-registered Today fixture provider ([DEBT-17](#-debt-17--today-search-provider-is-fixture-backed-not-over-real-records--p1)).
- **Related roadmap item.** [X-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-x-01--global-search-maturity); [NOTES-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-notes-03--organisation--search) ☑ for the Notes half; [DS-08](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-08--shared-search)/[DS-09](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-09--command-palette--quick-actions) for the shared seams.
- **Resolved (2026-07-29).** X-01 completes Search provider coverage for every
  shipped record type: Areas, Goals, Projects, Tasks, Notes, Diary, Meetings,
  People, Assets and Reviews. Areas/Goals/Projects/Diary gained real providers
  through their module manifests; Tasks now uses a richer bounded projection; the
  existing Notes/Meetings/People/Assets/Reviews providers remain real. Today is no
  longer a Search provider. `test/unit/module-registry/discovery.test.ts` asserts
  the exact production provider set, and `test/kernel/search-route.test.ts` seeds
  real records across all ten providers through the actual authenticated `/search`
  route.

### ☑ DEBT-37 — On-hold tasks appear on Today but are excluded from `/tasks` active planning views — P2
- **Current issue.** [TASKS-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-tasks-01--first-class-tasks-module) added `on_hold` as a first-class workflow status, and the `/tasks` `active` system view deliberately excludes it alongside completed, cancelled, Someday/Maybe and waiting ([`app/kernel/tasks/task.ts`](../../app/kernel/tasks/task.ts), ADR-043 §11) so a paused task stays out of a Matrix quadrant or Time Sector. But Today's planning read applies only `commitment_state <> 'someday' AND status <> 'cancelled'` ([`d1-task-repository.ts` `listPlanningTasks`](../../app/platform/storage/d1/d1-task-repository.ts)), so **an on-hold task still appears in Today's planning buckets** — and Today's `PlanningTaskItem` projection (`planning-view.ts` (since removed)) carries no `status`/`commitmentState`, so it renders indistinguishably from ordinary active work with no "On hold" label.
- **Impact.** The same task is "parked" on `/tasks` and "today's work" on `/today`. It contradicts [DEBT-28](#-debt-28--task-priority-is-invisible-where-triage-happens-and-status-resolves-three-different-ways--p2)'s resolution, which retired `taskDisplayStatus` precisely so every surface would resolve state identically — Today is the one surface that still does not run `taskDisplayState` at all.
- **Desired future state.** Decide the intent once and apply it in one place: either exclude `on_hold` from `listPlanningTasks` exactly as `/tasks` does, or widen the Today projection to carry the status and render the shared "On hold" state so the card is honest. Do not add a third state vocabulary.
- **Resolved (2026-07-31) by [TASKS-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-tasks-04--daily-driver-tasks-inbox-inline-editing-and-basic-recurrence).** The intent was decided ONCE and applied in one place: `listPlanningTasks` now excludes `on_hold` alongside Someday/Maybe and cancelled ([`d1-task-repository.ts`](../../app/platform/storage/d1/d1-task-repository.ts)), so a paused Task is not "today's work" on one surface and "parked" on another. No third state vocabulary was added and Today's projection is unchanged in shape. Proven by [`test/kernel/task-inbox-parent.test.ts`](../../test/kernel/task-inbox-parent.test.ts), which seeds one Task per state (active, in progress, waiting, on hold, Someday/Maybe, cancelled, completed) all scheduled for the same day and asserts the planning bands and the `/tasks` active view AGREE on every one of them — plus that a recurring successor shows on Today as ordinary active work and that completions stay visible so "completed today" still works.
- **Half of it came back, in the other direction, and TODAY-10 closed it (2026-08-12).** TASKS-04 applied the decision to `listPlanningTasks` (which Today reads) and left the canonical `/tasks` **date** views alone, so the same Task was "parked" on Today and "today's work" on `/tasks?system=today` — the original defect with the surfaces swapped, and invisible until TODAY-09 made the two surfaces' agreement an explicit contract. Measured on the heavy fixture with one on-hold Task due today: `/tasks?system=today` said "14 Tasks"; Today's own figure, which links straight to that view, said 12. The intent was NOT re-decided — this entry's decision stands, and `notParked` in [`d1-task-repository.ts`](../../app/platform/storage/d1/d1-task-repository.ts) now applies it to `today`, `upcoming` and `overdue` alongside the `waiting` exclusion those three already carried. `inbox` is deliberately untouched: it is about filing, not dating, and has never excluded waiting either. Proven by the set-equivalence block in [`test/kernel/today-route.test.ts`](../../test/kernel/today-route.test.ts) and by [`e2e/today-focus.spec.ts`](../../e2e/today-focus.spec.ts).
- **Related roadmap item.** [TASKS-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-tasks-04--daily-driver-tasks-inbox-inline-editing-and-basic-recurrence), [TASKS-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-tasks-01--first-class-tasks-module) / [TODAY-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-today-04--planning); [TODAY-10](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_2.md) for the follow-on.

### ☑ DEBT-38 — Notification toasts occlude bottom-anchored record actions — P1
- **Resolved (2026-07-27).** The DS-10 notification region no longer takes pointer input anywhere except its own controls. In [`app/styles/feedback.css`](../../app/styles/feedback.css), `.dh-feedback`, `.dh-feedback__toolbar` and `.dh-toast` are all `pointer-events: none`; only `.dh-feedback__dismiss-all`, `.dh-toast__action` and `.dh-toast__close` opt back in. Toasts stay fully visible and their Undo/Retry/Cancel/Dismiss controls stay operable; every other pixel of the region passes the click through to the page. One shared fix in the one shared feedback layer — no Reviews-only CSS, no test-only override, no forced or coordinate clicks anywhere in the suite.
- **What the original entry got half-right.** It identified the container/opt-in structure correctly but attributed the failure mainly to the toast stack. Measured on this branch (a probe over the real Reviews Settings tab at 1280×720): the *Restore review* button occupied y 425–470 and the **dismiss-all toolbar** occupied y 445–467 across the full 384px column, so `document.elementFromPoint` at the button's centre returned `div.dh-feedback__toolbar`. The toolbar is a full-width flex row containing one small right-aligned button — pure empty area absorbing clicks. The toast bodies are the second offender: the region grows upward from `bottom: 16px`, so five stacked toasts blanket y≈287–704 and can cover the same control. Both are fixed by the same rule set.
- **Hover-pause narrowed, deliberately and documented.** Auto-dismiss now pauses on focus anywhere in the region, or on hovering a toast's *controls*, rather than on hovering any part of a toast. A pointer crossing a click-through surface is interacting with the page beneath, not reading the toast, so pausing on it would prolong the very obstruction this fixes. Errors remain sticky, so nothing that must be read expires. Recorded in [`DESIGN_SYSTEM.md → Feedback`](../design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md#feedback-platform) and [`FEEDBACK_AND_INSPECTOR.md`](../development/FEEDBACK_AND_INSPECTOR.md).
- **Evidence.** Two guards, both of which fail on the pre-fix CSS (verified by reverting it): [`test/unit/feedback/notification-pointer-events.test.ts`](../../test/unit/feedback/notification-pointer-events.test.ts) checks the rule set at source; `e2e/feedback.spec.ts` → *"the notification stack never intercepts clicks meant for the page"* hit-tests the **whole** region with `document.elementFromPoint` on a 4px grid at **both** 1280×720 and 390×780, asserting no non-control pixel is hit-testable, that every control still is, and that Undo and Dismiss-all still work with ordinary clicks. End to end, `e2e/reviews.spec.ts` (*archive → restore*) passes, including on repeat runs — see [DEBT-41](#-debt-41--the-e2e-suite-is-unreliable-on-main-so-ci-is-green-claims-are-unverifiable--p1--resolved-2026-08-02).
- **Related roadmap item.** [DS-10](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-ds-10--inspector-settings-and-feedback-states) (the shared feedback layer); unblocks [REVIEWS-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-reviews-01--dalyhub-reviews-foundation) verification.

### ☑ DEBT-39 — `[[Wiki Links]]` create no EntityLink, and the resolver scans the whole workspace — P2
- **Current issue.** REL-01's wiki links are resolved at **navigation** time: [`wikilinks.ts`](../../app/platform/markdown/wikilinks.ts) rewrites `[[Title]]` to `/notes/resolve?title=…` and [`notes/routes/resolve.tsx`](../../app/modules/notes/routes/resolve.tsx) finds a matching entity and redirects. Two consequences follow.
  1. **No backlink is created.** Because no EntityLink row is written, a wiki-linked record has no idea it was referenced — the reference is invisible from the target's side and absent from its Linked Items and Activity. This is the substantive part of what [NOTES-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-notes-02--linking--backlinks) still owes, distinct from the *presentation* gap in [DEBT-08](#-debt-08--ad-hoc-cross-entity-links--p2).
  2. **The resolver is an unbounded read.** It pages through **every** entity in the workspace with a deliberate "no page cutoff" (documented in the route), stopping early only on a note match.
