### ☐ DEBT-76 — A Chromium renderer segfault fails Playwright shards non-deterministically, and `retries: 0` turns it into a red build — P2

- **Current issue.** `chrome-headless-shell-1228` on the `ubuntu-24.04` runner image intermittently dies mid-run with `Received signal 11 SEGV_MAPERR 0000000001b0` (`cr2: 0x1b0`, identical stack every time). The test that happens to be executing then fails with `browser.newContext: Target page, context or browser has been closed` — **no assertion has failed and nothing is wrong with the code**, but the shard exits non-zero and `CI Gate` goes red because it aggregates `playwright`.
- **It is not new, and it is not any one branch's.** The same signature appears on **`main` at [`6aba3ae`](https://github.com/acedaly/DalyHub-V2/commit/6aba3ae) (run 30802345484, shard 1, `/people` axe scan)** and on [PR #106](https://github.com/acedaly/DalyHub-V2/pull/106) (run 30841044978, shards 3 and 5, `diary` and `people`). It was briefly and wrongly attributed to a scroll-driven animation in that PR; the `main` occurrence predates that code, which is what settles it. The crash favours axe scans and repeated-viewport-resize tests — long-lived pages doing heavy layout work — but has hit at least three different specs.
- **Impact.** **Four of the ten most recent `main` CI runs are red**, and a red `main` is corrosive in a specific way: it stops being information. Once a maintainer learns that failures are usually noise, a real regression rides in behind one, and the cost of the flake is paid by the change that follows it rather than by the flake itself. It also makes every PR's CI a coin toss on 14 shards — the more shards, the likelier at least one crashes.
- **2026-08-07 — a fourth occurrence, and the shard count has moved against us.** On [PR #124](https://github.com/acedaly/DalyHub-V2/pull/124) (run 31134265194, head `3a0228b`) **shard 2/18** died during `e2e/accessibility.spec.ts:141` — the `/design/search` axe scan, a fifth distinct spec and again an axe scan, matching the pattern this entry already describes. The signature is identical to the letter: `Received signal 11 SEGV_MAPERR 0000000001b0`, `cr2: 00000000000001b0`, same `chrome-headless-shell-1228` stack. The shard reported **1 failed, 68 passed**, the other **17 shards were green**, and the test passes locally under `--repeat-each=3` (3/3) — so nothing in the diff is implicated. Two things are worth recording beyond "it happened again". First, **the matrix is 18 shards now, not the 14 this entry was written against**; since each shard is an independent chance to crash, every widening of the split has quietly raised the odds that a run is red for this reason alone, which means the split decisions and this entry are coupled in a way neither noted. Second, **re-running the failed job is not always available** — an automation without `actions: write` cannot clear a crash-only failure, so the only route back to green is a fresh push, which spends another full 18-shard run on a coin toss. That asymmetry is the practical cost of `retries: 0` here, and it is an argument for trying the browser-build upgrade **first**, as the remedy below already prefers.
- **2026-08-07 — the preferred remedy was tried and did NOT work; the crash follows the browser forward.** [PR #125](https://github.com/acedaly/DalyHub-V2/pull/125) took the remedy this entry prefers — keep `retries: 0`, move the browser build — and upgraded `@playwright/test` 1.61.1 → 1.62.1 specifically because "the crash is specific to `chrome-headless-shell-1228`". It is not. On [PR #126](https://github.com/acedaly/DalyHub-V2/pull/126) the identical signature appeared **twice, on two different commits and two different shards**, on the NEW browser: run 31152862102 shard 2/18 (job 92786092584, head `b449c7d`) and run 31154576594 shard 3/18 (job 92791337437, head `7b34772`). Both read `Received signal 11 SEGV_MAPERR 0000000001b0`, `cr2: 00000000000001b0`, in `chromium_headless_shell-**1234**` — one build number different, one byte of evidence identical. Both died inside `e2e/ai-assistance.spec.ts` during an axe scan, which is the sixth distinct spec and the same axe pattern this entry has recorded every time. Both shards reported **1 failed, 71 passed** with no assertion failure of any kind.
- **What that changes about the remedy.** The upgrade was the right thing to try first and it has now been tried; the crash is not a property of build 1228. So the branch of the plan that says "pin/upgrade the browser build, since the crash is specific to 1228" is **closed as ineffective**, and what remains is the `retries: process.env.CI ? 1 : 0` change this entry already describes — with the flaky-not-passed reporting that keeps the noise visible. That is a testing-contract change and belongs in its own PR with its own reasoning, not folded into a product change; PR #126 deliberately recorded this evidence rather than absorbing the fix.
- **Desired future state.** A shard that fails only because the browser died retries and passes, and a shard that fails because an assertion failed still goes red immediately.
- **How it would be done, so the path is not re-derived.** The repository sets `retries: 0` in [`playwright.config.ts`](../../playwright.config.ts) deliberately — "no retries that could mask flakiness" (ADR-008/ADR-016), and that instinct is right for **assertion** flakiness. A browser-process crash is a different class: it is not the product being non-deterministic, it is the harness dying. The narrow change is `retries: process.env.CI ? 1 : 0`, which leaves local runs strict; Playwright's HTML report marks a retried test `flaky` rather than `passed`, so the noise stays **visible** instead of being swallowed — which is the property that makes this different from simply weakening the gate. A stricter alternative is to keep `retries: 0` and pin/upgrade the Playwright browser build, since the crash is specific to `chrome-headless-shell-1228`; that is the better fix if an upgrade makes it go away, and it should be tried first.
- **Closing condition.** Ten consecutive `main` runs green, with any retried test still reported as flaky rather than silently passing.
- **Related roadmap item.** None — CI hygiene. Surfaced by [DS-14](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-ds-14--whole-application-visual-overhaul).

### ☑ DEBT-77 — A project card cannot say what the next action is — P3 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-28 (V2.5 STEER-04)**

- **Current issue.** POLISH-02's brief asked Today's project cards to carry a **next action** alongside progress and health. They now carry health for every project (not only the ones in trouble), the open-task count and a progress meter — all derived from data the loader already reads — but not the next action, because there is none to read. [`listProjectHealthFacts`](../../app/kernel/project-health/project-health-repository.ts) aggregates *counts* per project (`overdueOpen`, `waitingOpen`, `upcomingDueOpen`, …), not the identity of any task, and [`listProjects`](../../app/platform/storage/d1/d1-project-repository.ts) returns roll-ups rather than children.
- **Impact.** The owner can see that a project needs attention and how far along it is, but must open it to learn what to actually do. On a surface whose whole purpose is "what should I do now?", that is one click more than it should be for the six projects the section shows.
- **Desired future state.** Each "Continue working" card names its next actionable task — the highest-priority open, non-waiting task with the nearest scheduled or due date — as a row that opens that task in the same Drawer Today already hosts.
- **How it would be done, so the path is not re-derived.** This must NOT become six queries on the most-visited route in the product. The shape that fits the existing code is a single bounded, workspace-scoped statement over the six project ids — a `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY project ORDER BY <the Tasks smart-sort expression>)` filtered to rank 1 — added beside `listProjectHealthFacts` and read in the same `Promise.all`, returning a `Map<projectId, TaskListItem>`. The smart-sort expression already exists in [`d1-task-repository.ts`](../../app/platform/storage/d1/d1-task-repository.ts); reuse it rather than inventing a second notion of "next", or Today and `/tasks` will disagree about which task is next.
- **Closing condition.** Every card in "Continue working" names its next action, the route's query count is unchanged (one additional statement, not N), and a test pins Today's "next" to the same ordering `/tasks` uses.
- **Related roadmap item.** [POLISH-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-polish-02--the-today-command-centre).
- **Still open, with a proven rule to reuse (2026-08-05).** [REVIEW-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-review-02--weekly-review--delivered-2026-08-05) needed the same answer for its Project check and derived one WITHOUT a per-project query: ONE bounded scan of the workspace's most actionable open Tasks under the canonical `smart` sort, bucketed by Project, first-per-Project wins — and where a Project's work falls outside that bound it says "No next action visible here" rather than claiming there is none. That is a deliberately cheaper approximation than the `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY …)` statement described above, and it does NOT close this entry: Today's cards still name no next action, and Today should use the exact ranked statement so it can never disagree with `/tasks`. Reuse the wording ("No next action visible here") and the never-invent rule; do not reuse the bounded scan for a surface that must be exhaustive.
- **Closing condition (unchanged).** Every card in "Continue working" names its next action, the route's query count is unchanged, and a test pins Today's "next" to the same ordering `/tasks` uses.
- **V2.5 disposition — TAKEN, with this entry's closing condition made assertable.** [STEER-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-04--from-signal-to-step--delivered-2026-08-28) closes this by this entry's own path — the exact ranked statement, the reused smart-sort expression — and reads the same rule for a Goal's next step through its contributing Projects, so "next" exists once ([ADR-111](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-111-steering--owner-judgement-is-stored-beside-derived-signals-never-merged--one-next-action-rule-one-goal-story-and-a-collection-order-that-answers-a-recorded-question) decision 4). **One clarification, recorded because a budget test cannot hold both halves of the phrase:** the closing condition's *"query count is unchanged (one additional statement, not N)"* is read as its parenthetical — the budget moves by **exactly one** bounded statement and does not grow with the cards. "Unchanged" and "one additional" are otherwise mutually exclusive, and the entry's own how-it-would-be-done section (one `ROW_NUMBER()` statement beside `listProjectHealthFacts`) says which was meant.
- **RESOLVED 2026-08-28 by V2.5 STEER-04, by the path this entry itself prescribed in 2026 and never deviated from.**
  - **The statement is the one described here.** `TaskRepository.listProjectNextActions` ([`d1-task-repository.ts`](../../app/platform/storage/d1/d1-task-repository.ts)) is a single bounded, workspace-scoped `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY parent_id ORDER BY <the smart-sort expression>)` filtered to rank 1, returning `Map<projectId, TaskListItem>`. It reaches its population through `#resolveWorkspaceScope("active", { blocked: false })` and its ordering through `#workspaceSortSpec("smart")` — the SAME code paths `/tasks` uses, so there is nothing to keep in step.
  - **"A test pins Today's 'next' to the same ordering `/tasks` uses"** — three of them, in [`test/kernel/task-next-action.test.ts`](../../test/kernel/task-next-action.test.ts): the repository equals the pure kernel rule over a seeded fact matrix; the repository equals the FIRST row the canonical `/tasks` collection read returns for the same Project under the same view, sort and filters; and the pure sort key is asserted character-for-character against the SQL expression's four segments.
  - **"The route's query count … one additional statement, not N"** — measured with a counting database: the read is ONE statement for two Projects and ONE for eight, and `loadTodayDay`'s total is identical for two cards and six.
  - **The exclusions are existing DalyHub states, not new ones**: completed, cancelled, on hold, Someday/Maybe, waiting (TODAY-03) and dependency-blocked (TASKS-12, derived from live `task.blocks` edges rather than a stored flag). A blocked Task is never called "next".
  - **The wording and the never-invent rule are REVIEW-02's, reused as this entry asked.** Where nothing is eligible a record says *"No next action visible here"*; Today's cards render nothing at all, because a row of absences on a three-card list costs more than it says.
  - **The Review's bounded scan is untouched.** This entry's 2026-08-05 note asked that the cheaper approximation not be reused for a surface that must be exhaustive, and that the exhaustive statement not replace it where it is honestly disclosed. Both held.

### ☑ DEBT-78 — Goals can state completion but not trend — P3 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-27 (V2.4 FOLLOW-02)**

- **Narrowed, not closed.** [GOAL-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md) answered this for a
  Goal that carries a MEASUREMENT: a measurable Goal now records readings over
  time, states its recent pace against the pace it needs, and shows a trend line —
  all from one derivation (`evaluateGoalProgress`) that Today, the Goals gallery
  and the Goal record share, so they cannot disagree. What remains is the case
  this entry was originally written about: a Goal whose only progress signal is
  its CONTRIBUTING PROJECTS. "40% of Projects complete" still reads the same on a
  Goal that gained two this month and one that has not moved since March, and the
  approach below (a bounded Activity query over the contributing project ids) is
  still the right way to close it.

- **Original issue.** POLISH-02's brief asked the Goals widget for **trend, completion % and recent progress**. It now shows completion (from the contribution read the alignment evaluation already performs) and recent progress (the derived alignment label — "Recent action" / "No recent action"). It cannot show a trend, because nothing in the system stores a goal's completion *over time*: [`listGoalProjectContributions`](../../app/platform/storage/d1/d1-goal-repository.ts) returns the current roll-up only, and there is no snapshot table or historical projection to difference against.
- **Impact.** The owner sees where a goal stands but not whether it is moving. "40% complete" reads the same on a goal that gained two projects this month and one that has not moved since March — and *is it moving?* is the question a Goal exists to answer.
- **Desired future state.** A goal states its direction over a meaningful window ("+2 Projects complete this month", or a sparkline), on Today and on the Goal record, from one shared derivation.
- **How it would be done, so the path is not re-derived.** Do NOT add a snapshot table first — the Activity stream is already the historical record ([ADR-005](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-005-shared-activity-model)), and a goal's contributing projects completing is a `project.completed` activity on a project linked to the goal. A bounded activity query over the goal's contributing project ids within the window gives the delta without any new write path or migration. The derivation belongs in [`~/shared/alignment`](../../app/shared/alignment) beside the existing evaluator, so Today and the Goal record cannot disagree.
- **Closing condition.** A goal's direction is stated in the same words on Today and on its record, derived once, with no new table and no per-goal query on the Today route.
- **V2.4 disposition — TAKEN.** [FOLLOW-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-follow-02--did-the-goals-move--delivered-2026-08-27) closes this entry, by the path this entry itself prescribes: a bounded Activity query over the contributing Project ids inside a named window, derived once in `~/shared/alignment`. **No snapshot table** — that refusal is now a recorded decision ([ADR-110](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-110-follow-through-is-derived-from-the-activity-stream-never-stored--one-period-account-no-adherence-score-and-no-snapshot-table-for-a-plan-or-a-goal)) rather than advice inside a debt entry.
- **RESOLVED 2026-08-27 by [V2.4 FOLLOW-02](V2_4_FOLLOW_02_GOAL_MOVEMENT_2026_08.md), against this entry's own closing condition, word by word.**

  > *"A goal's direction is stated in the same words on Today and on its record, derived once, with no new table and no per-goal query on the Today route."*

  - **The same words**, and on the Goals collection as well: Today, `/goals` (row and pane) and the Goal record all render ONE component from ONE `GoalMovement` value. The E2E journey reads a stable machine key (`data-goal-movement`, `-events`, `-projects`) from all three and asserts they are EQUAL OBJECTS — not three sentences that happen to match today.
  - **Derived once.** `evaluateGoalMovement` in `app/kernel/alignment/goal-movement.ts`, re-exported through `~/shared/alignment` exactly where this entry said to put it, over `ActivityWindowRepository.readGoalMovementFacts` — the bounded Activity query over the contributing Project ids inside a named window this entry prescribed in 2026-08-09.
  - **No new table.** No column, no index, no migration, no schema or API change. Asserted rather than intended: a real-D1 test counts the workspace's Activity rows before and after two movement reads and fails if the number moves.
  - **No per-Goal query on the Today route.** EXACTLY TWO D1 statements for a whole page, with a flatness proof in both directions — six Goals cost what two do, and a Goal with twelve completions costs what one with a single completion does, because the aggregation happens in SQL. Bound parameters are `N + 1` and `N + 10` (51 and 60 at a fifty-Goal page) against D1's ceiling of 100, because the id list is bound ONCE per statement through a `VALUES` CTE rather than three times.

  **The original sentence, answered.** *"40% complete reads the same on a goal that gained two projects this month and one that has not moved since March"* — reproduced on `main` at `e1ba3e4` against a known fixture, where a Goal that moved on Monday and a Goal whose last completion was four days before the week opened were drawn identically as `DalyHub V2 · No measurement`. They now read *"Moved this week. · 1 Project contributed · 1 Task completed"* and *"No movement yet this week."*

  **What movement means was defined before any UI was written**, and the refusals are the definition: renaming a Project is Activity and is NOT the Goal moving; creating a Task is intent, not outcome; reopening a completed Task is an outcome being undone; and `goal.target_reached` is the same atomic write as the reading that caused it. Each has a test, and the metadata refusal was falsified by deliberately counting `entity.updated` and observing the intended failure.
- **Related roadmap item.** [POLISH-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-polish-02--the-today-command-centre); [FOLLOW-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-follow-02--did-the-goals-move--delivered-2026-08-27).

### ☐ DEBT-150 — A plan row restates the date its own band already states — P3

- **Current issue.** Today's plan groups the day into three named bands — Overdue, Due today, Planned today — and every row inside a band draws the shared row's DATE cell, which on "Due today" reads "Today" on every row and on "Planned today" reads "Today" on every row. MEASURED on the seeded fixture at 393: eight rows, seven of them printing a date that the heading twelve pixels above them has already stated, in a metadata line that also has to hold the project and the priority.
- **Why it was not changed in [TODAY-TASK-01](../design/TODAY_TASK_01_ONE_TASK_ROW_2026_08.md).** It is not a Today defect. `/tasks` grouped by due state does exactly the same thing for exactly the same reason — the row shows its own date and the group states the bucket — so suppressing it on Today alone would be a Today-only rule on the row that pass exists to stop having Today-only rules on. And the cell is not a label: it is the EDITOR, so it cannot simply be hidden without taking the inline reschedule with it.
- **Impact.** Small and cosmetic. What it costs is width on a phone's metadata line and a little scanning noise on a desktop; nothing is wrong or misleading.
- **Desired future state.** A SHARED capability on `TaskList` — an "implied date" the list declares once — which lets a row draw its date cell in its EMPTY presentation (the control, no value) when the value merely restates the group. It has to be shared, it has to keep the control reachable and it has to keep the accessible name honest ("Due date: Today"), which is why it is a design decision rather than a `display: none`.
- **Closing condition.** A grouped day (Today) and a grouped list (`/tasks?group=due`) both stop printing the bucket's own date on every row, through one declaration on the shared list, with the date still editable from the row and still announced in full.
- **Related roadmap item.** A future Tasks/Today refinement; the mechanism belongs with DS-04's row anatomy.

### ☑ DEBT-120 — The Goals gallery is ordered by alignment, not by outcome — P3 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-28 (V2.5 STEER-01)**

- **Current issue.** `/goals` is ordered by the workspace-wide alignment rank (DEBT-23): neglected Goals first, then active, then completed. That is the ADR-040 Alignment view's own ordering and it is correct for the question ADR-040 asked. UIX-03 changed the question the screen answers — it is now an outcomes gallery — and under that reading the order is arbitrary: an unmeasured Goal with no recent Task activity can sit above a measured Goal that is behind its own target date.
- **Why it was not changed here.** The order is established in SQL BEFORE pagination and the keyset cursor is bound to it, so re-ranking means a second ranking expression, a second cursor scope and a status the database can compute — and the status is a kernel derivation over measurements, dates and the owner's calendar. UIX-03 gave the owner the lens instead (the All / On track / Needs attention / Completed views), which answers "which Goals need me?" without a query change.
- **Desired future state.** Decide whether `/goals` is the Alignment view or the outcomes gallery. If the latter, an outcome-first ordering needs its own ranking expression and cursor scope, designed together with whether alignment keeps a surface of its own.
- **Impact.** The gallery answers *"which Goal have I been neglecting?"* on a screen UIX-03 turned into *"how are my outcomes going?"*. Nothing is hidden and nothing is wrong — the order is correct for a question the screen no longer asks — so the cost is one of emphasis: a completed Goal and a neglected one sit in an order that reads as a ranking of importance and is a ranking of attention.
- **Why it remains open.** It is **a decision, blocked behind a scheduled item**. What `/goals` IS — the Alignment view or the outcomes gallery — must be settled before its order can be, and [FOLLOW-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-follow-02--did-the-goals-move--delivered-2026-08-27) is building the movement statement an outcome ordering would sort on. Re-ranking now means inventing a second ranking expression and a second cursor scope against a fact that does not exist yet.
- **Closing condition.** `/goals` states which question it answers (recorded, not implied), and its order is established workspace-wide in SQL before pagination for THAT question with the keyset cursor bound to it — with the Alignment ordering kept somewhere if it is still wanted, rather than silently lost.
- **Related roadmap item.** [UIX-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_2.md); [FOLLOW-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-follow-02--did-the-goals-move--delivered-2026-08-27); [ADR-040](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md) (the Alignment ordering this inherits).
- **V2.4 disposition — NARROWED, not taken.** [FOLLOW-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-follow-02--did-the-goals-move--delivered-2026-08-27) gives every Goal a movement statement, which is the fact an outcome-ordered gallery would sort on. Whether the gallery's ORDER then changes is a separate presentation decision, needing the second ranking expression and cursor scope this entry names, and it is not in that item's scope.
- **NARROWED 2026-08-27 by [V2.4 FOLLOW-02](V2_4_FOLLOW_02_GOAL_MOVEMENT_2026_08.md), which took the half of this decision it could take and RECORDED it — and left the entry open rather than forcing a closure.**
  - **The half FOLLOW-02 settles: movement is an ATTENTION signal, not an outcome metric.** *"Did work that serves this Goal produce an outcome in the last seven days?"* is a question about the owner's engagement, in the same family as ADR-040's *"has this Goal had recent contributing activity?"* — not in the same family as *"is this Goal's number on schedule?"*. Adding movement therefore **strengthens** the alignment reading of `/goals` rather than converting the surface, and re-ranking on it would produce close to the order the collection already has. So the order does not change, and movement is documented as a signal WITHIN the alignment ordering rather than as a competing rank. **No card is re-sorted in React**, and the keyset cursor is untouched.
  - **The half it does NOT settle, which is why this stays open.** The surface still carries UIX-03's MEASUREMENT lenses (All / On track / Needs attention / Completed), and whether GOAL-02's derived status should govern the order is the unresolved question this entry was really about. Answering it still needs everything this entry already names: a second ranking expression, a second cursor scope, and a status the database can compute — while the status is a kernel derivation over measurements, dates and the owner's calendar. That is a disproportionate architecture change for a movement item, and closing on the half FOLLOW-02 happens to answer would leave the other half undocumented.
  - **The closing condition is unchanged**, and one of its two clauses is now met in writing: `/goals` states which question it answers (the alignment/attention question, recorded here and in FOLLOW-02's §11). What remains is the order for the OTHER question, if the product decides `/goals` should answer it.
- **V2.5 disposition — TAKEN.** [STEER-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-01--what-goals-answers--delivered-2026-08-28) takes the remaining half as its one recorded decision: `/goals` orders for the outcomes question, workspace-wide in SQL before pagination with a scope-bound cursor and a SQL↔kernel parity test, while `listGoalsByAlignment` is KEPT for the consumers that still ask the alignment question (the guided Review, insights, attention facts, Analytics) — the "kept somewhere" clause satisfied structurally rather than by promise.
- **RESOLVED 2026-08-28 by STEER-01, against this entry's closing condition clause by clause.**
  - **`/goals` states which question it answers, recorded rather than implied.** `GOAL_OUTCOME_QUESTION` in [`app/kernel/goals/goal-outcome.ts`](../../app/kernel/goals/goal-outcome.ts) — *"How are my outcomes going — and which need my decision first?"* — restated with its full precedence table and the argument for each rung in [`GOALS_MODULE.md`](../development/GOALS_MODULE.md#steer-01--what-goals-answers-v25-2026-08-28).
  - **Its order is established workspace-wide in SQL BEFORE pagination for THAT question, with the keyset cursor bound to it.** `GoalRepository.listGoalsByOutcome` computes `GOAL_OUTCOME_DISPLAY_RANK` over GOAL-02's derived status in the read; the cursor is bound to workspace + owner day + time zone + lens, so it cannot be replayed against a different question. This entry's stated blockers were built rather than worked around: the second ranking expression, the second cursor scope, and "a status the database can compute" — the last being a layered SQL derivation over the same stored facts the evaluator reads, with the schedule origin resolved by one bounded preliminary statement because SQLite cannot do IANA conversion and an approximate date would break exact parity.
  - **The SQL rank and the kernel comparator cannot disagree** — [`test/kernel/goal-outcome.test.ts`](../../test/kernel/goal-outcome.test.ts) drives both over one seeded matrix covering all nine statuses plus explicit completion, the `GOAL_ALIGNMENT_DISPLAY_RANK` precedent this entry asked for.
  - **The Alignment ordering is kept, not silently lost.** `listGoalsByAlignment` is unchanged and still serves the guided Review, the insights read, Today's attention facts and Analytics; alignment is still stated on `/goals` as the pane's indicator and in each row's accessible name.
  - **The entry's own exemplar defect is inverted and asserted:** an unmeasured Goal with no recent activity can no longer sit above a measured Goal that is behind its own target date.
  - **Falsified.** Sorting the page after pagination (rather than ordering before it) fails three tests, including one that walks four pages of a ten-Goal workspace.

### ☑ DEBT-121 — Status view counts describe the loaded page, not the workspace — P3 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-28 (V2.5 STEER-01)**

- **Current issue.** The Goals status views carry counts ("On track 3"), derived from the Goals loaded so far. A workspace with more Goals than one page shows counts for the page, beside a subtitle that already says "N Goals loaded".
- **Why it was not changed here.** A workspace-wide count per status means computing every Goal's derived status server-side for the whole workspace on every collection render — the status depends on measurement history, target dates and the owner's calendar day, so it cannot be a cheap aggregate. The per-page limitation is the same one ADR-040 §40.9 already discloses for the alignment recap, and the counts are consistent with the cards beneath them, which is the property that matters most.
- **Impact, and it is a TRUST cost rather than a cosmetic one.** "On track 3" is read as a statement about the workspace, and it is a statement about the page — so a workspace with more Goals than one page shows a number that is quietly wrong for the question it appears to answer. The mitigation is real but weak: the subtitle beside it says "N Goals loaded", which asks the reader to notice a qualifier and apply it to a figure two elements away.
- **Why it remains open.** A workspace-wide count means computing every Goal's derived status server-side on every collection render, and the status depends on measurement history, target dates and the owner's calendar day — so it is not a cheap aggregate, and doing it eagerly would put an unbounded derivation on a collection read. The honest alternatives are a bounded materialised status or dropping the counts, and choosing between them is a product decision about whether the figure is worth its cost.
- **Closing condition.** Either each status count is a workspace-wide figure computed within the collection's existing query budget — asserted with a counting-database test over a workspace of more than one page — or the counts are removed and the status views carry no number at all. **A count that describes the page must not remain beside a label that reads as the workspace.**
- **Related roadmap item.** [UIX-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_2.md); [AREA-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2.md#-area-02--goals).
- **Desired future state.** Either a bounded materialised status the collection can aggregate, or drop the counts if the workspace-wide figure is what owners read them as.
- **V2.5 disposition — TAKEN.** [STEER-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-01--what-goals-answers--delivered-2026-08-28) adopts this entry's closing sentence as an acceptance criterion verbatim: every lens filters the workspace with a workspace-true count under a stated budget, or the counts are removed — a count that describes the page does not remain beside a label that reads as the workspace.
- **RESOLVED 2026-08-28 by STEER-01, taking the FIRST of the two honest alternatives this entry named.**
  - **The count is a workspace-wide figure computed within the collection's query budget.** `GoalRepository.countGoalsByOutcomeLens` returns every lens's figure in ONE aggregate over the same status and lens expressions the page read is filtered by — so a lens's number and its result set cannot disagree — beside one bounded statement resolving schedule origins. TWO statements, flat in Goals, measurements, milestones and events, asserted with a counting database.
  - **Asserted over a workspace of more than one page**, which is the property this entry exists for: every lens is walked page by page at a page size of one and two, and its member count compared against the aggregate. A page-local implementation passes on one page and fails here.
  - **The page-derived helper is GONE rather than corrected.** `goalViewCounts` no longer exists; the client renders the loader's workspace figures and never tallies items. Where the workspace figure is unavailable — the Deleted scope, or a failed read — **no lens shows a number at all**, which is this entry's sentence applied to the residual case rather than a fallback that would reintroduce it.
  - **Falsified.** Making the counts page-local (bounding the counted set to the first page) fails the multi-page test immediately.

### ☐ DEBT-122 — `ExpressiveSummary` now has no consumer — P3

- **Current issue.** UIX-03 replaced the Goals gallery's expressive banner (a ring, two counts and a headline, all describing alignment rather than an outcome) with a compact status-view row. The Goals collection was `ExpressiveSummary`'s **last** consumer, so the component, its styles, its `MAX_SUMMARY_STATS` contract and its M3X "hierarchy Level 1" documentation now describe something no product surface renders.
- **Why it was not removed here.** It is a documented design-system component with a stated role in the M3X hierarchy, and `SupportingSurface` is defined in relation to it. Deleting it is a design-system decision — is "one dominant expressive surface per page" still a rule the product wants? — not a tidy-up to fold into a Goals redesign.
- **Impact.** Nothing an owner can see: dead code ships nothing, because it is tree-shaken out of every route that does not import it. What it costs is **documentation that is no longer true** — the M3X hierarchy describes a Level 1 the product does not use, and `SupportingSurface` is defined *in relation to* a surface with no consumer, so a future author composing "one dominant expressive surface per page" is following a rule nothing demonstrates.
- **Enlarged 2026-08-25.** `SupportingSurface` has no product consumer either, which makes this a question about the **whole M3X hierarchy** rather than about one component: is "one dominant expressive surface per page" still a rule DalyHub wants, now that DHDS is the governing design language and the shared card family answers the same jobs? Deleting the component without answering that leaves the rule; keeping it without answering that leaves the rule undemonstrated.
- **Why it remains open.** It is a **design-system decision, not a cleanup**. Deleting a documented primitive is a statement about the hierarchy that defines it, and this pass is not the place to make it — the same reason DHDS-13 gives for the findings it raised rather than took.
- **Closing condition.** An ADR or a DALYHUB_DESIGN_SYSTEM.md amendment states whether the M3X expressive hierarchy survives DHDS. If it does, at least one surface composes `ExpressiveSummary` and at least one composes `SupportingSurface`, so the rule is demonstrated rather than described. If it does not, both components, their styles and the hierarchy's documentation are retired **together** — never the component alone.
- **Related roadmap item.** [UIX-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_2.md) (removed the last consumer); [ADR-092](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-092-the-dalyhub-design-system-becomes-the-governing-design-language--a-product-owned-semantic-layer-an-explicit-density-model-and-md3-demoted-to-machinery) (DHDS as the governing language).
- **Desired future state.** Either a surface adopts it (the Reviews insights page is the obvious candidate), or the M3X hierarchy is restated without a Level 1 and the component, its styles and its docs are retired together.

Deleting the component while leaving the document describing it would swap a dead component for a lying document, which is worse.

### ☑ DEBT-79 — Asset permanent delete writes no audit event and destroys history — P2 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-05**

- **Current issue.** [AUDIT-03] `d1-asset-repository.ts:842` `permanentlyDelete` runs a six-DELETE batch (`:930`) with **no `activities` insert**, hard-deleting `asset_events`/`asset_obligations` and removing `activity_subjects` pointers, so the workspace feed keeps no tombstone that the asset or its service/financial history ever existed. The Area purge (`d1-spine-repository.ts:1481`) does the opposite — a retained `area.deleted` event carrying `{areaId, title}`.
- **Impact.** Irreversible history loss with no audit trail that a destruction happened — weakens the "Activity is the audit trail" guarantee (AGENTS.md §17).
- **Desired future state.** The asset purge writes a guarded, subject-less `asset.deleted` tombstone with `{assetId, title}`, on the Area purge pattern.
- **Closing condition.** A kernel test counts exactly one `asset.deleted` event after a purge and asserts the workspace feed retains it.
- **Resolved (2026-08-05, AUDIT-FIX-03).** Reproduced first against real Workers/D1: purging an Asset with one history event, one obligation and three Activity rows removed every domain row, retained the three `activities` rows, removed all three subject pointers, and wrote **0** `asset.deleted` events — the type did not exist. The kernel now defines `ASSET_DELETED`, and `permanentlyDelete` appends one subject-less tombstone carrying `{assetId, title}`, inserted DIRECTLY after the `entities` DELETE and guarded on that statement's `changes()`, so a blocked, already-gone or race-losing purge appends nothing. The existing strengths — active-link precheck, commit-time guards on every destructive statement, child-first FK-safe ordering, typed `AssetStorageError`, idempotent already-gone result — are preserved unchanged. **Evidence.** Source: [`app/platform/storage/d1/d1-asset-repository.ts`](../../app/platform/storage/d1/d1-asset-repository.ts) (`permanentlyDelete`, TEST-ONLY `deleteFault`), [`app/kernel/assets/asset-identifiers.ts`](../../app/kernel/assets/asset-identifiers.ts) (`ASSET_DELETED`), [`app/modules/assets/asset-activity.ts`](../../app/modules/assets/asset-activity.ts) + [`module.ts`](../../app/modules/assets/module.ts) (descriptor + manifest). Tests: five new real Workers/D1 cases in [`test/kernel/asset.test.ts`](../../test/kernel/asset.test.ts) — tombstone count/payload/subject-lessness with the workspace feed asserted to render it, second-purge idempotency, active-link blocking then release, a commit-time link race, and fault-injected rollback at both `after-entity` and `after-tombstone` — plus the shared invariants in [`test/kernel/permanent-delete-contract.test.ts`](../../test/kernel/permanent-delete-contract.test.ts).
- **Related finding.** [AUDIT-03](END_TO_END_AUDIT_2026_08_05.md#audit-03--asset-permanent-delete-writes-no-audit-event-and-destroys-history--p2). **Related roadmap item.** [AUDIT-FIX-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-audit-fix-03--permanent-delete-integrity-asset--review-purge-p2).

### ☑ DEBT-80 — Review permanent delete: broken event ordering, non-idempotent — P2 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-05**

- **Current issue.** [AUDIT-04] `d1-review-repository.ts:538` orders the append-activity statements before the deletes and lets the batch's own `deleteSubjects` remove the event's subject row; payload is `{}` (`:544`), so a surviving tombstone cannot name the review. This violates the recorder contract (`d1-activity-recorder.ts:44`, guard `WHERE changes() > 0`). A raced second purge fails on the subject-insert FK → `ReviewStorageError` instead of an idempotent `{deleted:false}`, and active links are silently destroyed.
- **Impact.** Unreliable/absent audit trail on review deletion; a concurrent double-delete errors instead of no-op'ing.
- **Desired future state.** Adopt the Area purge ordering + `{reviewId, title}` payload + idempotent second-purge + explicit active-link handling.
- **Closing condition.** Kernel tests assert tombstone presence, double-purge idempotency, and active-link behaviour.
- **Resolved (2026-08-05, AUDIT-FIX-03).** All five parts reproduced first against real Workers/D1: the tombstone was written with payload `{}`; its own subject row was deleted by the same batch; an ACTIVE link was silently destroyed; and two concurrent purges yielded one `{deleted:true}` plus `ReviewStorageError` ← `D1_ERROR: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed: SQLITE_CONSTRAINT`, while committing **two** tombstones for one destroyed Review. The purge is now delete-then-tombstone — `entity_links` → `activity_subjects` → `review_sections` → `review_details` → `entities` (`RETURNING`) → subject-less `review.deleted` with `{reviewId, title}` guarded on the entity DELETE's `changes()` — with the same "no active link" guard repeated on every destructive statement so the batch is all-or-nothing at commit. Active links now REFUSE the purge: `ReviewDeleteResult` gained `blockedReason: "has_links"` and `linkCount`, matching `AssetDeleteResult`; soft-deleted links do not block and are removed with the Review. Idempotency and race-safety come from the SQL guards, not from catching database errors — no `catch` suppresses a failure, and exactly one tombstone can exist per destroyed Review. **Evidence.** Source: [`app/platform/storage/d1/d1-review-repository.ts`](../../app/platform/storage/d1/d1-review-repository.ts) (`permanentlyDelete`, TEST-ONLY `deleteFault`), [`app/kernel/reviews/review.ts`](../../app/kernel/reviews/review.ts) + [`review-repository.ts`](../../app/kernel/reviews/review-repository.ts) (result type + contract), [`app/modules/reviews/routes/mutate.tsx`](../../app/modules/reviews/routes/mutate.tsx) and [`ReviewRecord.tsx`](../../app/modules/reviews/ReviewRecord.tsx) (blocked-result handling and honest danger-zone copy), [`app/modules/reviews/review-activity.ts`](../../app/modules/reviews/review-activity.ts) (payload-driven tombstone descriptor). Tests: six new real Workers/D1 cases in [`test/kernel/review.test.ts`](../../test/kernel/review.test.ts) — successful-purge tombstone with feed rendering, second-purge idempotency, a genuine two-way concurrent purge asserting neither call rejects and exactly one tombstone lands, active-link blocking then release, soft-deleted links not blocking, and fault-injected rollback at both points — plus [`test/kernel/permanent-delete-contract.test.ts`](../../test/kernel/permanent-delete-contract.test.ts).
- **Related finding.** [AUDIT-04](END_TO_END_AUDIT_2026_08_05.md#audit-04--review-permanent-delete-nondeterministicempty-tombstone-non-idempotent--p2). **Related roadmap item.** [AUDIT-FIX-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-audit-fix-03--permanent-delete-integrity-asset--review-purge-p2).

### ☑ DEBT-81 — No application-level CSRF defence — P2 — RESOLVED 2026-08-05

- **Original issue.** [AUDIT-05] No `Origin`/`Sec-Fetch-Site`/`Referer` check existed on any mutation (`app/platform/request/request-boundary.ts:61` authenticated but did not check origin); no CSRF token was minted; there is no app session cookie — auth rides the Cloudflare Access `CF_Authorization` cookie whose SameSite is set by Cloudflare and asserted nowhere. ADR-016 reasoned only about token *forgery*, not session-riding CSRF.
- **Impact.** A compromised/XSS'd sibling subdomain of `daly.id.au` is same-site and could drive authenticated mutations; a future `SameSite=None` Access config would open plain cross-site CSRF.
- **Resolved (2026-08-05, AUDIT-FIX-04).** The absence was confirmed first: nothing in the request platform read either header. One canonical policy now runs ONCE at the shared boundary, so it covers every current and future mutation route without a single per-route check. `GET`/`HEAD`/`OPTIONS` are safe; everything else — including unknown and future methods, because the safe list is an allowlist — must carry an `Origin` that matches the request URL's own origin by exact scheme + hostname + effective port. There is no suffix match, no registrable-domain comparison and no wildcard subdomain, so **`same-site` is rejected as firmly as `cross-site`**: `https://other.daly.id.au` is same-*site* with `hub.daly.id.au` and is refused. `Sec-Fetch-Site` is read as corroboration only — `same-origin` or absent is accepted alongside an exact `Origin`, anything else is a rejection, and a hostile `Origin` claiming `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` is rejected as inconsistent. **Missing `Origin` fails closed** even when `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` is present: browsers attach `Origin` to every non-`GET`/`HEAD` request and DalyHub has no non-browser mutation client, so the compatibility case was deliberately not taken. The trusted origin is `new URL(request.url).origin` — authoritative because production disables `workers_dev`/`preview_urls`, so only the Access-protected custom domain routes here; no configuration value, no secret and no forwarding header (`X-Forwarded-Host`/`X-Forwarded-Proto`) is consulted. Ordering: authenticate → establish session → check provenance → reject, so a rejected mutation never provisions membership, never invokes React Router, never touches a repository, never records Activity and never mutates data; an unauthenticated request keeps its existing 401/403/503. The rejection is a generic `403 Request rejected.` with the baseline security headers, `private, no-store`, no reflected origin, no reason code, no CORS header and no redirect. `/health` keeps its exact-path public bypass for safe methods only. Offline replay is unaffected: it posts to the ordinary create routes with a plain same-origin `fetch`, so the browser supplies the provenance, and a 403 is classified `blocked` (not retried indefinitely). No migration, no token table, no cookie, no third-party dependency.
- **Evidence.** Source: [`app/platform/request/mutation-provenance.ts`](../../app/platform/request/mutation-provenance.ts) (the pure policy), [`request-boundary.ts`](../../app/platform/request/request-boundary.ts) (ordering + public-path method restriction), [`security-headers.ts`](../../app/platform/request/security-headers.ts) (`buildCrossOriginRejectionResponse`). Tests: 47 policy cases in [`test/unit/request/mutation-provenance.test.ts`](../../test/unit/request/mutation-provenance.test.ts); the eight boundary proofs in [`test/unit/request/request-boundary.test.ts`](../../test/unit/request/request-boundary.test.ts); real-runtime/real-D1 proof that a rejected mutation leaves no Task, no Activity and no membership row in [`test/kernel/request-boundary-csrf.test.ts`](../../test/kernel/request-boundary-csrf.test.ts); a real second local origin driving a genuine browser-generated `Origin` in [`e2e/csrf.spec.ts`](../../e2e/csrf.spec.ts); replay provenance in [`test/unit/pwa/offline-sync.test.ts`](../../test/unit/pwa/offline-sync.test.ts).
- **Related finding.** [AUDIT-05](END_TO_END_AUDIT_2026_08_05.md#audit-05--no-application-level-csrf-defence--p2). **Related roadmap item.** [AUDIT-FIX-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-audit-fix-04--csrf-defence-in-depth--react-router-bump-p2p3).

### ☑ DEBT-82 — Multi-device preference lost-update; `version` never enforced — P3 — RESOLVED 2026-08-08

- **Original issue.** [AUDIT-07] `d1-app-preferences-repository.ts` `update` read the whole record, merged the caller's fields into that read, and upserted **every** column from the merged snapshot; `version = version + 1` was bookkeeping only — nothing compared it. Two devices saving different settings from reads of the same version each wrote the other's field back to its stale value, and both calls reported success. Confirmed on `main` before the fix and reproduced as the first test in the regression suite below.
- **Resolved (2026-08-08, AUDIT-FIX-06).** The write is now a **patch**, not a snapshot replacement: the statement's `DO UPDATE SET` names only the columns present in the validated patch, and its change predicate and version guard are evaluated **inside** that one statement, so nothing can be written between a check and the write. Two consequences, chosen deliberately because preferences are two different shapes of value:
  - **Independent fields merge.** A device saving `timezone` cannot touch `appearance`, so the common two-device case has no conflict to resolve and the owner is never asked about a disagreement that does not exist. This is the same per-column shape `updateTask` already used.
  - **A DERIVED value gets a real precondition.** The navigation hidden-set is read-modify-write (read the set, add an id, write the whole set) and therefore cannot merge by column. `update` accepts `options.expectedVersion`; supplying it appends `AND owner_app_preferences.version = ?` to the write, and a stale write matches zero rows and raises the new typed `AppPreferencesConflictError` instead of reporting success. **`version` is therefore no longer incremented-and-ignored** — it is the write precondition on the one path whose value is derived from the old one.
  - The Settings `toggle-navigation` action quotes the version it read and re-derives from the newer set on a conflict (bounded to 3 attempts), so the owner's toggle is never lost, never overwrites another device's toggle, and neither device is asked to resolve anything. A conflict that survives the retries answers **`409`**, never a `500`.
- **Also fixed on the way.** `parseTimezone` rejected `UTC` — `Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone')` lists canonical zones only and omits links — while the Settings picker offered it, so choosing UTC failed validation on save. The validator now falls through to the runtime probe, which is what every owner-calendar helper actually uses.
- **Evidence.** Source: [`d1-app-preferences-repository.ts`](../../app/platform/storage/d1/d1-app-preferences-repository.ts), [`app-preferences.ts`](../../app/kernel/preferences/app-preferences.ts) (`UpdateAppPreferencesOptions`), [`app-preferences-errors.ts`](../../app/kernel/preferences/app-preferences-errors.ts) (`AppPreferencesConflictError`), [`settings/routes/index.tsx`](../../app/modules/settings/routes/index.tsx) (`withPreferenceRetry`, the `409`). Tests: 10 real-D1 cases in [`test/kernel/app-preferences-concurrency.test.ts`](../../test/kernel/app-preferences-concurrency.test.ts) — two stale devices keep BOTH changes, untouched columns are byte-identical, a same-field race resolves to the later write with the version advancing once per change, a stale compare-and-set is refused with the newer data intact, version 0 means "no row yet", an unchanged write is an idempotent no-op rather than a conflict, and a concurrency token from one workspace cannot authorise a write in another.
- **Remaining limitation.** Two devices changing the SAME scalar setting still resolve to the later write. That is the only honest answer for one field with two intentions, and nothing else is lost with it; the entry does not claim otherwise.
- **Related finding.** [AUDIT-07](END_TO_END_AUDIT_2026_08_05.md#audit-07--multi-device-preference-lost-update--p3). **Related roadmap item.** [AUDIT-FIX-06](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-audit-fix-06--concurrency-and-one-owner-day-p3--delivered-2026-08-08).

### ☑ DEBT-83 — Concurrent note-content saves are blind last-write-wins — P3 — RESOLVED 2026-08-08

- **Original issue.** [AUDIT-08] `d1-note-details-repository.ts` overwrote the whole content guarded only against *identical* content; there was no base-version precondition, so two tabs or devices editing one note silently lost one side's writing. Extends [DEBT-47](#-debt-47--an-open-autosave-editor-does-not-adopt-a-server-side-change-to-its-field--p2--resolved-2026-08-20) from "does not adopt a change" to "destroys one". Offline note *editing* is not shipped (PWA-02 deferred), so the trigger was concurrent online editing.
- **Resolved (2026-08-08, AUDIT-FIX-06).** `NoteDetailsRepository.update` accepts `options.expectedContentUpdatedAt` — the content version the editor loaded — and folds it into the SAME upsert as a compare-and-set, so the check cannot be raced. A stale save matches zero rows and is reported as the typed `NoteDetailsConflictError`; the route answers **`409`** carrying the newer stored text, never a `500` and never a false success. `null` is a distinct quoted value meaning "this note had no saved content when I opened it", guarded as "the stored content is still empty" so a `setTags`/`setArchived` row creation cannot manufacture a false conflict. Callers that quote nothing (the capture panel writing a brand-new note's first body) keep the previous behaviour exactly, but a caller that quotes an UNPARSEABLE value is refused with `400` and writes nothing — degrading that to "no precondition" would have left a stale client an opt-out from the compare-and-set, and refusing costs the owner nothing because their draft never left the editor.
- **The editor's answer reuses the ONE existing reconciliation UI.** No Notes-only dialog and no automatic Markdown merge. A refusal is fed into the shared DS-06 coordinator through a new, honest third save outcome — `{ outcome: "conflict" }`, which is neither success (nothing was written) nor error (nothing malfunctioned) — so the draft stays in the editor, the status returns to `unsaved` rather than `error`, and the newer server text is OFFERED through the same [`RemoteChangeBanner`](../../app/shared/forms/RemoteChangeBanner.tsx) an out-of-band change already uses: *load the newer version*, or *keep mine*. The quoted base version is held until the owner answers, so a stray blur cannot quietly win in the meantime — and while the banner is up, a blur does not attempt a save that is certain to be refused.
- **Evidence.** Source: [`d1-note-details-repository.ts`](../../app/platform/storage/d1/d1-note-details-repository.ts), [`note-details.ts`](../../app/kernel/notes/note-details.ts) (`UpdateNoteContentOptions`), [`notes/routes/mutate.tsx`](../../app/modules/notes/routes/mutate.tsx) (the `409`), [`autosave.ts`](../../app/shared/forms/autosave.ts) (`conflicted`), [`NoteContentForm.tsx`](../../app/modules/notes/NoteContentForm.tsx). Tests: 9 real-D1 repository + route cases in [`test/kernel/note-content-concurrency.test.ts`](../../test/kernel/note-content-concurrency.test.ts); 7 editor cases in [`test/unit/notes/NoteContentForm.test.tsx`](../../test/unit/notes/NoteContentForm.test.tsx); and a genuine two-writer browser journey in [`e2e/notes.spec.ts`](../../e2e/notes.spec.ts) where a second same-origin writer saves the note mid-edit — the banner appears, both versions survive, and reload-then-save recovers.
- **Remaining limitation.** Deliberately no revision history, no CRDT and no automatic prose merge: the owner chooses between two whole versions. Recovering the discarded side after choosing "load the newer version" is not offered — the draft is shown before the choice, never destroyed behind it.
- **Closing condition (met).** Kernel tests assert a stale content save is refused, not silently applied, and that the newer stored content is intact afterwards.
- **Related finding.** [AUDIT-08](END_TO_END_AUDIT_2026_08_05.md#audit-08--concurrent-note-content-saves-are-blind-last-write-wins--p3). **Related roadmap item.** [AUDIT-FIX-06](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-audit-fix-06--concurrency-and-one-owner-day-p3--delivered-2026-08-08); [DEBT-47](#-debt-47--an-open-autosave-editor-does-not-adopt-a-server-side-change-to-its-field--p2--resolved-2026-08-20).
- **The Review section path was fixed first (2026-08-05) and is the precedent this copied.** `ReviewRepository.updateSection` was blind last-write-wins in exactly the same way. [REVIEW-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-review-02--weekly-review--delivered-2026-08-05) added an optional `expectedUpdatedAt` precondition: quoting it turns the write into a compare-and-set, a stale save raises `ReviewConflictError`, the route answers `409` with the newer text, and the owner's own words stay in the editor. A kernel test asserts a stale save is refused and the newer text survives; callers that quote no base version keep the previous behaviour, so nothing existing changed. Notes now follow the same shape, with two additions the Review path did not need: the base version is held until the owner answers, and the refusal is routed into the shared reconciliation banner rather than shown as a save error.

> deployment (`cf596658-d648-4a58-a521-09cf6c0e279f`, deployed
> 2026-08-30T05:56:35Z), Worker secrets (seven, by name only) and D1 migrations
> (nothing unapplied) all pass. Two of the three things this entry named as
> unknown — the **secret names** and the **deployment identity** — are therefore
> answered.
>
> **Application health remained SKIPPED, and this entry closes saying so rather
> than around it.** `https://hub.daly.id.au/health` answered **302** to the
> Cloudflare Access login. That is the intended hardening, and it is the finding
> this entry itself established in 2026-08-11 — but Access terminates at the edge
> before the origin, so **the RUNNING RELEASE VERSION is still not independently
> confirmed**, and nothing here claims it is. No attempt was made to bypass
> Access; a `PASS` would need `PRODUCTION_ACCESS_SERVICE_TOKEN_ID` / `_SECRET`,
> or an owner reading `/about` while signed in.
>
> **Why that does not hold the entry open.** The closing condition names the act
> — *an owner runs the verifier with credentials and records the result* — not a
> `VERIFIED` verdict, and deliberately so: the script's own contract is that
> `SKIPPED` *"is never a pass"* and is reported as itself. A `PARTIALLY VERIFIED`
> recorded honestly **is** production state stated with evidence. The one
> remaining unknown is carried forward as the running-release clause of
> [V2.4-GATE-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-v24-gate-01--recoverable-green-released)
> criterion 6, where it belongs, rather than kept here as a second home for it.
>
> **The measurement also produced a correction worth carrying.** `.production.env`
> does not export `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, which `verify-production.mjs` lists as
> required, and the script spawns bare `wrangler`, which is not on the global
> PATH — so the verifier under-reports by default on a fresh owner machine.
> Recorded in the checklist beside the output.

- **Current issue, as raised.** [AUDIT-06 / AUDIT-09] `README.md` says "Current release … `2.0.1` … used daily" while `docs/development/DEPLOYMENT.md` in places reads "Next: the V2.0.1 hotfix" and fixes production at the `0001`–`0025` schema; migration-count prose drifts across `0025`/`0027`/`0028`; migrations `0026`–`0028` are not recorded as applied to production; AUDIT-IDENTITY-01 is "RESOLVED 2026-08-04" in this register but "carried forward as outstanding" in `ROADMAP_V2.md`'s closure log; and `help-content.ts` says "choose from the five [themes]" while seven ship.
- **Corrected 2026-08-11 by [AUDIT-FIX-05](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-audit-fix-05--documentation-truth-pass-p2p3--delivered-2026-08-11), inside HARDEN-01.** Every contradiction above is fixed, and the drift got worse before it was caught: by 2026-08-11 `DEPLOYMENT.md` stated the migration head as `0027` in one place and `0035` in another while the committed sequence had reached `0038`. It now states no number at all, because a repository cannot know what a database has applied — `pnpm run db:production:list` is the only honest answer, and the document says so. Help no longer claims "There is no AI in DalyHub yet" one topic below its own AI section, nor offers a choice of five themes in a product that has had no theme feature since M3-01.
- **One finding was worse than documentation drift.** Every document, the audit's own §19 checklist and `scripts/deploy-production.mjs` all asserted that `/health` is public and that a Cloudflare Access redirect from it is a misconfiguration. Measured on 2026-08-11 from an unauthenticated network, `GET https://hub.daly.id.au/health` returns **302 to the Access login** — because Access protects the whole hostname, which is precisely the origin hardening the deployment documentation exists to enforce. The deploy's post-upload health assertion therefore **could not have passed on any successful deployment**. It now distinguishes "the application answered and reports this release" from "Access answered, so the release is not verified from here" from "this is a real failure".
- **What is NOT closed, and why this entry is ◐ rather than ☑.** The closing condition has two halves: "no two canonical docs disagree" is met; **"production state is stated with evidence" is not.** No production verification was performed, because the implementation environment holds no Cloudflare credentials. The applied migration set, the Worker's secret names and the running release are all unknown. `pnpm run verify:production` performs the whole check in one read-only command and reports `SKIPPED` — never a pass — for anything it cannot reach.
- **Impact.** The documentation half cost real time: `scripts/deploy-production.mjs` and every deployment document asserted `/health` was public and that an Access redirect from it was a misconfiguration, and it is not — a claim that would have sent an operator hunting a configuration fault that does not exist. That half is fixed. What is left costs credibility rather than time: the repository still cannot say what is deployed, only what it believes is deployed.
- **Desired future state.** One canonical statement of production's release, schema head and health-endpoint behaviour, produced by RUNNING `verify:production` rather than by writing it down — so the documents quote a measurement and drift becomes impossible rather than merely discouraged.
- **Why it remains open.** **Owner-blocked, on exactly one thing.** `verify:production` needs Cloudflare credentials; `wrangler whoami` in every implementation environment to date reports not authenticated, and no `.production.env` exists. This is the same blocker as [DEBT-139](#-debt-139--migration-0042-has-not-been-applied-and-no-production-backup-has-been-taken--p1--two-of-three-clauses-met-2026-08-30-one-owner-ui-check-remains) and [DEBT-198](#-debt-198--the-off-cloudflare-encrypted-backup-has-never-been-produced-because-the-github-production-environment-holds-no-secrets--p2), and the repository side is ready: the script exists, the checklist names it, and nothing else is owed here.
- **Closing condition (unchanged).** No two canonical docs disagree about production state; production state is stated with evidence — i.e. an owner has run `pnpm run verify:production` with credentials and recorded the result.
- **V2.4 disposition — ADVANCED.** [V2.4-GATE-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-v24-gate-01--recoverable-green-released) requires `pnpm run verify:production` to be run **with credentials** and its output recorded in a release checklist, which is this entry's one unmet half. It closes if that happens; it stays ◐ if the credentials are not available to whoever takes the item, and saying so is the honest outcome rather than a pass.
- **It STAYS ◐, which is the branch above taken (V2.4-GATE-01, 2026-08-23).** The credentials were not available. `pnpm run verify:production` was run at this commit and reports **PARTIALLY VERIFIED** with five `SKIPPED` checks — its own honest answer to having none — recorded verbatim in [`RELEASE_CHECKLIST_V2_4_0.md`](../release/RELEASE_CHECKLIST_V2_4_0.md) and in [the implementation record § 4.3](V2_4_GATE_01_RECOVERABLE_GREEN_RELEASED_2026_08.md), without account ids, tokens or secrets.
  - `hub.daly.id.au/health` answered **302** to the Cloudflare Access login. That is the intended hardening rather than an outage, and the verifier says so in its own words — but it also means **the running release is NOT confirmed**, and this document does not guess at it.
  - **The half this entry is really about is met and stays met:** no two canonical documents disagree about production state, because none of them claims to know it. `DEPLOYMENT.md` still states no migration number of its own. The unmet half is the same one it has always been — an owner running the verifier with credentials.
- **ADVANCED substantially, and it STILL stays ◐ (V2.4-GATE-01 operational pass, 2026-08-24).** The half this entry has been open on since AUDIT-06 — *"production state is stated with evidence"* — is, for the first time, **partly satisfied by an actual reading of production** rather than by a refusal to guess.
  - **What is now stated with evidence.** Production's `d1_migrations` ledger reports **49 applied migrations, `0001`–`0047`, an exact set match with the committed sequence — nothing pending and nothing orphaned** — with `0047` applied 2026-08-20 09:32:44; the database holds **52 tables** and is ~1.73 MB. The production Worker `dalyhub-v2-production` and the production database `dalyhub-v2` both exist, as do BACKUP-01's `dalyhub-v2-backup` Worker and its private `dalyhub-v2-backups` R2 bucket. Recorded in [`RELEASE_CHECKLIST_V2_4_0.md` § 6](../release/RELEASE_CHECKLIST_V2_4_0.md), with no account id, database id, token or secret written down.
  - **Why that is not enough to close it.** This entry's closing condition names a specific act: *"an owner has run `pnpm run verify:production` **with credentials** and recorded the result"*. That did not happen. `verify:production` was run at this commit and reports **PARTIALLY VERIFIED** with the same five `[SKIPPED]` checks — Configuration, Worker deployment, Worker secrets, D1 migrations, Application health — because `wrangler whoami` still reports not authenticated. The migration reading above came from an owner-authorised Cloudflare API connection — **write-capable, used read-only** — not from the verifier and not from `db:production:list`, so it settles the *fact* without satisfying the *condition*.
  - **Three things this entry wanted that are still unknown.** The Worker's **secret names**, the **deployment identity** of what is live, and the **running release version** — `/about` and `/health` both render `APP_VERSION`, and both sit behind Cloudflare Access, which answered **302** to an unauthenticated probe. Access terminates at the edge before the origin, so that redirect identifies no release and establishes nothing about the Worker behind it. This entry does not guess at it.
  - **The "no two canonical docs disagree" half remains met.** [`DEPLOYMENT.md`](../development/DEPLOYMENT.md) still states **no migration number of its own**, and nothing in this update changes that — the measurement above is recorded as a dated observation in a release checklist, which is where evidence gathered with credentials belongs, rather than as a number a repository claims to know.
- **Related finding.** [AUDIT-06](END_TO_END_AUDIT_2026_08_05.md#audit-06--production-state-documentation-drift-production-unverifiable-here--p2), [AUDIT-09](END_TO_END_AUDIT_2026_08_05.md#audit-09--help-contradicts-the-shipped-theme-count--p3). **Related roadmap item.** [AUDIT-FIX-05](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-audit-fix-05--documentation-truth-pass-p2p3--delivered-2026-08-11). **Record.** [HARDEN-01](HARDEN_01_RELEASE_RELIABILITY_2026_08.md).

### ☑ DEBT-85 — CSP has no `script-src`/`default-src` — P3 — RESOLVED 2026-08-08

> **This entry was SPLIT on 2026-08-08.** It originally carried two unrelated
> audit findings, AUDIT-10 (CSP) and AUDIT-11 (the plaintext production dump).
> AUDIT-11 is resolved and now has its own entry,
> [DEBT-105](#-debt-105--the-scheduled-production-backup-uploaded-a-plaintext-copy-of-the-whole-database--p2p3--resolved-2026-08-08),
> so it can be marked closed without implying the CSP work is done. **The CSP
> concern below remains outstanding.**

- **Original issue.** [AUDIT-10] `app/platform/request/security-headers.ts` set only `base-uri`/`frame-ancestors`/`object-src` — no `script-src`/`default-src`, so the Markdown sanitiser was the sole script-injection defence with no second layer.
- **Impact before resolution.** No defence-in-depth if an XSS sink were ever introduced.
- **Resolved (2026-08-08, with SET-03).** A complete, ENFORCING policy is built per response around a fresh 128-bit nonce, in one place — [`content-security-policy.ts`](../../app/platform/request/content-security-policy.ts) — and applied by the request boundary to every exit: served documents, data requests, the public `/health` path, 403 CSRF rejections and 401/403/503 authentication failures alike. Production carries `default-src 'self'`, `script-src 'self' 'nonce-…'` with **no** `'unsafe-inline'` and **no** `'unsafe-eval'`, `object-src 'none'`, `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `frame-src 'none'`, `base-uri 'none'`, `form-action 'self'`, `worker-src 'self'`, `manifest-src 'self'`, `connect-src 'self'`, `font-src 'self'`, `img-src 'self' data: https:` and `style-src 'self' 'nonce-…'`. The nonce reaches the render through the typed request context, so the header and the document can never name different values.
- **The one exception, stated.** `style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'`, for React `style={{…}}` attributes. Confined to attributes, so an injected `<style>` ELEMENT is still refused; a style attribute cannot execute script. CodeMirror's runtime `<style>` injection is *nonced* through `EditorView.cspNonce` rather than exempted.
- **Development is separate and gated at BUILD time.** `resolveCspMode` returns the relaxed Vite policy only when `import.meta.env.DEV` (false in every production bundle) and an explicit development/test `ENVIRONMENT` agree, so a deployed bundle cannot be argued into it by an environment variable, header or hostname.
- **Proved, not asserted.** `test/unit/request/content-security-policy.test.ts` asserts each invariant individually (never a snapshot of the whole string). `test/unit/request/request-boundary.test.ts` proves the header's nonce is the one the render received, that it differs per request, and that rejection and failure responses carry the same policy. `e2e/csp.spec.ts` reads the header off the real production build and then, in a browser on the production origin, proves that policy blocks an injected inline `<script>`, an inline `onclick`, an unexpected external script source and a `javascript:` URL — while a nonced script still runs, so the suite cannot pass by blocking everything. The Markdown sanitiser is untouched and still strips all four first; CSP is the second, independent layer.
- **Related finding.** [AUDIT-10](END_TO_END_AUDIT_2026_08_05.md#audit-10--csp-has-no-script-srcdefault-src--p3--resolved-2026-08-08). **Related ADR.** [ADR-082](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-082-a-nonce-based-content-security-policy-one-header-authority-and-a-security-surface-that-refuses-to-overclaim). **Related roadmap item.** [SET-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-set-03--account--security--substantially-delivered-2026-08-08).

### ☑ DEBT-105 — The scheduled production backup uploaded a plaintext copy of the whole database — P2/P3 — RESOLVED 2026-08-08

- **Original issue.** [AUDIT-11] `.github/workflows/production-backup.yml` exported the entire production database daily to a GitHub Actions artifact as a plain `.sql` file with 30-day retention. Credentials were handled correctly and that was never the finding: the dump is all personal data — People and their contact details, Diary entries, Meeting notes, Reviews, archived and soft-deleted records — and its exposure scaled with who could read the repository's Actions. Raised as half of DEBT-85; split out on resolution so the CSP work stayed independently traceable — it has since been resolved too, by SET-03.
- **Resolved (2026-08-08, with SET-02).** The dump is now encrypted **on the runner, before it becomes an artifact**, with GnuPG symmetric AES-256 and explicitly stated S2K parameters (`--s2k-mode 3`, `--s2k-digest-algo SHA512`, `--s2k-count 65011712`). One pipeline, `scripts/production-backup.mjs`, serves the scheduled and the manually dispatched run identically — there is no weaker manual path.
- **What GitHub now stores.** `dalyhub-v2-production-<stamp>.sql.gpg` and a `metadata.json` of sizes, SHA-256 digests, run identity and the decrypt command. **No plaintext dump. No key.** The plaintext exists only in a scratch directory removed by a trap that runs even on failure, and a guard step refuses the upload if the artifact directory contains anything unencrypted or the metadata names a credential-shaped field.
- **The key.** `BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_PASSPHRASE`, in the protected `production` GitHub environment. It is read from a file written under `umask 077`, never from `argv` and never interpolated into a shell string; shell tracing is never enabled and no log line carries backup contents. It is not committed, not documented, not uploaded and not printed. The owner holds a copy **off GitHub**; rotation, and what happens to older backups, are documented in [`BACKUP_AND_RESTORE.md` §6](../development/BACKUP_AND_RESTORE.md#6-the-recovery-key).
- **Recoverability is proved, not asserted.** Every run decrypts its own artifact back, compares SHA-256 with the original and asserts the plaintext does not appear in the ciphertext. `test/unit/deploy/production-backup-encryption.test.ts` does the same end to end with a real dump, a throwaway key and the real `gpg` invocation: encrypt → prove the sensitive strings are absent → decrypt → byte-identical → still passes structural validation; a wrong key fails; a tampered ciphertext fails. `test/unit/deploy/production-backup-workflow.test.ts` holds the workflow contract — upload contents, cleanup, no secret on a command line, the pre-export key guard, minimal permissions, `schedule`/`workflow_dispatch` only (no pull request can run it), and the deliberate retention.
- **Retention.** Unchanged at 30 days, and the reasoning is recorded beside the value: it was not reduced (encryption addressed the exposure) and not extended (encryption is not a reason to keep more data on GitHub for longer).
- **Related finding.** [AUDIT-11](END_TO_END_AUDIT_2026_08_05.md#audit-11--production-d1-dump-stored-as-a-github-artifact--p2p3--resolved-2026-08-08). **Related roadmap item.** [SET-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-set-02--backup--restore-v21--delivered-2026-08-08).

### ☑ DEBT-86 — `react-router@8.0.0` carries a published advisory — P3 — RESOLVED 2026-08-05

- **Original issue.** [AUDIT-12] `pnpm audit --prod` flagged `react-router` `8.0.0` (GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2, "RSC Mode CSRF Bypass", `>=7.12.0 <8.3.0`, patched `8.3.0`). DalyHub runs framework mode (not RSC), so the specific exploit likely did not apply, but it sat on a **direct production dependency** and paired with the CSRF gap (DEBT-81).
- **Resolved (2026-08-05, AUDIT-FIX-04).** `react-router` and `@react-router/dev` were bumped **together**, `8.0.0` → `8.3.0`, keeping the repository's exact-version pinning (`pnpm add --save-exact`); `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` are the only dependency changes, and no unrelated package moved. `pnpm why` resolves ONE version of each — `react-router@8.3.0` (direct dependency, plus via `@react-router/dev@8.3.0` → `@react-router/node@8.3.0`) and `@react-router/dev@8.3.0`. **`pnpm audit --prod` → "No known vulnerabilities found"**, and GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 no longer appears anywhere in `pnpm audit --json`.
- **Advisory scope, stated accurately.** The official advisory scopes the flaw to the **unstable RSC code paths** ("Framework mode is not affected"): a follow-up to CVE-2026-22030 where action execution could occur before a 400 response. A codebase search found **no unstable RSC entry point or API in DalyHub** — no `react-router/unstable_rsc*`, no `unstable_rsc/*` virtual module, no `@vitejs/plugin-rsc`; the only `renderToReadableStream` is the ordinary framework-mode SSR entry from `react-dom/server` in `app/entry.server.tsx`. This entry therefore does **not** claim DalyHub was exploited, and does not claim the advisory applies to ordinary non-RSC actions. The upgrade was still required: the advisory sat on a direct production dependency, and removing it prevents future exposure if RSC APIs are ever adopted.
- **8.3.0 compatibility reviewed** (changelog, not just the advisory). The behavioural change of note is path-parameter encoding in `href`/`generatePath`, which now follows RFC 3986 path-segment rules so `$ & + , ; = : @` stay literal. DalyHub uses **neither** `href()` nor `generatePath()` from React Router (the one local `href` in `CollectionFilterChips.tsx` builds a query string), and every route parameter is an entity id — `crypto.randomUUID()`, hex and hyphens only. The changed encoding is therefore unreachable from DalyHub's route contract, so no speculative regression test was added; the existing navigation and deep-link coverage was run instead and is green.
- **Remaining advisories, recorded honestly.** Full `pnpm audit` (including dev dependencies) still reports **11 advisories — 6 high, 5 moderate — all dev-only and transitive**: `brace-expansion` (via `eslint` and `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` → `minimatch`), `sharp` and `undici` (via `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` → `miniflare`), and `postcss` (via `vite`). None is a production dependency; none was upgraded here, because unrelated dependency upgrades are out of this item's scope. `pnpm audit` is **not** clean, and this entry does not claim it is — only `pnpm audit --prod` is.
- **Related finding.** [AUDIT-12](END_TO_END_AUDIT_2026_08_05.md#audit-12--react-router-800-dependency-advisory--p3). **Related roadmap item.** [AUDIT-FIX-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-audit-fix-04--csrf-defence-in-depth--react-router-bump-p2p3).

### ☑ DEBT-87 — Non-atomic cross-repository flows can leave inconsistent state — P3 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-08**

- **Original issue.** [AUDIT-13] Meeting item→task conversion (`app/platform/meetings/follow-up-operations.ts`) and obligation→task completion (`d1-asset-history-repository.ts`, task completed in a separate transaction *before* the obligation batch) span two writes; a mid-way failure leaves an orphan Task, or a completed Task against a still-open obligation. Documented in the code, untested.
- **Resolved (2026-08-08, AUDIT-FIX-07).** Both are now ONE `D1Database.batch()`.
  - **Meeting item → Task** was five transactions with a compensating `spine.softDelete`. The compensation covered a *thrown* failure and could not cover the process not being there to run it, which is exactly the orphan the finding described. The conversion is now one transaction assembled from the Task, Meeting and EntityLink adapters' OWN prepared statements — no repository's SQL is re-authored — behind ONE domain operation, `MeetingTaskConversionRepository.convert`. A failure now leaves **no row at all**, not a soft-deleted one, so a retry is a first attempt. Idempotency is the `meeting_item_tasks (workspace_id, item_id)` unique index: a losing concurrent conversion rolls its whole transaction back and returns the winner's Task.
  - **Obligation → Task completion** closed the Task first.
