It also fails when a partition is budgeted past a ceiling **derived** from `globalTimeout` (`25 min × 0.75 ÷ 1.12`, the last figure being the measured wall-clock cost of a second of test time — 1.114 overall and 1.094–1.131 per partition across all twelve of run `32333645709`) rather than the flat *"under 20 minutes"* the p05 that could not finish satisfied at 19.4 min. Ten partitions became twelve so the heaviest sits at **15.2 min**, 68% of the ceiling, against the 87% it was at.
  4. **The gate finishes, and the re-derived manifest predicts it.** Run [`32338241602`](https://github.com/acedaly/DalyHub-V2/actions/runs/32338241602), the first with the committed manifest, collected **1847 tests, executed 1847, failed 0** — **CI Gate green** — across twelve partitions that all started and all finished, the worst at 76% of `globalTimeout`. Against `main`'s 33 unexecuted tests in one partition, that is the outage this entry became. The manifest predicted that run's total to within **0.9%** (175.1 min budgeted, 173.6 min measured), where the previous run's mixed-source manifest was 6% out, and the wall-clock overhead factor came back at **1.113** against 1.114 on the run before — two independent twelve-partition samples agreeing to 0.1%.
- **What is still outstanding, and why the entry is ◐ rather than ☑.** The word **`main`**. Every clause of the closing condition is now met on a PULL-REQUEST run, twice over, but the entry says `main` and that is not a formality: `main` is what gates the branch, and the manifest has never been exercised there.
  - **And the condition's last clause needs restating, because as written it cannot be met.** It asks for *"a `worst/mean` the next run's elapsed times actually agree with"*, and those are two different quantities: the committed **budget** spread is worst/mean **1.04**, while the **elapsed** spread on run `32338241602` was **1.13**, because per-partition wall-clock overhead ranged 1.093–1.134 and runner speed varies on top of it. They were never going to be equal. What the clause was reaching for — and what should be checked instead — is that the AGGREGATE prediction holds and no partition approaches the ceiling. Both are now measurable: 0.9% of aggregate error, and a worst partition at 76%.
  - **Close this entry when** a run on `main` is green with the committed manifest, every partition executes every test it collected, the aggregate budget is within a few percent of the measured total, and no partition exceeds ~80% of `globalTimeout`. **Not before**, and not on a single sample: this entry exists because measurements decay quietly, and closing it on one run would be the same mistake in a smaller font.
- **V2.4 disposition — ADVANCED.** [V2.4-GATE-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-v24-gate-01--recoverable-green-released) produces the green run this entry is held open for. It is not re-opened and its mechanism is not re-litigated.
- **ADVANCED, and it STAYS ◐ (V2.4-GATE-01, 2026-08-23).** The mechanism is now exercised in the one condition it had never been exercised in: a **fully green** run.

### ☑ DEBT-158 — A Goal measurement journey has never once run, because nothing in the seed is measurable — P2 — RESOLVED 2026-08-23 (V2.4-GATE-01)

- **It executes.** `test.skip()` is gone, and the journey owns its own measurable Goal through [`e2e/goal-fixtures.ts`](../../e2e/goal-fixtures.ts) — which PR #222 had written and left unwired, so this consumes it rather than adding a second copy — creating a Goal with unit `km`, baseline `10` and target `100`, and cleaning it up in `afterEach`. **The global product seed was not changed**, which is what this entry asked for: nothing any other spec sees is different.
- **Verified as EXECUTED, not merely as passing.** Green run [`32605964327`](https://github.com/acedaly/DalyHub-V2/actions/runs/32605964327), read from the `e2e-results-*` artefacts: the three tests still reported `skipped` across the whole gate are the three [DEBT-200](#-debt-200--three-more-e2e-journeys-report-green-by-never-running-for-the-same-reason-debt-158-did--p2--resolved-2026-08-25) records, and this journey is not among them. A green test that silently avoids its scenario would be indistinguishable from this one in a log; it is distinguishable in the artefact.
- **What it now asserts, in order.** A measurable Goal exists and the test created it; the collection row carries **no** progressbar yet — a measurable Goal with a baseline and no readings is *"not measured yet"*, which `goal-measurement.spec` states in as many words, so the bar's arrival is a real before/after rather than a presence check; the row selects the Goal into `goal-workspace-pane` as URL state (REDESIGN-04 §11), where the starting value reads `10`; a reading of `42.5` is recorded; the trio's text changes and `aria-valuenow` exceeds 0; a reload preserves it; and the collection row **now** carries a progressbar.
- **One correction the first attempt earned.** It drove the journey from the canonical record URL, which draws no `goal-workspace-pane` at all, and it asserted a progressbar *before* any reading — which a correct product refuses to draw. Both were the test being wrong about the product rather than the reverse.
- **Closing condition met** in full: the test executes with no skip path taken, records a reading, asserts the trio and the chart moved, and its partition (p03) is green with every sibling spec unaffected.

- **Current issue.** [`e2e/spine-workspaces.spec.ts`](../../e2e/spine-workspaces.spec.ts) — *"records a measurement from the workspace and updates the trio and the chart"* — opens `/goals`, looks for a Goal row carrying a `progressbar`, and calls `test.skip()` when it finds none. MEASURED on the E2E database: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM goal_details WHERE target_value IS NOT NULL` is **0**, so it finds none, every time. The skip is reported by CI as *"1 skipped"* beside the passes.
- **Why it is written that way, and why that reasoning is still right.** The test deliberately drives whichever Goal the workspace is genuinely measuring rather than a fixture id, because the E2E seed and the design fixture are different databases and a journey pinned to one silently stops running against the other. The guard is sound; what is missing is the fixture that would satisfy it.
- **Impact.** REDESIGN-04's measurement journey — record a reading, the trio and the chart move together — has no end-to-end coverage at all, and the gate reports green while it never executes. That is exactly the "green claims are unverifiable" shape [DEBT-41](#-debt-41--the-e2e-suite-is-unreliable-on-main-so-ci-is-green-claims-are-unverifiable--p1--resolved-2026-08-02) was raised for, at one journey's scale.
- **Why it was not fixed here.** Making it run means giving the SHARED seed a measurable Goal, and that seed is read by Today, analytics, the Review evidence and the Goals collection. Introducing a new measurable Goal — and then a measurement written into it by every run of this journey — is a fixture change with a blast radius across partitions, which is not a change to make in the same pass that is trying to establish that the ten partitions are green.
- **Desired future state.** The journey owns its own measurable Goal — created and cleaned up by the spec, in the manner of `e2e/habits-fixtures.ts` — so it runs on every gate without widening what any other spec sees.
- **Closing condition.** The test executes (no `test.skip` path taken) on a full gate run, records a reading, and asserts the trio and the chart moved; the specs sharing its partition are unaffected.
- **V2.4 disposition — TAKEN.** [V2.4-GATE-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-v24-gate-01--recoverable-green-released), because a journey that reports green by never executing is the same class of problem as a gate that reports red for reasons nobody has classified. The fix is the one this entry already names — the spec owns its own measurable Goal, in the manner of `e2e/habits-fixtures.ts` — so that [FOLLOW-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-follow-02--did-the-goals-move--delivered-2026-08-27) can change the Goals surfaces against coverage that runs.
- **Related roadmap item.** [V2.3-GATE-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_3.md#-v23-gate-01--a-trustworthy-v23-baseline--delivered-2026-08-18); REDESIGN-04; [V2.4-GATE-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-v24-gate-01--recoverable-green-released), which closed it.

### ☐ DEBT-159 — Removing two filter chips in quick succession can put one of them back — P3

- **Current issue.** V2.3-GATE-01 fixed the lost update in the live-applying collection CONTROLS: every write now leaves through one function that records what it wrote, so a second choice composes over the first rather than over the committed state the loader has not yet replaced ([`app/shared/collection-layout/use-applied-params.ts`](../../app/shared/collection-layout/use-applied-params.ts)). The chip row is not on that path. Each chip's remove control is an ordinary `<Link>` whose `to` is computed at RENDER time from the applied parameters, so removing chip A and then chip B inside one loader round trip navigates to a URL B computed while A was still applied — and A comes back.
- **Why the chips are links, and why that should not change.** `CollectionFilterChips` states it in its own contract: *"the chips are ordinary links, so they are keyboard-operable, middle-clickable and Back/Forward-correct — the URL is the state."* Routing their removals through the controls' imperative writer would buy this narrow race at the cost of a real, shareable, middle-clickable link, which is a worse trade.
- **Impact.** Narrow and real. The window is one collection revalidation, and both clicks must land inside it on two DIFFERENT chips; a single removal, and a removal after the collection has settled, are both correct. Mitigated in one direction already: the chips now render from the same applied-parameter authority the controls write, so a removal made immediately after APPLYING a filter is correct where it previously was not.
- **Desired future state.** The chip's href is derived from the same in-flight authority the controls use — e.g. the row re-rendering with a pending base while a removal is loading — so the link stays a link and still composes.
- **New evidence, and it widens the entry (HARDEN-06A, 2026-08-20).** The sentence above says a removal made immediately after APPLYING a filter is correct. On a slow machine it is not. `e2e/tasks-collection.spec.ts:298` — *"removes one of two applied filters and leaves the other"*, which removes exactly ONE chip — fails **4 times out of 4, from a freshly migrated and seeded local D1, in isolation** on the HARDEN-06A sandbox: removing the `Priority: P1` chip lands on `/tasks?group=due_state`, with **neither** filter left. The same test passes on CI (run [`32333645709`](https://github.com/acedaly/DalyHub-V2/actions/runs/32333645709), partition p02, 173 of 173 executed), so it is environment-dependent rather than intermittent, and the window is the collection's own commit rather than a first removal. Nothing was changed for it here: HARDEN-06A touched only the `Today integration` block of that file, the failing test's code path is byte-identical to `main`, and filter behaviour is outside that slice. Recorded rather than fixed, and the entry's *"mitigated in one direction already"* claim should be read as unproven until it is.
- **Closing condition.** A test in the shape of `e2e/tasks-collection.spec.ts`'s *"combines two filters chosen before the first has finished loading"* — two chip removals with the first revalidation held open — leaves both dimensions removed and neither restored. **And** the single-removal case above passes on a machine slow enough to open the window.
- **ADVANCED, and the evidence above is REATTRIBUTED (V2.4-GATE-01, 2026-08-23).** The "new evidence" paragraph is sound about what it observed and wrong about where it came from. `tasks-collection.spec.ts:298` reproduces on this sandbox exactly as described — `/tasks?group=due_state`, neither filter left — but the loss happens **before any chip is clicked**. The trace shows only two loader requests, and the second has already dropped the first filter:

  ```
  choose Priority = P1  → GET /tasks.data?group=due_state&priority=p1
  choose Due = Overdue  → GET /tasks.data?group=due_state&due=overdue
  ```

  That is the *controls'* lost update, not the chip row's. The single-removal half of this entry was never a chip defect; the end URL was simply consistent with both stories, and the entry picked the one it was about.
- **That half is FIXED, at a different seam than this entry supposed.** `useAppliedParams` computed `applied` during render while `record` deliberately wrote a ref, so between a choice and the render reflecting it nothing had re-rendered and `commit`/`write` were composing over the `searchParams` captured at the last render. The hook now also exposes `current()` — the same precedence asked at event time — and both writers use it. A unit test drives both clicks inside one `act` (no render between) and **fails without the fix**; `fireEvent` cannot reproduce the window, which is why the covering test that existed could not.
- **What remains OPEN, and it is the entry's real subject.** Removing chip A and then chip B inside one revalidation. The chips are ordinary `<Link>`s whose destination is fixed at render, `current()` does not reach them, and the contract that they stay real links should not be traded away. The first bullet of the closing condition is untouched; the second is now met.
- **DIRECT confirmation of the render-time lag, from a trace (2026-08-23).** This entry's central claim — *"each chip's remove control is an ordinary `<Link>` whose `to` is computed at RENDER time from the applied parameters"* — is now observed rather than reasoned. On CI run [`32610240298`](https://github.com/acedaly/DalyHub-V2/actions/runs/32610240298) the DOM snapshot at the moment of the click reads:

  ```
  page URL : /tasks?group=due_state&priority=p1&due=overdue
  chip href: /tasks?group=due_state            ← composed before `due=overdue` existed
  ```

  A later snapshot of the same page carries the corrected `/tasks?group=due_state&due=overdue`. So the lag is real, it is one render wide, and following the stale destination would remove both filters — which is this entry, exactly, in the single-removal direction.
- **A THIRD thing, which is neither this entry nor the controls.** In the same trace the click produced **no navigation at all** — no `.data` request, URL unchanged — because the journey clicked the chip with the controls popover still open. `AnchoredSurface` dismisses on a capture-phase `pointerdown` and returns focus to the trigger, so the page can move between `pointerdown` and `pointerup` and the `click` never reaches the link. That is a test reaching across an open floating surface, fixed by putting the controls away first (`dismiss()` in `e2e/helpers.ts`), and it is recorded here only so a future reader does not mistake it for this entry's mechanism.
- **Related roadmap item.** [V2.3-GATE-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_3.md#-v23-gate-01--a-trustworthy-v23-baseline--delivered-2026-08-18); SMART-01; [V2.4-GATE-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-v24-gate-01--recoverable-green-released).

### ☐ DEBT-160 — Only checklist COMPLETION is offline-capable — P3

- **Current issue.** TASKS-13 made ticking and unticking a checklist item an offline mutation, carried by PWA-12's existing queue, receipts and conflict rule (`set_checklist_completed`, with the new `targetId` naming the item — [`app/kernel/offline/offline-mutation.ts`](../../app/kernel/offline/offline-mutation.ts)). Adding, renaming, deleting and reordering a checklist item are ONLINE-ONLY: a transport failure on any of them is reported as an ordinary refusal, exactly as it was before the slice existed ([`app/shared/task-record/use-task-checklist.ts`](../../app/shared/task-record/use-task-checklist.ts)).
- **Why it was not done.** Each of the four needs something the queue's contract does not carry. Adding needs a server-assigned id AND a server-assigned dense position; renaming and deleting address an item whose identity the device may no longer share; reordering contends over the list's WHOLE current order, which is not a single comparable field and cannot be arbitrated by PWA-12's one-field rule. Queueing any of them would mean inventing a second conflict model beside the one that exists — which is precisely what PWA-12's own contract refuses.
- **Impact.** Small and honest. The one act an owner performs repeatedly while working through a Task — ticking a step — works offline; the structural edits, which are made once when the checklist is written, need a connection and say so with their own wording rather than failing silently.
- **Desired future state.** Either a widened offline contract that can carry a client-minted id and a list-shaped conflict, or a documented decision that structural checklist edits stay online — taken deliberately rather than by omission.
- **Closing condition.** Either an E2E journey in the shape of `e2e/tasks-checklist.spec.ts`'s offline pair, adding an item offline and replaying it exactly once with no duplicate; or this entry closed as WON'T DO with the reasoning recorded in [`PWA_AND_OFFLINE.md`](../development/PWA_AND_OFFLINE.md#151-what-may-be-changed-offline).
- **Related roadmap item.** [TASKS-13](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_3.md#-tasks-13--checklists--delivered-2026-08-18); PWA-12.

### ☐ DEBT-161 — A phone Task row shows no checklist progress — P3

- **Current issue.** The shared `TaskRow` draws a compact "2 of 5" beside the title, and `app/styles/task-checklist.css` hides it below `md`. On a phone the step count is reachable only by opening the Task record.
- **Why it was done that way, MEASURED.** On the same page, with and without a checklist ([`measurements.json`](../design/assets/v2-3-tasks-13-checklists/measurements.json)): at 1440 and 1280 a row with the figure is 44px and a row without is 44px — it costs nothing. At 393 and 320 the row is two stacked lines and the title has the narrowest measure it ever gets, so five characters beside it took width off the title and wrapped it: 100px against 81px, nineteen pixels a row, on the surface where density matters most. The item's own brief gave the rule that was followed — if the indicator harms row clarity, keep it to the record.
- **Impact.** A phone owner scanning a list cannot see how far through a Task's steps they are without opening it. Narrow: the record is one tap away and is where the steps are worked through anyway.
- **Desired future state.** A phone row that can carry the figure without costing the title — most likely in the row's quiet second metadata line rather than in the title cell, which needs the shared row's phone composition to place it there rather than a CSS override.
- **Closing condition.** A measurement in `e2e/tasks-checklist-screenshots.spec.ts` showing a 393 and a 320 row WITH the figure at the same height as one without, and `e2e/tasks-checklist.spec.ts` asserting the figure is visible at 390.
- **Related roadmap item.** [TASKS-13](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_3.md#-tasks-13--checklists--delivered-2026-08-18); DS-04.

### ☐ DEBT-162 — The six-column planning board needs a 1440px viewport — P3

- **Current issue.** UX-02 draws Mockup 7's six-column week board from 90rem (1440px) up, and FOLDS it to three columns over two rows below that ([`app/styles/plan.css`](../../app/styles/plan.css)). MEASURED with `node scripts/ux-02-shot.mjs --measure 1`: at 1440 the board is 888px and a day column is 147px; at 1280 the board is 696px, so six columns would be 108px and a Task card's title about 35px.
- **Why it was done that way.** 108px is narrower than the card the board needs, and squeezing it would truncate every title to two or three words — which is the exact failure ADR-101 §10 originally rejected a board to avoid. The fold is the product's standing "recompose, never squeeze" rule, and the three-column form is a good composition rather than a degraded one.
- **Impact.** An owner on a 1280 or 1366 laptop sees the board as 3 + 3 rather than as one row of six. The information is identical and nothing truncates; what is lost is the single-glance week the reference draws.
- **Desired future state.** Six columns at 1280, reached by finding width rather than by taking it off the title — the shell's 216px rail and the page gutters are the candidates, and neither has been measured for this.
- **Closing condition.** A measurement in `scripts/ux-02-shot.mjs`'s output showing six columns at 1280 with a card title at or above the 73px it measures at 1440, and no horizontal document overflow at 1280 or 1024.
- **V2.4 disposition — KEPT OPEN, DEFERRED.** [V2.4-GATE-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-v24-gate-02--honest-signals-on-a-task-row-and-one-day-on-a-phone--delivered-2026-08-25) names this as a non-goal: it is a composition question needing its own measurement, and nothing is lost to the owner but a single-glance week.
- **RE-READ AND RE-VERIFIED, STILL OPEN (V2.4-GATE-02, 2026-08-25).** Taken on trust by nobody: the entry was re-read against current code and the fold is still what `plan.css` draws, still at 90rem. **It remains real and its rationale is still valid** — at 1280 the board measures 696px, so six columns would be 108px and a card title about 35px, which is the exact truncation ADR-101 §10 rejected a board to avoid. **Nothing in V2.4-GATE-02 made it trivial**: that item changed the queue's interaction and the row's semantics and did not touch the board's width, the shell's 216px rail or the page gutters — the two places its closing condition says the width would have to come from, neither of which has been measured for it. Closing it would mean taking the measurement and the composition decision this entry describes, which is the Weekly Planning redesign V2.4-GATE-02's own terms forbid. **It stays open with its reason unchanged.**
- **Related roadmap item.** [UX-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_3.md#-ux-02--weekly-planning-and-habits-rebuilt-to-the-visual-references--delivered-2026-08-19); [ADR-104](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md).

### ☐ DEBT-163 — A Sunday-start week draws seven board columns and wraps the seventh — P3

- **Current issue.** The board pairs ADJACENT weekend days into one column, computed from the loader's own `isWeekend` so it follows the owner's `firstDayOfWeek` rather than assuming Monday ([`app/modules/plan/PlanWorkspace.tsx`](../../app/modules/plan/PlanWorkspace.tsx), `toColumns`). With `firstDayOfWeek: sunday`, Sunday leads the week and Saturday trails it, so neither has a neighbour to pair with: the week yields seven groups and the seventh wraps to a second row.
- **Why it was done that way.** The alternative — pairing the two weekend days wherever they sit — would draw "Sun / Sat" as the FIRST column of a Sunday-start week, which puts the two days out of order to save a column. Ordering the days truthfully was judged worth an untidy wrap, and the wrap is legible.
- **Impact.** A Sunday-start owner sees six columns and one below them, instead of one row. Correct, and slightly untidy. The default preference is Monday, so it is not the common case.
- **Desired future state.** A weekend treatment that reads well when the two days are not adjacent — most likely a narrower column for each of them rather than a pairing — decided as a design question with a measurement.
- **Closing condition.** A capture at 1440 with `firstDayOfWeek: sunday` showing one row of columns in calendar order, and `plan-responsive.spec.ts` asserting no wrap at that preference.
- **V2.4 disposition — KEPT OPEN, DEFERRED.** Named as a non-goal by [V2.4-GATE-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-v24-gate-02--honest-signals-on-a-task-row-and-one-day-on-a-phone--delivered-2026-08-25), for the same reason as [DEBT-162](#-debt-162--the-six-column-planning-board-needs-a-1440px-viewport--p3).
- **RE-READ AND RE-VERIFIED, STILL OPEN (V2.4-GATE-02, 2026-08-25).** `toColumns` in [`PlanWorkspace.tsx`](../../app/modules/plan/PlanWorkspace.tsx) still pairs ADJACENT weekend days from the loader's own `isWeekend`, so a Sunday-start week still yields seven groups and still wraps the seventh. **Real, and the rationale still holds**: pairing the two weekend days wherever they sit would draw "Sun / Sat" as the FIRST column of a Sunday-start week, putting two days out of calendar order to save a column, and ordering the days truthfully is worth an untidy wrap. **Not made trivial by anything in V2.4-GATE-02**, which changed the queue rail and the shared row and left `toColumns`, the board and the week's column model untouched. Its closing condition is a DESIGN decision plus a capture at `firstDayOfWeek: sunday` — a weekend treatment that reads well when the two days are not adjacent — which is a composition question of its own. **It stays open with its reason unchanged.**
- **Related roadmap item.** [UX-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_3.md#-ux-02--weekly-planning-and-habits-rebuilt-to-the-visual-references--delivered-2026-08-19).

### ☑ DEBT-164 — A planning queue row carries two checkboxes — P3 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-25 (V2.4-GATE-02, with DEBT-194)**

- **Current issue.** A row in "Still to place" draws the shared selection checkbox AND the shared completion circle, because PLAN-01 gave the queue bulk selection over the ordinary Task row ([`app/modules/plan/PlanWorkspace.tsx`](../../app/modules/plan/PlanWorkspace.tsx)). Mockup 7 draws one control per row.
- **Why it was not changed.** Both are useful and they mean different things: one chooses the Task for placement, the other finishes it. Merging them needs a decision about what a single tick on a queue row MEANS — and guessing wrong makes a surface whose purpose is deliberate placement complete work by accident.
- **Impact.** Two adjacent square controls at the head of every queue row, which reads as a duplicate until the owner has used it once. Cosmetic, and only on this one rail.
- **Desired future state.** Either one control with a stated meaning and the other act moved to the row's overflow, or a visual distinction strong enough that the two never read as a pair.
- **Closing condition.** A capture of the rail at 1440 and 393 with one control per row (or two that are unmistakably different), and `plan-weekly-planning.spec.ts` still proving both acts are reachable by keyboard.
- **CLOSED WITH DEBT-194 (V2.4-GATE-02, 2026-08-25), as its supersession required — worked as ONE item, not two.** This entry's own closing condition is met and is worth stating in its own words, because it asked for something DEBT-194's did not: *"a capture of the rail at 1440 and 393 with one control per row (or two that are unmistakably different), and `plan-weekly-planning.spec.ts` still proving both acts are reachable by keyboard."* Both halves hold. **One control per row** is now MEASURED rather than captured — at 320/360/375/393/430/820/900/1280/1440, in both appearances, at rest and in selection mode, every row reports exactly one checkbox-like control. And `plan-weekly-planning.spec.ts` still proves both acts by keyboard: its placement journey now enters the mode with Enter on a real button before selecting with Space, and completion keeps its own keyboard path at rest. This entry's preferred remedy — *"one control with a stated meaning and the other act moved to the row's overflow"* — is exactly what shipped, in both directions: at rest completion is the control and placement is in the overflow; in selection mode selection is the control and completion is in the overflow.
- **SUPERSEDED by [DEBT-194](#-debt-194--the-plan-queue-draws-a-selection-control-and-a-completion-control-side-by-side-which-the-design-systems-own-invariant-forbids--p2--resolved-2026-08-25-v24-gate-02) (2026-08-22).** They are the same defect. This entry recorded it as cosmetic (*"reads as a duplicate until the owner has used it once"*); DHDS-13 measured it against `task-signals.css`'s own stated invariant and found the real cost — **a mis-click completes work the owner meant to schedule** — and raised it at P2. DEBT-194 is the authoritative statement. **The entry is kept rather than deleted** so its existing cross-references still resolve, and both close together under [V2.4-GATE-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-v24-gate-02--honest-signals-on-a-task-row-and-one-day-on-a-phone--delivered-2026-08-25). Do not work them as two items.
- **Related roadmap item.** [UX-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_3.md#-ux-02--weekly-planning-and-habits-rebuilt-to-the-visual-references--delivered-2026-08-19); PLAN-01.

### ☐ DEBT-165 — A template carries no dates, relative or otherwise — P2

- **Current issue.** A Project template stores no date of any kind, so a project created from one arrives with every task undated and unplanned ([`app/kernel/project-templates/project-template.ts`](../../app/kernel/project-templates/project-template.ts); [ADR-105 §4](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md)). The roadmap item explicitly asked whether "Book venue — due 14 days after the project is created" should ship, and PROJECT-02 answered no.
- **Why it was done that way.** DalyHub already has three date authorities — a due date, the `scheduled_date` that IS the plan (ADR-030), and a recurrence anchor (ADR-062/ADR-085). A relative offset would be a FOURTH: resolved once at instantiation and never re-derivable afterwards, needing its own vocabulary (from creation? from a start date? business days?), its own timezone rule and its own edge cases. PLAN-01 already built the surface where a fresh project gets its days.
- **Impact.** An owner instantiating a twelve-task template plans all twelve from scratch each time, even where the cadence is genuinely fixed ("send the draft on the 10th, present on the 15th"). The create drawer says nothing is scheduled, so it is stated rather than discovered — but it is real work the owner repeats.
- **Desired future state.** A CLOSED offset vocabulary — a whole number of days after project creation, and nothing else — resolved into the existing `due_date`/`scheduled_date` at instantiation, with the owner's timezone deciding the day. Never an expression language.
- **Closing condition.** An ADR fixing the vocabulary and its timezone rule; the offset stored as an integer column on `project_template_tasks`; a kernel test proving a template instantiated in two timezones lands on the owner's day in both; and the create drawer stating the resulting dates before it writes them.
- **Related roadmap item.** [PROJECT-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_3.md#-project-02--project-templates--delivered-2026-08-19); [ADR-105](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md).

### ☐ DEBT-166 — A template task cannot repeat — P3

- **Current issue.** A template task carries no recurrence rule, so a project made from a template that "always has a weekly check-in" arrives with a single one-off task ([`migrations/0046_create_project_templates.sql`](../../migrations/0046_create_project_templates.sql)).
- **Why it was done that way.** A DalyHub recurrence rule is anchored to concrete dates (`date_kind`, `anchor_day`, and a series whose next occurrence is computed from the last one). A template holds no dates (DEBT-165), so a recurrence rule in a template is not merely undesirable — it is not representable. This one is blocked on that one.
- **Impact.** The owner adds the repeat by hand after creating the project, once per project. Small, and only for templates that genuinely contain routine work.
- **Desired future state.** Once DEBT-165 gives a template task a resolvable first date, a recurrence rule can be carried alongside it and instantiated as a real series.
- **Closing condition.** A kernel test showing a template task with a repeat producing a project task with a live recurrence series whose first occurrence is the resolved date, and no successor generated at instantiation.
- **Related roadmap item.** [PROJECT-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_3.md#-project-02--project-templates--delivered-2026-08-19); TASKS-12.

### ☐ DEBT-167 — Creating a project from a template requires connectivity — P3

- **Current issue.** PROJECT-02 added no offline mutation: browsing templates works from whatever the PWA has cached, but saving, editing and instantiating all require the network ([`docs/development/PWA_AND_OFFLINE.md`](../development/PWA_AND_OFFLINE.md); [ADR-105 §8](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md)).
- **Why it was done that way.** The PWA-12 replay ledger exists for single, idempotent, narrow Task mutations, and its `operation` set is a closed CHECK constraint for exactly that reason. An instantiation is a compound write of up to ~287 statements whose whole guarantee is atomicity; replaying it offline would mean either giving up that guarantee or reimplementing it client-side.
- **Impact.** An owner on a plane cannot start a project from a template. Given the frequency of the act — a handful of times a month — this was judged a fair boundary rather than a gap.
- **Desired future state.** If it ever matters, the honest shape is a QUEUED INTENT (template id, title, parent) replayed as one server-side instantiation when connectivity returns — never a client-side assembly of the rows.
- **Closing condition.** An offline journey creating a project from a template, coming back online, and proving exactly one project with exactly the right rows — including after a duplicate replay.
- **Related roadmap item.** [PROJECT-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_3.md#-project-02--project-templates--delivered-2026-08-19); PWA-12.

### ☐ DEBT-168 — A template captures no links and no Knowledge — P3

- **Current issue.** Capturing a project copies its tasks and their checklists, and nothing else: the project's `project.relates_to` links and its Knowledge notes are left behind ([`app/platform/storage/d1/d1-project-template-repository.ts`](../../app/platform/storage/d1/d1-project-template-repository.ts), `createTemplateFromProject`).
- **Why it was done that way.** A link is a relationship between two records that EXIST. Copying "related to the 2026 vendor contract" into a template means either carrying an entity reference that a new project may have no business claiming, or inventing a second kind of soft reference. Neither was worth deciding for PROJECT-02.
- **Impact.** A project whose shape genuinely includes "always linked to the supplier note" has to be relinked once per instantiation.
- **Desired future state.** A decision about whether a template may hold a reference to a live record at all — and if so, what happens when that record is deleted between saving the template and using it.
- **Closing condition.** An ADR answering that question, and a kernel test proving a template whose referenced record has been deleted still instantiates cleanly.
- **Related roadmap item.** [PROJECT-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_3.md#-project-02--project-templates--delivered-2026-08-19).

### ☐ DEBT-169 — Dependencies are occurrence-local, so a recurring pair must be relinked every cycle — P3

- **Current issue.** TASKS-12 attaches a dependency to concrete Task OCCURRENCES and never clones it onto a successor ([ADR-107 §7](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-107-advanced-recurrence-widens-a-closed-vocabulary-and-dependencies-are-occurrence-local--one-successor-authority-a-remembered-grid-and-no-relationship-cloning)). An owner whose "Prepare monthly report" genuinely gates their "Submit monthly report" every month re-adds the dependency once a month.
- **Why it was done that way.** An occurrence that has not been created is a prediction, not work, so an edge to one would reference something that may never happen — a series can end, a rule can be removed, an occurrence can be deleted. Cloning would also require guessing which future occurrence of A corresponds to which of B, and the only available mappings ("by date", "by sequence") are each wrong the moment one series is completed late or skipped. Shipping the simple rule and SAYING SO was judged better than shipping a guess.
- **Impact.** One extra interaction per cycle for the small number of recurring pairs that genuinely depend on each other. The product states the rule rather than surprising anyone with it.
- **Desired future state.** If it is wanted, the honest shape is corresponding-occurrence inheritance keyed on SERIES IDENTITY plus sequence, cloned with fresh ids and only when both matching successors can be identified — and it needs a product answer for two series of different cadences before it needs an implementation.
- **Closing condition.** An ADR answering the different-cadence question, plus a kernel test proving occurrence #13 of A blocks occurrence #13 of B and nothing else, including when one series is skipped and when one ends.
- **Related roadmap item.** [TASKS-12](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_3.md#-tasks-12--advanced-recurrence--dependencies--delivered-2026-08-19).

### ☐ DEBT-170 — Adding or removing a dependency requires connectivity — P3

- **Current issue.** TASKS-12 added no offline mutation for dependencies or for recurrence rules: reading blocked state works from the cached snapshot, but both writes require the network ([`docs/development/PWA_AND_OFFLINE.md`](../development/PWA_AND_OFFLINE.md); [ADR-106](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-106-a-task-dependency-is-a-directed-entitylink-not-a-second-join-model--derived-blocked-state-and-cycle--bound-enforcement-inside-the-write)).
- **Why it was done that way.** A dependency's outcome is a property of the GRAPH at the moment of the write — only the server knows whether an edge closes a cycle or crosses a bound — so a queued dependency is an intent the device cannot evaluate and might have to withdraw hours later. A recurrence rule's validity likewise depends on the Task's own anchor date. Building a local dependency engine to decide either would be a second authority for the one thing this programme exists to keep singular.
- **Impact.** An owner offline can complete a blocker (that already queues) but cannot record a new dependency. It also leaves a documented temporary state: the device knows a blocker is complete while the server does not, so the dependent may still read as blocked until the completion replays.
- **Desired future state.** If it matters, a QUEUED INTENT arbitrated server-side on replay — with a refusal the sync surface can state in words when the graph moved underneath it — never a client-side cycle check.
- **Closing condition.** An offline journey adding a dependency, coming back online, and proving exactly one edge — plus a journey whose queued edge is refused because another device closed the cycle first, reported without data loss.
- **Related roadmap item.** [TASKS-12](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_3.md#-tasks-12--advanced-recurrence--dependencies--delivered-2026-08-19); PWA-12.

### ☐ DEBT-171 — The recurrence editor states the rule but never the next few dates — P3

- **Current issue.** The shared editor says what a rule MEANS ("The last Friday of every month, moved to the Friday before, 12 times") and never what it will DO ("25 Sep, 30 Oct, 27 Nov…"). For the advanced rules TASKS-12 added, the sentence is harder to verify at a glance than a plain "Every week" was.
- **Why it was done that way.** DalyHub materialises recurrence incrementally ([ADR-062](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-062-intentional-unassigned-tasks-inbox-semantics-and-calendar-recurrence)): exactly one occurrence exists at a time, and a projected calendar is a claim about Tasks that do not exist. `planNextTaskOccurrence` could be iterated to produce a preview, but a preview is a promise, and one that a later edit, a skip or a late completion would silently break.
- **Impact.** An owner authoring "the last Friday, skipping weekends, twelve times" reads a sentence and trusts it, rather than seeing three dates and recognising them.
- **Desired future state.** A read-only "next three dates" line under the summary, computed from the same authority, worded as a projection rather than a schedule ("if nothing changes: …").
- **Closing condition.** A preview whose dates are produced by `planNextTaskOccurrence` and nothing else, with a unit test proving it agrees with what completion actually creates for every rule shape.
- **Related roadmap item.** [TASKS-12](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_3.md#-tasks-12--advanced-recurrence--dependencies--delivered-2026-08-19).

### ☑ DEBT-172 — The service-worker budget bounds the worker and its precache manifest as one number — P3 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-25**

- **Current issue.** `SERVICE_WORKER_MAX_BYTES` in [`e2e/pwa-budget.spec.ts`](../../e2e/pwa-budget.spec.ts) measures `/sw.js` WHOLE — the worker's logic and the list of shell bundles the build substitutes into it. MEASURED 2026-08-19: the logic is 22,925 bytes (`vite-plugins/sw-template.js`, unchanged by TASKS-12) and the manifest is 1,013 bytes / 31 assets on `main`, 1,074 / 33 after TASKS-12 added one resource route. The ceiling was 24,000 with `main` at 23,960 — forty bytes of headroom — so TASKS-12's sixty-five-byte manifest growth failed it.
- **Why it was done that way.** The budget was written for V2.0.1 against a 12 kB worker, where 24,000 was ~2x headroom. The worker doubled over eighteen roadmap items without the number being revisited, and one ceiling over two things that grow for completely different reasons cannot say which one moved.
- **Impact.** A ceiling with forty bytes of headroom stops answering "did anyone triple what a phone downloads?" and starts answering "did anyone add a route?" — which fires on changes that are not regressions and, worse, would stay quiet about real worker growth once someone raises it far enough to stop the noise. TASKS-12 re-baselined it to 27,000 (measured + ~12%) with the numbers recorded in the file, which restores the ratchet but does not fix the conflation.
- **Desired future state.** TWO ceilings: one on the worker's own source (`sw-template.js`, which nothing but a deliberate change to the worker moves) and one on the substituted manifest's byte count — beside `PRECACHE_MAX_ASSETS`, which already bounds the manifest's LENGTH and is the natural place for its size.
- **Closing condition.** Two budgets, each with its own measured value and headroom, and a run proving that adding a route moves only the manifest number.
- **RESOLVED 2026-08-25 by the [all-open-debt pass](PRODUCT_DEBT_CLOSURE_2026_08.md), as two ceilings — and a third assertion the entry did not ask for and needs.**
  - **The LOGIC ceiling** is over `vite-plugins/sw-template.js` **on disk**, not over the served file. That is the substance: a route cannot reach the template, so this number moves only when somebody changes the worker. **Measured 2026-08-25: 22,925 B against 25,000** (2,075 B of worker-only headroom, where the single ceiling left 3,015 B shared between two things).
  - **The MANIFEST ceiling** is over the URL literals the plugin substitutes, and it sits beside `PRECACHE_MAX_ASSETS`, which already bounds the manifest's LENGTH. This one bounds its **bytes**, so a route with a very long path is caught as well as a route that is merely one more. **Measured 1,004 B against 2,000.**
  - **The third assertion is the one that keeps the split honest.** Two ceilings over two parts of a file can both pass while a THIRD thing grows inside it, which is the regression splitting a budget introduces. So the test asserts the served worker is no bigger than logic + manifest + a bounded substitution slack. **Measured: 23,985 B served, and 22,925 + 1,004 = 23,929 — fifty-six bytes of build id and offline-document literal.**
  - **FALSIFIED, each ceiling on its own.** Lowering the logic ceiling to 22,000 and the manifest ceiling to 900 fails the run; and the accounting assertion was falsified **separately**, with both ceilings back at their real values and only the slack reduced, so it is shown to be non-vacuous by itself: *"the served worker (23985 B) is larger than its logic (22925 B) plus its manifest (1004 B) can explain"*. All three restored, and green.
  - **What is NOT claimed.** The closing condition asks for *"a run proving that adding a route moves only the manifest number"*. No route was added, and one is not needed: the logic number is read from a **source file the build does not modify**, so a route cannot move it by construction — and the manifest number is computed from the same `urls` array `PRECACHE_MAX_ASSETS` already bounds, which this entry itself accepts as route-sensitive. Stating that is more honest than adding a throwaway route to manufacture a run.
  - **This does NOT close [DEBT-75](#-debt-75--the-service-worker-byte-budget-has-2185-b-of-headroom--p3).** That entry is about the worker's own COMMENTS costing budget, and the logic ceiling still measures them — it just no longer measures them against a number a route can exhaust.
- **Related roadmap item.** [TASKS-12](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_3.md#-tasks-12--advanced-recurrence--dependencies--delivered-2026-08-19); PWA-10.

### ☐ DEBT-173 — E2E specs assert against the shared workspace's ACCUMULATED state, so re-ordering the suite changes what they see — P2

> **PRESERVED 2026-08-27 by [V2.4 FOLLOW-02](V2_4_FOLLOW_02_GOAL_MOVEMENT_2026_08.md), which added NO new leaker and met this entry from both sides again.** `follow-02-fixtures.ts` owns every row it writes under an `fm-` prefix — six Goals, ten Projects, nine Tasks, three measurements and their Activity — and `cleanupMovementFixture` removes all of it dependents-first (`activity_subjects` → orphaned `activities` → `entity_links` → measurements and milestones → the three detail slices → `spine_records` → `entities`), because every foreign key in the schema is ON DELETE RESTRICT. It is idempotent at both ends: seeding twice repairs, cleaning twice is a no-op, and the journey cleans BEFORE it seeds so an interrupted previous run repairs rather than duplicates.
>
> **Its window is the CURRENT week, which is the opposite of FOLLOW-01's choice, and the isolation argument is what makes that safe.** FOLLOW-01 used a CLOSED week precisely because other specs complete real Tasks stamped NOW; FOLLOW-02 states movement for the owner's current week and therefore cannot. What protects it instead is that every assertion is **per-Goal**, never a workspace-wide count: another spec completing its own Task cannot reach a Goal it does not structurally contribute to — which this very fixture also proves as a PRODUCT rule, with a Project that advances no Goal and a completed Task under it. **No exact global workspace count is asserted anywhere in the journey.**
>
> **No concrete new leaker was encountered**, so nothing was fixed against this entry. It remains open on its own closing condition.

> **ADVANCED 2026-08-26 by [V2.4 FOLLOW-01](V2_4_FOLLOW_01_WEEK_ACCOUNT_2026_08.md), which EXERCISED this entry's closing condition for the first time — and failed it, on measured evidence.** It added no leaker of its own (its fixture is prefixed `fw-`, its period is a CLOSED week nothing else in the suite can write into, and its `afterAll` removes every row dependents-first), and it worked around the seed's moving dates rather than widening the entry: the journey asserts the five figures only its own fixture can produce, each needing an EVENT inside the period the seed never writes, plus internal consistency between the sentence, its outcome lines and the rows behind them. Both exact; neither a bound.
>
> Then it had to raise `PARTITION_COUNT` from twelve to thirteen — forced, not chosen: the committed split was packed to within **0.1 s** of the ceiling, its emptiest partition had **11.5 s** of headroom and the new journey needs 43.2 s. `derivePartitions` is a greedy bin-pack, so a change of count re-derives every assignment: **117 of 117 spec files got a different neighbour set.** That is this entry's closing condition performed for real — *"the split re-derived and the partition assignment materially reshuffled"* — and the answer is that specs DID change their result.
>
> **One changed deterministically, and it was a genuine leaker, now removed.** `cleanupMeetingByTitle` swept Tasks and Meetings by the same pattern, `title LIKE '<the exact meeting title>'`, but a follow-up Task's title is the action item's BODY — `` `${title} — do the thing` `` — so `audit-13-conversion-atomicity.spec.ts` removed each Meeting and left the Task it spawned alive for the rest of the partition. Invisible until the repack sat it next to `tasks-dependencies.spec.ts`, which matches a row by the substring *"Book the venue"*; a leaked *"Meetings e2e idempotent-…-2 — book the venue"* made that locator resolve to two rows and fail strict mode. Reproduced locally under p01's exact order from a fresh seed, measured as two orphaned Tasks and ZERO Meetings, fixed with a prefix wildcard, verified at zero of both. **One leaker removed; the entry's mechanism is untouched and it stays open.**
>
> **Two other partitions went red once each and did not reproduce** — `project-settings.spec.ts:234` (passed on the next CI run, unchanged) and `inline-editor-overlay.spec.ts:230` (passed locally in its own new composition at 10.1 s). Neither is recorded here as this entry's shape, because neither was demonstrated to be; the second did expose an incoherent test budget, fixed separately.
>
> **A lead for whoever closes this.** The reshuffle bought nothing. A churn-minimal 13-way split — keep every existing grouping, put the new spec in the new bin — was simulated at the **identical** heaviest partition of 1003.9 s with **0 of 117** neighbour sets changed. Makespan is set by the ceiling, not by the packing, so balance and stability are not in tension here. FOLLOW-01 did not make that change because `manifestProblems` re-derives the split and rejects a manifest that is not what the durations produce; a derivation that remembered the previous grouping would validate the manifest against itself, and trading that guard away is not a feature PR's call. It is, however, the cheapest route to this entry's closing condition: a split that does not reshuffle cannot reshuffle a spec into failure.

- **Current issue.** Every partition runs its spec files against one dev server and one local D1 seeded identically, but the specs inside it run in sequence and each leaves its fixtures behind. A spec that asks for *"the first task row"*, or for its own task to be visible in a bounded band, is therefore asserting against *the seed plus whatever every earlier spec in its partition happened to create* — and that set is a property of the SPLIT, not of the product. The split is derived from measurements, so it moves whenever the suite's timings move.
- **Evidence (HARDEN-06A, 2026-08-20).** Three twelve-partition runs, [`32333645709`](https://github.com/acedaly/DalyHub-V2/actions/runs/32333645709) (run A, the interim split), [`32338241602`](https://github.com/acedaly/DalyHub-V2/actions/runs/32338241602) (run B) and [`32340347468`](https://github.com/acedaly/DalyHub-V2/actions/runs/32340347468) (run C) — B and C on an **identical executable tree**. Every partition of all three FINISHED and executed every test it collected: **36 of 36 partitions, zero unexecuted tests**, so this is not F-03 returning. What varied was which tests passed:
  - **Run B: 0 failures. Run C: 4 partitions red** (p02, p07, p08, p10), each on a different, unrelated test.
  - Three of the four were diagnosed. Two of those three are this entry:
  - `e2e/iphone-daily-driver.spec.ts:185` asserts the overflow sheet's last row sits inside the phone viewport, and measured **853.85 against a 845 limit** — an 8.85 px overrun. It opens the menu of `taskRows(page).first()` on a **bare `/tasks`**, so *which* task, and therefore how many actions the menu offers, is decided by the accumulated collection.
  - `e2e/tasks-journey.spec.ts:379` reopened a P1 task and could not find it in the `Priority 1` band of `/tasks?view=list&system=active&group=priority`. The URL is fully explicit, so this is not the default-view leak HARDEN-06A fixed; the band is bounded and the workspace had accumulated more active P1 tasks than it did on the run before.
  - The third, `e2e/notes.spec.ts:424` (the unsaved-changes navigation guard not appearing), is **not** this entry — it is an ordinary timing race, and it belongs with [DEBT-125](#-debt-125--mains-e2e-suite-is-red-for-reasons-unrelated-to-the-change-that-finds-it--p1--no-longer-broadly-red-and-the-browser-fix-is-holding-the-suite-still-cannot-finish-harden-03-2026-08-12). p10's was not individually diagnosed. Do not fold the two shapes together: one is fixed by giving a spec its own fixture, the other is not.
- **Why HARDEN-06A did not fix it.** It is neither F-03 nor F-11, it is not one defect but a property of ~111 specs, and the repair is per-spec fixtures — the shape `e2e/habits-fixtures.ts` and `e2e/reviews-fixtures.ts` already use. HARDEN-06A fixed the two instances it *caused* (a `main.innerText()` snapshot over a live region, and an owner-level default Tasks view restored only on success) and named this one rather than opening the whole suite in a slice whose stated non-goals include exactly that.
- **Impact, stated precisely.** It does **not** make the gate unable to report — that was F-03, and it is fixed. It makes a green gate *harder to obtain* than it should be, and it means a re-derivation of the split can turn a passing spec red without any product change, which is a bad property for a mechanism that is supposed to be re-derived routinely.
- **Desired future state.** A spec that asserts over "the first row", a bounded band, or a count either creates and cleans up its own fixture, or scopes its assertion to a record it owns by title. No spec's result depends on which other specs preceded it.
- **A fresh instance, MEASURED 2026-08-29 by [V2.6 FIND-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_6.md#-find-01--search-answers-before-you-type--delivered-2026-08-29), which did not touch Assets.** `assets-ownership.spec.ts:582` — *"the collection surfaces the obligation signal and filters on it"* — fails on a **strict-mode violation** rather than on a wrong value: `page.getByText("1 obligation overdue")` resolves to **two** elements, the spec's own seeded asset and the shared seed's *"Hilux SR5 — work ute"*. The assertion is a workspace-wide text query where it means *"my fixture's asset"*, which is exactly the shape this entry describes; it did not need a re-ordered split to break, only a second overdue obligation anywhere in the workspace. Reproduced on a clean tree at `bc26fd2` with FIND-01's work absent, so it is the suite's, not that item's. Recorded here rather than as a new number, because this entry already owns the class and the register forbids restating one defect under two ids.
- **Closing condition.** The split can be re-derived and the partition assignment materially reshuffled without any spec changing its result, demonstrated by two runs of the same commit under two different derived splits.
- **V2.4 disposition — TAKEN.** [V2.4-GATE-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-v24-gate-01--recoverable-green-released), together with [DEBT-179](#-debt-179--the-e2e-gate-is-red-on-main-19-tests-across-8-partitions-plus-a-network-dependent-unit-test--p2--resolved-2026-08-23-v24-gate-01), because that entry's own closing condition requires passing against a freshly seeded database **and** against accumulated state — which is this entry. One answer to *"why did this assertion fail?"*, as DEBT-179 asks for.

The gate did not need any spec's dependence on accumulated state repaired to reach green, and none was repaired by resetting D1 between tests.
