A wipe and reseed passed all three. That is this entry's shape at the scale of many separate runs rather than one sequence — and underneath it sat a genuine P2 ([DEBT-201](#-debt-201--both-record-pickers-stop-seeing-a-workspace-at-its-500th-record-and-say-nothing--p2--resolved-2026-08-23-v24-gate-01)) that would have gone unrecorded had the three been written off as flake.
- **CORRECTION — the accumulated-state run DID produce instances, and the note above understates it (2026-08-23).** The claim that no failure had this signature is true of the 55 measured on `main`, and stops being the whole story once the full sequential gate ran. It produced **two**, and neither could ever appear in CI:
  - **`entity-icons.spec.ts` × 3.** `identity.spec.ts` (p01) mutates the shared seeded Area `a-dh`, giving it the Wellbeing icon. `entity-icons.spec.ts` (p10) uses that same Area as its `AREA_WITHOUT_ICON` and asserts `not.toHaveAttribute("data-icon-key", /./)`. Nine partitions apart, one record, two beliefs — MEASURED as `Received "heart"` and `Received "Wellbeing, Emerald"`. This entry's own definition, exactly: the result is a property of the SPLIT rather than of the product.
  - **`identity.spec.ts:268`, which is this shape turned INWARD.** It asserts a Goal reads "Automatic" before choosing, then chooses Rose + Reading on a Goal it picks BY POSITION (`a[href*='/goals/']` first) and never puts back. It passed on a pristine database and failed on the second run against the same one — `Expected "Automatic" / Received "Reading, Rose"`. A spec whose own precondition its own previous run destroys.
- **Both are fixed by this entry's own prescription, and one of them taught a refinement.** The mutator cleans up: `identity.spec.ts` now clears the Area through the picker's "Use the defaults" control — which had no coverage of its own, so the cleanup is also a test. But cleanup at the END is not enough on its own: **a test that fails at its own precondition never reaches its cleanup and stays dirty for good.** So `:268` ESTABLISHES the state rather than assuming it, healing whatever the last run left before it asserts. Verified by running that file three times in a row against one database — 9, 9, 9 passed — which is the check this entry has always been asking for, at one file's scale.
- **Why it is STILL NOT closed.** Its closing condition is *"two runs of the same commit under two different derived splits"*, and that was not performed. What exists is adjacent and weaker: the split was re-derived from green run `32605964327` and the next push ran the suite under the new assignment. And the deeper point stands — these two were found because a full sequential run happened to be performed, not because anything prevents the next one. ~117 spec files still share one seeded workspace, and the mechanism that let these two disagree is untouched.
- **MEASURED at the scale of a whole sequential run, and it is bigger than a re-ordering problem (V2.4-GATE-02, 2026-08-25).** This entry has been argued from partition re-ordering; running the COMPLETE local gate in one process against one database puts a number on the underlying leak.

  | | active entities |
  |---|---|
  | committed seed, freshly reseeded | **325** |
  | before the run (a few earlier rehearsals) | 347 |
  | **after one complete 1,928-test run** | **564** |

  **One run leaks 217 records it never cleans up** — enough on its own to carry the workspace two-thirds of the way past the 500-entity horizon [DEBT-201](#-debt-201--both-record-pickers-stop-seeing-a-workspace-at-its-500th-record-and-say-nothing--p2--resolved-2026-08-23-v24-gate-01) was raised for, from a clean start, in a single pass.

  Three tests failed on that run and **all three passed after a wipe and reseed**, with nothing else changed:
  - `dhds-11-drag-reorder.spec.ts:481` — the drag resolved no destination on a page of many buckets (the section was marked `data-dh-drop-candidate` and never `data-dh-drop-active`). It is the same line this register already names among the three that failed on a developer machine and in no CI run.
  - `tasks-dependencies.spec.ts:488` — a strict-mode violation: **three** rows titled "Book the venue" where the assertion expects one. Named at last: `ai-assistance.spec.ts` accepts an AI proposal that CREATES a real Task with that title and never removes it, so every full run leaves one more behind. The database held four — the committed seed's, the test's own fixture, and one from each of two gate runs.
  - `tasks-dependencies.spec.ts:220` — **not** this entry. A genuine date fuse, fixed in the same change; see below.

- **What this adds to the entry.** Two things it did not have. First, a **rate**: the leak is ~217 records per complete run, so the local gate is not repeatable twice from one seed without an explicit wipe — which is a stronger claim than "re-ordering changes what a spec sees". Second, a **named leaker** rather than a class: the AI-proposal journey creates domain records through the real mutation path and has no `afterEach`. The desired future state below is unchanged and now has a first, concrete instance to apply it to.
- **Why V2.4-GATE-02 did not fix it.** It is ~118 spec files' hygiene, and this item's subject is the Task row's signals; taking it would have been the second programme in one PR that its own non-goals forbid. What that item did instead is measure it, name the leaker, and — because a full local gate is now part of how an item is verified — record the wipe-and-reseed step so the next agent does not spend a run diagnosing the environment.
- **V2.8 disposition — TAKEN by [V2.8 CONV-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-03--green-is-a-property-not-a-lottery--delivered-2026-09-04-less-one-owner-held-measurement) (2026-09-02).** Closing condition unchanged (two runs of one commit under two derived splits, identical results); the named leakers, the owned-fixture rule for every "first row"/bounded-band assertion, and a local gate that wipes and reseeds between runs are CONV-03's part 2.
- **WORKED 2026-09-04 by [V2.8 CONV-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-03--green-is-a-property-not-a-lottery--delivered-2026-09-04-less-one-owner-held-measurement) — every named leaker repaired, the local gate given a clean start, and the closing condition made PERFORMABLE.** The entry has been argued about for five programmes and never once tested, because nothing in the repository could compare two runs. It can now.
  - **The leakers, each with the smallest correct fix this entry's own prescription names.**

    | leaker | what leaked | repair |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `ai-assistance.spec.ts` — the AI proposal's accepted Tasks | one real Task per acceptance journey per run, created through the real mutation path and matched by no cleanup prefix. The register's named instance: a bare *"Book the venue"* is also the substring `tasks-dependencies.spec.ts` matches a row on, and **four** had accumulated in one local database | the item titles are now `` `${meetingTitle} — …` ``, so the `cleanupMeetingByTitle` prefix wildcard V2.4 FOLLOW-01 already added sweeps them. **Own the fixture** — no second cleanup path to keep in step with the first |
    | `entity-icons.spec.ts` vs `identity.spec.ts` — the shared `a-dh` Area | one record, two beliefs, nine partitions apart: `identity` chooses an icon, `entity-icons` asserts there is none. MEASURED as `Received "heart"` and `Received "Wellbeing, Emerald"` on a re-derived split | `entity-icons` **establishes** the precondition (a `beforeEach` that clears `icon_key` and `colour_slot`) instead of assuming the mutator cleaned up. Cleanup at the end cannot help a test that failed before reaching it — the refinement `identity.spec.ts:268` taught, applied to the other side |
    | `project-templates.spec.ts` | every `project_template` and every instantiated Project, when a run died between its seed and its `afterAll` | `removeTemplateFixtures` at **both** ends |
    | the responsive overlay sweep | a dialog or an inline editor left open on the shared `a-dh` and `g-launch` fixtures — `Escape` was pressed and never awaited | every scenario asserts the surface it opened is closed. A mutation this scan declines to make is now declined as a fact rather than as a hope |
    | `iphone-daily-driver.spec.ts:185` | nothing — it READS. Its result depended on which task the accumulated collection put first, because the sheet's height is a function of how many actions the task offers | it drives a NAMED seeded row on an Area-scoped collection. (Its intermittency turned out to be two mechanisms; the second is [DEBT-203](#-debt-203--the-e2e-suite-carries-latent-timing-races-at-roughly-one-per-two-runs-so-green-is-probabilistic--p2)'s and is recorded there) |
    | `tasks-journey.spec.ts:334`/`:379` | nothing — the `Priority 1` band is a bounded slice of the workspace's first keyset page, so whether this journey's own task appears in it depends on how many other active P1 tasks the run has accumulated | the band is **scoped to the Project this file creates under**. Every task it creates is created there, so the filter changes nothing about what is asserted and everything about whether the answer is this spec's to determine |

  - **The local gate starts clean, and says so.** `pnpm run e2e:gate` deletes `.wrangler/state/v3/d1` and re-migrates and re-seeds it **before any server starts**, and refuses to run while a server is holding the database (a wipe under a live Miniflare leaves the server serving a deleted file). It prints the workspace's live-entity count before and after, so this entry's own **217-records-per-run** measurement is a number the gate reports rather than one somebody has to go and take: the first run under it reported **325 live entities (freshly seeded)**, which is exactly the committed seed V2.4-GATE-02 measured. It is deliberately NOT a per-test reset — inside an invocation the specs still share one seeded workspace exactly as a CI partition does, which is the condition this entry's fixture ownership has to hold under.
  - **And the closing condition is now a command.** `derivePartitions` already took a partition count, so a second legitimate arrangement is one call to the same pure function `generate` and `check` use, over the same committed durations: `pnpm run e2e:gate --partitions=14 --out=<dir>`. Derived at fourteen, **134 of 134 spec files get a different neighbour set** — a total reshuffle, which is the "materially reshuffled" this entry asks for. `pnpm run e2e:order-proof <a> <b>` then compares the two runs test by test, keyed on each test's own identity rather than on the partition that ran it, and reports tests present on one side only (a coverage change) separately from tests whose outcome differs. **It fails if nothing was reshuffled**, so a comparison of two identical splits cannot pass vacuously.
  - **Result of the two-arrangement proof.** Recorded on the roadmap item with the commit, both arrangements' derivation inputs and the per-test comparison.

- **Related roadmap item.** [HARDEN-06A](HARDEN_06A_FINISHING_E2E_GATE_2026_08.md); the [whole-application audit](DALYHUB_WHOLE_APP_BUG_AUDIT_2026_08.md) §21, which found the same shape one instance at a time.

### ☑ DEBT-174 — A whole-document autosaving field is not REQUIRED to carry a base version — the contract is per-module, not product-wide — P2 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-25**

- **Current issue.** THREE modules now write a whole authored document with a base-version precondition folded into the write: Review sections ([REVIEW-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_1.md#-review-02--weekly-review--delivered-2026-08-05)), the Note body ([AUDIT-FIX-06](#-debt-83--concurrent-note-content-saves-are-blind-last-write-wins--p3--resolved-2026-08-08)) and — since [HARDEN-06B](DALYHUB_WHOLE_APP_REPAIR_2026_08.md) — a Meeting's agenda and notes. Nothing REQUIRES a fourth to. `useAutosaveField`'s reconciliation contract is opt-in via `serverValue`, the repository precondition is an optional parameter on each repository separately, and no test asserts the shape as a rule over the product.
- **Impact.** It is the exact mechanism by which F-01 happened. The Notes fix was written as *"Notes now follow the same shape [as Reviews]"*, and nothing failed when Meetings shipped a third such field without one — for eleven weeks, during which a Meeting's notes could be silently destroyed by a second writer with no trace and no recovery. A fifth surface that autosaves a document is one PR away from repeating it.
- **What ADR-108 does and does not do.** [ADR-108](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-108-three-product-wide-rules-the-whole-application-audit-found-were-per-module-conventions--a-base-version-on-every-whole-document-write-an-owner-day-that-never-travels-without-its-zone-and-maintenance-that-is-not-contact) states the rule, which is why the next author has something to read. It does not ENFORCE it, which is why this entry exists.
- **Desired future state.** A mechanism, not a convention. Two candidates, either acceptable: a shared `useDocumentAutosave` that cannot be constructed without a version and a conflict handler, so the opt-in is structural; or an inventory test that enumerates the whole-document fields (an editor bound to a Markdown column) and asserts each one's repository takes a precondition. The second is cheaper and catches a new surface at the same moment CI would.
- **Closing condition.** A new whole-document autosaving field cannot reach `main` without a base version — demonstrated by adding one without a precondition and watching a test fail, not by inspection.
- **RESOLVED 2026-08-25 by the [all-open-debt pass](PRODUCT_DEBT_CLOSURE_2026_08.md), by the second of the two candidates this entry names** — the inventory test, because it is the one that catches a new surface *at the moment CI would* rather than at the moment somebody remembers the rule.
  - **The mechanism.** [`test/unit/architecture/whole-document-autosave.test.ts`](../../test/unit/architecture/whole-document-autosave.test.ts) walks `app/modules`, `app/shared` and `app/routes`, and treats a component that composes BOTH the shared Markdown writing surface (`LiveMarkdownEditor` / `MarkdownEditorField`) and the shared autosave coordinator (`useAutosaveField`) as a whole-document autosaving field. Each one must send a base version (`expectedUpdatedAt` / `expectedContentUpdatedAt` / `expectedVersion`) and must handle the server's refusal — because a precondition nobody reads the answer to is worse than none: the save fails, the draft is discarded as saved, and the owner is told nothing.
  - **Derived, never pinned.** There is no allowlist of known-good files to forget to update. A new surface is caught because it MATCHES, not because somebody registered it. The one exemption is `app/routes/design-*.tsx`, excluded by path: a design fixture posts to nothing, so there is no document a base version could be checked against.
  - **The detector is checked before what it detects.** One assertion pins that the scan still finds `MeetingMarkdown.tsx` and at least two surfaces in total — because a rename or a re-export that silently stopped the regexes matching would turn every other assertion green and vacuous. *A passing test that could never fail is not evidence*, and an inventory test is the shape most prone to becoming one.
  - **The server half is pinned too.** Three assertions hold `note-details.ts`, `meeting.ts` and `review.ts` to accepting the precondition, so the field the editors send cannot become one nobody checks.
  - **FALSIFIED BY EXACTLY THE ACT THE CLOSING CONDITION NAMES.** A fourth surface was written — `app/modules/notes/__FalsifyDoc.tsx`, a `LiveMarkdownEditor` bound to `useAutosaveField`, posting to `/notes/:id/mutate` with no base version and no conflict path, the shape F-01 actually had — and the test went **red on both assertions for that file** (`× app/modules/notes/__FalsifyDoc.tsx sends a base version with every save`, `× … handles the refusal rather than swallowing it`) without a line of the test being changed. The file was then deleted and the suite is green at 8 passed. That is the demonstration this entry asked for, rather than an inspection.
  - **What this does NOT claim.** It does not prove the three existing surfaces reconcile *correctly* — that is `useAutosaveField`'s own contract and [DEBT-47](#-debt-47--an-open-autosave-editor-does-not-adopt-a-server-side-change-to-its-field--p2--resolved-2026-08-20)'s, both already tested. It proves that a fourth surface cannot ship without one, which is the exact gap the entry was raised for.
- **Related finding.** [F-01](DALYHUB_WHOLE_APP_BUG_AUDIT_2026_08.md#f-01--a-meetings-agenda-and-notes-are-blind-last-write-wins-and-the-overwritten-text-exists-nowhere--p0). **Related roadmap item.** MEET-04; [`SHARED_FORMS.md`](../development/SHARED_FORMS.md).

### ☑ DEBT-175 — The Project record's Tasks tab is the last surface that does not render the shared `TaskRow` — P2 — **RESOLVED 2026-09-03 (V2.8 CONV-01)**

- **RESOLVED 2026-09-03 by [V2.8 CONV-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-01--the-project-record-renders-the-shared-task-row--delivered-2026-09-03).** `ProjectTasksTab.tsx` imports and renders the shared `TaskRow` inside the shared `TaskList`, over the shared list-item shape, hosted by the shared `useTaskSurfaceActions`, selected through the shared reducer and acted on in bulk through the shared `TaskBulkActionBar` (moved out of `TasksWorkspace.tsx` so `/tasks` and the tab render one bar over one `/tasks/bulk` contract). The comment at `:452` is gone with the Card-prop builder it sat in; `e2e/helpers.ts`'s `taskRows()` finds a Project's tasks and its exception comment is deleted. **The closing condition is met as written:** the shared row is the only task-row implementation on an actionable surface, and a fact added to it appears on all four with no per-surface change — asserted by `test/unit/task-record/shared-row-consumers.test.ts`, which enumerates the consumers (`/tasks`, Today, `/plan`, the Project tab) and proves each imports the row and the list. The measured delta of 2026-09-02 is closed item by item: overflow menu, inline title, selection with Shift-range, long-press, swipe, departure with focus handoff, recurrence signal, ADR-086 patch map, one bulk path, the shared container ladder (priority is on the row at 393 px). Drag is the one capability deliberately absent, through the row's own slot (no `dragHandle`; the scope draws no destination and stores no order — DEBT-188 stands), asserted rather than assumed. Statement budget pinned by `test/kernel/conv-01-project-tasks-budget.test.ts`: 3 per page before and after, plus one bounded parent-candidate read per record load; flat with task count. The UIX-01 Card override layer in `tasks.css` is untouched: `/today/waiting` still paints from it, and CONV-02 deletes it with that last consumer.

- **Current issue.** `app/modules/projects/ProjectTasksTab.tsx` builds `Card` props by hand. The only three importers of the shared `TaskRow` are `TasksWorkspace.tsx`, `PlanWorkspace.tsx` and `TodayScreen.tsx`. UIX-02 made the Project rows *"the SAME `Card` props Tasks builds"*, which was true then; DS-04 subsequently replaced the Tasks card with `TaskRow` and this tab did not follow. [DEBT-143](#-debt-143--todays-plan-draws-its-own-task-row-not-the-shared-taskrow--p2--resolved-2026-08-17-today-task-01) closed the same fork for Today.
- **Impact.** It is why F-09 was possible: the checklist figure was added to `TaskRow` and the Project tab, being a second implementation, simply did not have it — for the surface an owner works a Project FROM. [HARDEN-06E](DALYHUB_WHOLE_APP_REPAIR_2026_08.md) made the FIGURE correct (both Project task loaders read the same bounded aggregate, and the row draws it through the shared `checklistProgressLabel`), which closes the defect and not its cause. The next thing added to a Task row will be missing here again.
- **Why it was not done in the repair pass.** It is a real UI change to a record surface, with its own responsive, axe and screenshot consequences, and the audit's own slice plan says to split it out if it grows. Bundling a row redesign into a correctness pass is how a hardening branch stops being reviewable.
- **Desired future state.** `ProjectTasksTab` imports `TaskRow`, and `e2e/helpers.ts`'s `taskRows()` locator finds a Project's tasks too — at which point the comment there stops needing an exception.
- **Closing condition.** The shared row is the only task row implementation in the product, and a fact added to it appears on all four surfaces with no per-surface change.
- **What DHDS-10 did do, and did not.** It did not adopt the row — that is still this entry. It did close the two behaviours that had actually diverged: the tab's priority was a read-only `PriorityIndicator` while every other surface edited it inline (the comment beside it claimed otherwise), and its due-date field posted `set_due` and told the surface nothing, so the Project's health, its overdue counts and its progress band kept the answer they were loaded with until the next navigation. Both now use the shared control and report the accepted save. The cause is unchanged: the next fact added to `TaskRow` will still be missing here.
- **What [V2.4-GATE-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-v24-gate-02--honest-signals-on-a-task-row-and-one-day-on-a-phone--delivered-2026-08-25) did do, and did not (2026-08-25).** It did NOT adopt the row — that is still this entry, and the convergence stays with [DEBT-128](#-debt-128--today-projects-and-search-still-render-tasks-as-cards-so-one-object-has-two-anatomies--p2--resolved-2026-09-03-v28-conv-02), where the two should close together. What it did is make the tab answer the SAME semantic question as the row without forking it: the due date's urgency and the completion control's affordance both now come from the kernel's `isTaskStillOwed`, through the shared `InlineTaskDate` and the shared `taskUrgency` the tab already used. A cancelled Task's passed date reads here exactly as it does on `/tasks`, `/today` and `/plan`, and that is asserted by reading the painted colour on this surface (`e2e/gate-02-honest-signals.spec.ts`). **The cause is unchanged**, and this entry's own sentence still holds: the next fact added to `TaskRow` will be missing here again.
- **V2.5 disposition — NOT TAKEN.** Stays paired with [DEBT-128](#-debt-128--today-projects-and-search-still-render-tasks-as-cards-so-one-object-has-two-anatomies--p2--resolved-2026-09-03-v28-conv-02), whose V2.5 disposition records the reason; the two close together in their own bounded pass.
- **V2.8 disposition — TAKEN by [V2.8 CONV-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-01--the-project-record-renders-the-shared-task-row--delivered-2026-09-03) (2026-09-02).** Re-measured on `main` at `036d3da`: the comment at `ProjectTasksTab.tsx:452` still says *"does not render `TaskRow` yet"* (last touched `d87315c`); the importer count is now four (`TasksWorkspace`, `PlanWorkspace`, `TodayScreen`, `TaskDragging`) plus a module-private component ALSO named `TaskRow` in `OfflineSnapshotView.tsx:339`. The measured delta against the row: no overflow action menu, no inline title editor, no row selection or shift-range, no long-press, no swipe, no drag handle, no departure animation with focus handoff, no recurrence signal, a page re-fetch (`:184`) where `/tasks` uses ADR-086's patch map, its own bulk path (`postTaskBulkAction`, `:581`), and a second responsive ladder (`tasks.css:1657, 1738, 1818`) that below 26rem hides priority, repeat and waiting-for (`:1907-1913`, asserted hidden by `iphone-daily-driver.spec.ts:72`) — including the inline priority editor DHDS-10 added to this tab. Formatting is NOT duplicated (urgency, dates, blocked wording and the status triple are single-sourced); the fork is anatomy and interaction.
- **Related finding.** [F-09](DALYHUB_WHOLE_APP_BUG_AUDIT_2026_08.md#f-09--checklist-progress-is-missing-on-the-one-surface-where-the-steps-matter-most-and-the-projects-task-list-is-still-a-second-task-row--p2). **Related roadmap item.** DS-04; [DEBT-01](#-debt-01--duplicate-card-implementations-per-module--p2); [DHDS-10](../design/DHDS_10_INLINE_MANIPULATION_AND_DIRECT_EDITING_2026_08.md) §6.

### ☐ DEBT-176 — The non-secret half of notification settings and calendar sources leaves the export by TABLE rather than by COLUMN — P3

- **Current issue.** `notification_settings`, `notifications`, `notification_deliveries`, `calendar_sources`, `external_calendar_events` and `external_calendar_meeting_links` are absent from the workspace snapshot. Since [HARDEN-06E](DALYHUB_WHOLE_APP_REPAIR_2026_08.md) the omission is NAMED in `EXPORT_EXCLUSIONS` and documented in [`EXPORT_AND_PORTABILITY.md`](../development/EXPORT_AND_PORTABILITY.md), which is what F-10 was actually about — the silence, not the omission.
- **What is still owed.** Each of those tables holds something that genuinely must not be exported: Pushover credentials, a sealed feed URL, or an operational ledger. But the digest time and its zone, the per-source toggles and a calendar's display NAME are ordinary owner configuration of exactly the kind `owner_app_preferences` and the saved views are already exported as — and they are omitted only because they share a row with a secret. Omitting by column rather than by table would carry them.
- **Impact.** A restored workspace comes back with notifications off, the digest time and its zone gone, the per-source toggles gone and every subscribed calendar gone. The owner is now TOLD that, which is the difference between a documented limitation and a surprise; they still have to set it all up again.
- **Why it was not done in the repair pass.** It adds snapshot collections, which is a schema change with restore, validation and manifest consequences — and it is the same judgement [DEBT-94](#-debt-94--ai-preferences-are-the-one-kind-of-owner-configuration-the-export-snapshot-omits--p3--resolved-2026-08-25) records for AI preferences, which is still open on its own terms. Deciding both at once, deliberately, is better than deciding this one alone inside a bug-fix branch.
- **Desired future state.** Column-scoped export of the non-secret notification settings and calendar-source names, under `owner`, with the credential columns and the sealed URL omitted by name — resolved together with DEBT-94 so the product has ONE answer to "is configuration exported?".
- **Closing condition.** A restored workspace comes back with the owner's digest time, zone and per-source toggles, and their calendar subscriptions named (unauthenticated, awaiting re-entry of the feed URL) — or a recorded decision that it deliberately does not, consistent with DEBT-94.
- **Related finding.** [F-10](DALYHUB_WHOLE_APP_BUG_AUDIT_2026_08.md#f-10--notification-settings-the-notification-ledger-and-calendar-sources-leave-the-export-silently--p2). **Related roadmap item.** SET-02; NOTIFY-01; CAL-01.

### ☑ DEBT-177 — A completed row does not LEAVE; it disappears on the next revalidation — P3 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-21 ([DHDS-11](../design/DHDS_11_DRAG_REORDER_AND_OBJECT_CONTINUITY_2026_08.md))**

- **Current issue (was).** DHDS-08 shipped steps 1–4 and 6 of the canonical completion sequence (the control responds, the ink recedes, the strike draws, the Undo toast) and left steps 5–6 of the visual sequence — the row departing and its neighbours closing the gap — deliberately unimplemented, with two blockers written down: **focus** (the control the owner just clicked is inside the row about to go, and where it should land instead is an interaction decision `AGENTS.md` §15 forbids guessing at) and **the surfaces disagreeing about what completion means** (`/tasks` All-active removes the row; a Completed section keeps it; a Project's history keeps it forever).
- **Resolved by.** Both blockers were taken as decisions rather than worked around.

  **Which rows depart is not a per-surface flag.** A row departs when it ACTUALLY left — when an id the surface has just mutated is no longer in the list the loader answered with. A surface that keeps completed work produces no departure at all, because the row is still there; a surface that removes it produces exactly one. The animation therefore cannot disagree with what happened, because it is derived from what happened. A filter change, a page and a navigation remove rows too, and none of those is a departure: only ids the owner just acted on are eligible.

  **Focus goes to the row that takes this one's place** — the next live row's completion control, the previous one when there is no next, and the list itself (a named region, `tabIndex={-1}`) when the list is now empty. Never `<body>`. The rule is the one `TaskChecklistSection` already uses when a step is deleted, so it is a precedent rather than a guess.
- **How it is implemented.** [`use-departing-rows.ts`](../../app/shared/task-record/use-departing-rows.ts) derives the departure DURING RENDER and splices the row back at the index it held, so the DOM node is never removed and never moved — which is what makes the focus decision possible at all, and is why the leaving row is `aria-hidden` and pointer-inert rather than `inert` (`inert` blurs its subtree synchronously). `motion.css` collapses `block-size` at `--dh-motion-deliberate` on `--dh-ease-exit`: the third documented structural exception in that file, beside disclosure's `grid-template-rows` and progress's `inline-size`, and for the same reason.
- **Reduced motion.** No row is ever marked as leaving, so the collapse simply does not run — the row goes when the loader says it went, exactly as before. The focus handoff, which is not motion, still runs.
- **Verified by.** `test/unit/tasks/departing-rows.test.tsx` (which rows depart, which simply go, the three focus fallbacks, and a row that comes back cancelling its own exit) and `e2e/dhds-11-drag-reorder.spec.ts` Journey E.
- **Related roadmap item.** DHDS-11; [`DHDS_08_MOTION_AND_INTERACTION_GRAMMAR_2026_08.md`](../design/DHDS_08_MOTION_AND_INTERACTION_GRAMMAR_2026_08.md) §21.

### ☐ DEBT-178 — Focus-trapping panels cannot exit, because focus restoration is bound to unmount — P3

- **Current issue.** DHDS-08 published one exit grammar (`data-dh-exit`, `--dh-motion-exit`, `usePresence`) and the toast uses it. The Drawer, Inspector, Sheet and mobile navigation do not: `useDrawerFocus` (`app/shared/drawer/use-drawer-focus.ts`) restores focus to the opener in an **unmount-only** effect, so keeping a panel mounted for its 140ms exit would delay the focus restoration by the same 140ms.
- **Impact.** These four surfaces arrive with the shared grammar and vanish instantly. That is at least *faster* than their entrance, which is the direction DHDS-08 asks for, so nothing reads as broken — but the asymmetry is visible if you look for it, and the shared exit grammar has one consumer where it should have five.
- **Why it was not done in DHDS-08.** `AGENTS.md §15` and DHDS-08 §19 both require that motion never delay or obscure focus. Restoring focus 140ms after a panel closes is exactly that, and the fix is a change to the DS-03 focus contract — decoupling restoration from unmount so it fires when the panel becomes non-interactive rather than when it leaves the tree. That is a focus-management change with its own keyboard and axe consequences, not a motion one.
- **Desired future state.** `useDrawerFocus` restores on an explicit "closing" signal; the four panels take `usePresence`, mark themselves `data-dh-exit` and `inert`, and leave at `--dh-motion-exit` with focus already back on the opener.
- **Closing condition.** Closing a Drawer, an Inspector, a Sheet or the mobile navigation plays the mirrored exit; a keyboard user's focus is on the opener before the panel has finished fading; the existing drawer and inspector focus E2E coverage is unchanged and still passes.
- **Related roadmap item.** DS-03; DHDS-09 (floating surfaces); [`DHDS_08_MOTION_AND_INTERACTION_GRAMMAR_2026_08.md`](../design/DHDS_08_MOTION_AND_INTERACTION_GRAMMAR_2026_08.md) §21.

Read from the partitions' own `e2e-results-*` artefacts rather than from a log line: **1911 tests collected, 1911 executed, 0 failed, 0 flaky.** The three reported `skipped` are the three conditional guards [DEBT-200](#-debt-200--three-more-e2e-journeys-report-green-by-never-running-for-the-same-reason-debt-158-did--p2--resolved-2026-08-25) records, unchanged and pre-existing.

One `test.skip()` was REMOVED (DEBT-158's), so the suite executes more than it did, not less.

The failure set as actually measured on `main` at `054b98f` was **55 failures across 10 partitions, plus 5 tests that never executed** — recorded per partition, per spec, per mechanism in [the implementation record § 3.1–3.4](V2_4_GATE_01_RECOVERABLE_GREEN_RELEASED_2026_08.md).
- **The dominant signature was DHDS-13's, and it generalised.** Completing a Task files the row under a closed `Completed · n` `<details>`, so a re-assertion on the same locator resolves to nothing. Taken product-wide: the assertions now open the disclosure the product actually uses, or assert the OUTCOME rather than the projection. No completed Task was made to stay visible to satisfy Playwright.
- **One correction this entry owes its reader.** It classified `e2e/tasks-collection.spec.ts:298` as [DEBT-173](#-debt-173--e2e-specs-assert-against-the-shared-workspaces-accumulated-state-so-re-ordering-the-suite-changes-what-they-see--p2) — *"it passes in isolation and fails only when run after another spec, which is the accumulated-state signature"* — while warning, correctly, that *"only a mechanism can"* tell contamination from a regression. **That classification was wrong.** The mechanism is a real lost update in `CollectionControls`, reproduced deterministically in a browser and fixed at its authority; see [DEBT-159](#-debt-159--removing-two-filter-chips-in-quick-succession-can-put-one-of-them-back--p3). The entry's own warning was sound and its conclusion was not, which is worth more to the next reader than a silent edit.
- **The network-dependent Unit test is green**, in isolation and in the full suite, on #222's module-load fix. 6 399 unit and 2 849 kernel tests green.
- **What this does NOT close.** DEBT-173 (its closing condition needs two derived splits, not a green gate) and DEBT-159's genuine half. Both are recorded below with what changed.

Most share one signature: `locator.check()` clicks a task's completion checkbox, Playwright reports the click as performed, the checkbox never becomes checked, and `check()` retries to timeout. `main` additionally fails **Unit** — `test/kernel/calendar-security.test.ts:94` expects a promise to reject and it resolves, which is network-dependent.
- **Confirmed on `main` itself.** CI run 32409611083, on `main` at `157a3f4`, fails **exactly these nineteen** — the same list, test for test. That is independent of any local reproduction: the base branch's own gate is red on precisely this set.
- **How it was established as pre-existing.** DHDS-08 also reproduced **all nineteen** locally, by checking `app/` out at `157a3f4` and re-running each spec against the same reseeded database: all nineteen fail identically on the base tree. The four inside that phase's blast radius — `inline-editor-overlay` (the anchored reveal) and `today-task-convergence` (the completion grammar) — were checked first rather than last.
- **The set is NOT stable — it churns.** Four CI runs of the same branch produced **19, 19, 18 and 20** failures. Eighteen are constant; three tests move in and out — `tasks-collection.spec.ts:298` (fail, fail, **pass**, fail), and `identity.spec.ts:124` and `notes.spec.ts:382`, which appeared in one run only, on a commit that changes **two markdown files and nothing else**. Neither newcomer has a mechanism: every file implementing the Notes save-status/Retry control (`SaveStatusIndicator.tsx`, `use-autosave-field.ts`) and the entire colour-scheme path are untouched by that branch, `scheme:check` is green, and both specs pass locally against a fresh database (23/23). **They are left unclassified, deliberately.** `tasks-collection.spec.ts:298` *is* DEBT-173 — it passes in isolation and fails only when run after another spec, which is the accumulated-state signature. The other two are not: `notes.spec.ts:382` creates its own uniquely-titled Note before it does anything (`e2e/notes.spec.ts:385-386`), so "passes in isolation" says nothing about shared fixtures, and one failure in four runs is not a reproducer. Filing them under DEBT-173 would aim the next investigation at fixture isolation on no evidence. What is established is only this: **no mechanism in the branch, one occurrence, cause unknown.**
- **Impact.** Nineteen tests are not protecting what they were written to protect, several of them on the surfaces where completing a task matters most. Worse, the failure mode is indistinguishable from a real defect, so the next agent has to re-establish all of this from scratch — which is what this entry exists to prevent. **And because the set churns, "the failing set changed" cannot by itself distinguish a regression from contamination: only a mechanism can.**
- **Why it was not done in DHDS-08.** Diagnosing why an optimistic completion does not settle in these specific fixtures is a different investigation from a motion pass, and it is plausibly a case of [DEBT-173](#-debt-173--e2e-specs-assert-against-the-shared-workspaces-accumulated-state-so-re-ordering-the-suite-changes-what-they-see--p2) (specs asserting against the shared workspace's accumulated state) rather than a product defect at all. Bundling it in would have made a grammar branch unreviewable.
- **Desired future state.** Either the product defect is found and fixed, or the specs are made independent of accumulated workspace state — resolved together with DEBT-173, so the product has one answer to "why did this assertion fail?".
- **Closing condition.** All nineteen pass against a freshly seeded database and against the accumulated state a full gate run produces, and the set stops churning between runs of identical code.
- **Two that are NOT that signature, and were investigated separately.** `e2e/tasks-collection.spec.ts:298` **passes in isolation** (9.6s, freshly seeded) and **fails only when run after another spec** — on this branch and on `157a3f4` alike. That is DEBT-173's signature exactly rather than a filter defect, and is distinct from [DEBT-159](#-debt-159--removing-two-filter-chips-in-quick-succession-can-put-one-of-them-back--p3), which is a real ordering bug in the chips themselves. **Confirmed by observation, not just by reasoning:** two consecutive CI runs on the *same branch content* disagreed about it — it failed on `5aade13` and passed on `4d093f2`, with no change between them that touches filtering. A test whose result moves while the code does not is a test reading state it does not own. `e2e/plan-weekly-planning.spec.ts:233` is the row-reveal hit-testing gap, root-caused and recorded as DEBT-180.
- **Impact of leaving it.** With the gate red for unrelated reasons, a genuine regression in a future branch is invisible: it lands in a sea of expected red, and the only way to tell the difference is the base-tree comparison DHDS-08 had to run nineteen times by hand.
- **The dominant signature is now ROOT-CAUSED, by [DHDS-13](../design/DHDS_13_COMMERCIAL_QUALITY_GATE_2026_08.md) (2026-08-22), and it is not a product defect.** The completion checkbox *does* become checked. What happens next is that `TodayScreen` files the completed row under the plan's `Completed · n` disclosure, and that `<details>` renders **closed** — so the row leaves the accessibility tree while staying in the DOM, and `getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Reopen …" })` scoped to the plan resolves to **nothing**. `check()` re-resolves the locator to verify the new state, finds no element, and retries to timeout; a `toBeChecked()` written the same way reports "element(s) not found" while the page's own live region says *"Completed …"*. This is exactly the behaviour the entry above describes as "Playwright reports the click as performed, the checkbox never becomes checked" — the click was performed, and the checkbox is checked somewhere the assertion cannot see. **A specification that completes a task and then re-asserts on the same locator will fail for this reason on any surface with a collapsed completed group, no matter how long it waits.**
- **Three of the nineteen are fixed by that finding (19 → 16).** `today-task-convergence.spec.ts` :165 and :396 now assert where the product actually files the row, opening the disclosure by clicking its summary — no assertion weakened, no timeout raised. `iphone-daily-driver.spec.ts:279` was **not** this signature and **not** test debt at all: it was a real product defect (the Diary's phone week strip laid out in 254px instead of 288, giving seven 35px touch targets at 320), fixed in `diary.css` and recorded as DHDS-13's P2-11. Both were established as pre-existing by re-running against `origin/main` at `b31323c` on a re-seeded database, with byte-identical failure messages.
- **What this leaves for whoever takes this entry.** The remaining sixteen have not been re-checked against the mechanism above. `today.spec.ts` (4), `today-focus.spec.ts` (2), `tasks-collection.spec.ts`, `record-anatomy.spec.ts` and `goal-measurement.spec.ts` all complete a task and re-assert, so they are the first place to look; DHDS-13 deliberately did not widen a design gate into a sixteen-test suite repair, and says so in its own §17.
- **V2.4 disposition — TAKEN.** [V2.4-GATE-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-v24-gate-01--recoverable-green-released). Current evidence on `main`: CI run [`32482182727`](https://github.com/acedaly/DalyHub-V2/actions/runs/32482182727) at `b31323c` reports **Scope, Static, Unit and Build green and nine of twelve E2E partitions failed** (p02–p10; p01, p11 and p12 green). The sixteen remaining tests start from DHDS-13's root-caused mechanism, and the gate item forbids reaching green by skipping, weakening, quarantining or deleting any of them.
