### ◐ DEBT-204 — Every CI job re-downloads pnpm from the npm registry, so one truncated response turns the whole gate red — P2 — **mechanism fixed 2026-08-25; held open for the `main` run its own closing condition names**

- **Current issue.** [`.github/actions/setup`](../../.github/actions/setup/action.yml) runs `corepack enable` and then `actions/setup-node@v4` with `cache: pnpm`. To resolve the cache directory, `setup-node` executes `pnpm store path --silent`, and because `package.json` pins `packageManager`, **corepack downloads `pnpm-10.33.0.tgz` from `registry.npmjs.org` at that moment** — in **every** job, on every run. There is no retry, no pin to a runner-cached pnpm, and no fallback.
- **MEASURED on `main`, and it cost the gate a green run.** CI run [`32710624636`](https://github.com/acedaly/DalyHub-V2/actions/runs/32710624636) (run 743) at `f2b504b`, a **documentation-only** commit. Job **E2E p07** failed **11 seconds after it started**, inside `Set up toolchain`:

  ```
  ! Corepack is about to download https://registry.npmjs.org/pnpm/-/pnpm-10.33.0.tgz
  node:internal/assert/utils:77
  AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: The expression evaluated to a falsy value:
    assert(!this.paused)
      at Parser.finish (node:internal/deps/undici/undici:6165:9)
      at TLSSocket.<anonymous> (node:internal/deps/undici/undici:6499:36)
  ```

  The HTTP response was truncated mid-stream and Node's bundled undici crashed on it. `Install dependencies` was `skipped`, Playwright never started, and `scripts/e2e-partition-summary.mjs` correctly refused to read the absence of a `results.json` as an absence of failures — *"treat it as a failed partition, not as an absence of failures"*. **The other eleven partitions ran the identical action on the identical commit and passed.**
- **The gate behaved CORRECTLY, and that is why this is P2 rather than P1.** Nothing here reported a false green; the summary script is the reason the run went red instead of quietly reporting eleven partitions as twelve. The defect is in the **toolchain step**, not in the gate's honesty.
- **Impact, stated precisely.** It is a **fan-out** problem. Sixteen jobs each make the same network call, so the chance that at least one fails is roughly sixteen times the per-call failure rate, and **any single one of them turns the whole run red**. That lands directly on [V2.4-GATE-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-v24-gate-01--recoverable-green-released)'s criterion 3, which asks for *"green on `main` for two consecutive pushes"*: run 743 was the candidate second, and it was lost to a registry hiccup on a commit that changed only prose. It is **not** [DEBT-203](#-debt-203--the-e2e-suite-carries-latent-timing-races-at-roughly-one-per-two-runs-so-green-is-probabilistic--p2) — that entry is about assertions inside the suite; this one never reached a test.
- **Desired future state.** The pnpm binary is obtained once per run, or from a cache, or with a bounded retry — so a transient registry response costs a few seconds rather than a partition. Candidate directions, none of them chosen here: `corepack prepare --activate` wrapped in a retry inside the composite action; caching corepack's download directory alongside the pnpm store; or `pnpm/action-setup` ahead of `setup-node`, which fetches pnpm before the cache probe needs it.
- **Why V2.4-GATE-01 did not fix it.** It was a release-evidence pass with no source change in it, and the fix edits the machinery **every** job depends on — the wrong thing to change without a full gate run behind it, at a release boundary, in a PR whose whole point is that it touches nothing executable. Recorded with its measurement so the next agent starts from the log line rather than from a rediscovery.
- **MECHANISM FIXED 2026-08-25 by the [all-open-debt pass](PRODUCT_DEBT_CLOSURE_2026_08.md), by the first of the three directions this entry lists.** [`.github/actions/setup`](../../.github/actions/setup/action.yml) now materialises pnpm in a step of its own — `corepack prepare --activate`, three attempts, 5s then 10s backoff — **before** `actions/setup-node` runs. The ordering is the substance, not the retry: `setup-node`'s `cache: pnpm` probe is what used to trigger the download, inside a step this repository does not own and cannot wrap. By the time it runs, pnpm is already on disk, so that call cannot reach the network at all.
  - **It is a bounded retry, not a generic one.** `set -euo pipefail`; the third failure prints `::error::corepack could not obtain the pinned pnpm after 3 attempts.` and exits 1. A genuinely unreachable registry still fails the job, loudly, at the step that owns the problem. Nothing is swallowed, no test is retried, and the retry covers exactly one command.
  - **Falsified by execution, not by reading.** The script was run twice against a stubbed `corepack` on `PATH`: with two simulated truncations followed by a success it printed `pnpm 10.33.0 ready (attempt 3)` and exited 0; with every attempt failing it printed the `::error::` line and exited 1. The previous action had no loop to run.
  - **The property is pinned so an edit cannot quietly undo it.** [`test/unit/ci/toolchain-setup.test.ts`](../../test/unit/ci/toolchain-setup.test.ts) asserts the ORDER (the prepare step precedes `actions/setup-node`), the RETRY (a bounded loop, a backoff, and no unbounded `while true`), the LOUD FAILURE (`::error::`, `exit 1`, `set -euo pipefail`), that the action's own description states the mechanism, and that no workflow sets up the toolchain itself instead of calling this action. All five fail against the previous action.yml — the first because there was no prepare step to precede anything.
- **Why it stays ◐ rather than ☑, and this is the honest half.** The closing condition asks for *"a gate run in which no job fails before `Install dependencies`"*. That run can only happen on `main`, after this merges — the failure it guards against is a per-job network fetch on GitHub's runners, which this repository cannot observe from here. The MECHANISM is fixed and pinned; the DEMONSTRATION is owed. Claiming it now would be claiming production evidence this pass does not possess, which is the thing [DEBT-198](#-debt-198--the-off-cloudflare-encrypted-backup-has-never-been-produced-because-the-github-production-environment-holds-no-secrets--p2) and [DEBT-199](#-debt-199--a-d1-dump-cannot-be-restored-by-the-command-the-recovery-documentation-gave-and-whether-the-remote-path-is-affected-is-unmeasured--p1--resolved-2026-08-30) exist to prevent.
  - **What closes it.** One `main` gate run after this merges in which all sixteen jobs reach `Install dependencies`. No further repository change is required, and none should be made: if a job still fails in `Set up toolchain`, the log line will name a different cause and this entry should be re-opened against that cause rather than re-patched against this one.
- **Closing condition.** The setup action obtains pnpm without an unretried network fetch per job, demonstrated by a gate run in which no job fails before `Install dependencies`; and the mechanism is stated in the action's own description so a future edit does not reintroduce it. **First half met 2026-08-25** (above, with the description carrying it and a test pinning it); second half outstanding, and outstanding for a reason that is not a repository change.
- **Related roadmap item.** [V2.4-GATE-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-v24-gate-01--recoverable-green-released); [DEBT-157](#-debt-157--the-e2e-partition-durations-can-only-be-refreshed-from-a-failing-run--p1-re-rated-2026-08-20-mechanism-closed-by-harden-06a-the-same-day-held-open-for-its-confirming-run); [DEBT-203](#-debt-203--the-e2e-suite-carries-latent-timing-races-at-roughly-one-per-two-runs-so-green-is-probabilistic--p2).

### ☑ DEBT-205 — 536 seconds of E2E gate capacity is stranded, because a sliced spec file takes its partitions exclusively — P2 — **RESOLVED 2026-09-04 (V2.8 CONV-03)**

- **Current issue.** `derivePartitions` (`scripts/e2e-partitions.mjs`) gives a spec file bigger than one partition's share of the work its OWN partitions, divided by Playwright's `--shard`, and nothing else may share them. `e2e/responsive.spec.ts` is **1471.6 s in one generated matrix file** — `--shard` is the only way to divide it — so it takes **two exclusive partitions of 735.8 s apiece** against a derived ceiling of 1004 s.
- **The measurement.** 2 × (1004 − 735.8) = **536 s, 8.9 minutes, of gate capacity that no partition can use** — 4.7% of a 192-minute suite, permanently. Every other partition sits at ~1005 s, hard against the ceiling, while these two sit at 73% of it. Measured over the committed durations at [V2.4 FOLLOW-01](V2_4_FOLLOW_01_WEEK_ACCOUNT_2026_08.md), 2026-08-26.
- **Impact.** It is why the twelve-partition split looked exhausted. V2.4-GATE-02 could not fit its own coverage without making a spec genuinely cheaper; FOLLOW-01 could not fit four tests at all and raised `PARTITION_COUNT` to thirteen — which costs ~2.3 min of extra runner setup and puts the gate one job past the pool figure interpolated from run 31445526789. Both were paying for capacity that already exists and cannot be reached. It compounds: the next item to add coverage faces the same wall a partition earlier.
- **Desired future state.** One of two, and the choice is the decision this entry exists to put:
  1. **Let a sliced group carry whole spec files.** Every shard of the group must run an **IDENTICAL** spec list, or `--shard` loses and duplicates tests — so the packer assigns extra files to the GROUP, and each shard runs `playwright test <group specs> --shard=i/N`. Recovers the whole 536 s. Changes what every partition holds, and splits those extra files' tests across two jobs, which needs checking against the specs that mutate owner-level state (`owner-timezone.spec.ts`, `appearance.spec.ts`).
  2. **Split `responsive.spec.ts` near 50/50 into two real spec files** — by viewport tier is the natural seam, since every test in it is an independent `goto` + overflow check with no shared fixture. Two ~736 s files then fall BELOW the target and are packed like any other file, needing no change to the algorithm at all. Both halves must be measured before the manifest is regenerated.
- **Why V2.4 FOLLOW-01 did not fix it.** It edits the machinery **every** job depends on, and the only honest validation is a full gate run. That is the wrong change to make inside a feature PR whose own coverage is four tests — the same reasoning V2.4-GATE-01 recorded for [DEBT-204](#-debt-204--every-ci-job-re-downloads-pnpm-from-the-npm-registry-so-one-truncated-response-turns-the-whole-gate-red--p2--mechanism-fixed-2026-08-25-held-open-for-the-main-run-its-own-closing-condition-names). Recorded with its numbers so the next pass takes it deliberately rather than rediscovering it.
- **PRESERVED 2026-08-27 by [V2.4 FOLLOW-02](V2_4_FOLLOW_02_GOAL_MOVEMENT_2026_08.md), and deliberately NOT taken — because it did not have to be.** FOLLOW-01 warned that *"the next item that adds E2E coverage will have to answer that question rather than shave seconds"*. The answer turned out to be that the coverage fits: `follow-02-goal-movement.spec.ts` is **18.7 s over 2 tests** (measured locally from a green run, `--as local/v2.4-follow-02`), `PARTITION_COUNT` is **unchanged at 13**, the ceiling was not touched, and the heaviest partition is **15.3 min against 16.7 min** with `worst/mean` 1.04.

  The coverage was sized to fit rather than the gate resized to hold it: 2 tests over **5 page LOADS**, with every other width and appearance a resize or an `emulateMedia` in place, and ONE axe scan per appearance on the meaningful new state rather than one per width.

  **So the numbers in this entry are unchanged and still true**: 536 s is still stranded in the two exclusive `responsive.spec.ts` shards, and the next item that genuinely needs that capacity still faces the same wall. Taking it here would have meant editing `derivePartitions` — machinery every job depends on, whose only honest validation is a full gate run — inside a feature branch whose own coverage is two tests. That is the same reasoning FOLLOW-01 recorded, and it is unchanged.
- **Closing condition.** The heaviest partition's budget and the LIGHTEST partition's budget are within one ceiling of each other — no partition is budgeted below ~70% of `MAX_PARTITION_SECONDS` while another sits at 100% — with the split derived, `pnpm run e2e:partitions:check` green, and a `main` gate run in which every partition executes every test it collects. If direction (1) is taken, a test asserting that a sliced group's shards carry identical spec lists closes the correctness half.
- **V2.8 disposition — TAKEN by [V2.8 CONV-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-03--green-is-a-property-not-a-lottery--delivered-2026-09-04-less-one-owner-held-measurement), option 2 (2026-09-02).** Re-confirmed on the committed manifest: p12/p13 are `responsive.spec.ts` alone (`--shard=1/2`, `2/2`) at 12.3 min each while p01–p11 sit at 15.9–16.1; `partitionCount` is 13. The split lands with CONV-03 because its only honest validation — a full gate — is that item's own.
- **RESOLVED 2026-09-04 by [V2.8 CONV-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-03--green-is-a-property-not-a-lottery--delivered-2026-09-04-less-one-owner-held-measurement), by this entry's own option 2 — the file was split, the packer was not.**
  - **Re-measured on `main` first rather than trusted.** The committed manifest at `7c52987` still said what this entry says: `e2e/responsive.spec.ts` **1471.5 s over 519 tests**, p12 and p13 running it alone at `--shard=1/2` and `2/2` for **735.8 s (73% of the 1004 s ceiling)** while p01–p11 sat at **974–976 s (97%)**. 2 × (1004 − 735.8) = **536 s**. The numbers had not moved.
  - **The split, and the seam it was chosen on.** `responsive-phone.spec.ts` takes the phone tiers (320, 375, 390, 430 and the 844×390 landscape) plus the narrow overlay extreme and the mobile navigation sheet — **248 tests**; `responsive-desktop.spec.ts` takes 768, 1024, 1280, 1440 and 2560 plus the POLISH-01 audit band and the wide overlay extreme — **271 tests**. The routes, the twelve overlay scenarios and every test TITLE live in `e2e/responsive-matrix.ts` and are shared, so the split is a change of which file declares a test and of nothing else. **248 + 271 = 519, and the two files' test titles are identical as a SET to the file they replace** — compared by listing all three and diffing, not by inspection. `PHONE_VIEWPORTS ++ WIDE_VIEWPORTS === RESPONSIVE_VIEWPORTS` is asserted in [`test/unit/ci/responsive-matrix.test.ts`](../../test/unit/ci/responsive-matrix.test.ts), so a viewport cannot leave the product's canonical matrix by leaving a tier, and the same test fails if either tier file stops sweeping its tier, if the audit band or either overlay extreme goes missing, or if the retired file comes back.
  - **The measurement, before and after.** The two halves were measured together on a clean seed — 519 passed, 496.0 s and 569.6 s of test time — and normalised to the CI-measured total of the file they replace (×1.381, the ratio this machine runs the identical 519 tests at), so the manifest keeps the magnitude CI measured and takes only the RATIO from the local run. Re-derived through `pnpm run e2e:partitions:generate`:

    | | spec files | partitions | heaviest | lightest | `worst/mean` | stranded |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | before | 133 | 13, two of them `--shard` slices | 16.3 min · **97%** | 12.3 min · **73%** | 1.33 (utilisation) | **536 s** |
    | after | 134 | 13, **none** sliced | 15.7 min · **94%** | 15.5 min · **93%** | **1.00** | **0 s** |

  - **Thirteen was KEPT because the arithmetic keeps it, not to preserve history.** Derived over the same durations at each count: **11 →** 18.49 min, **12 →** 16.95 min — both over the 16.73 min `MAX_PARTITION_SECONDS` — **13 →** 15.68 min, **14 →** 14.54 min. Thirteen is still the smallest count that fits, because the split changed how the suite's 203.0 min is distributed and not how much of it there is. The ceiling was not touched, and `PARTITION_COUNT` was not touched.
  - **The condition is now a CHECK rather than a memory.** `manifestProblems` fails when the heaviest partition is at or above 90% of the ceiling while any partition sits more than 15% of a ceiling below it (`PARTITION_PRESSURE_THRESHOLD`, `PARTITION_SPREAD_TOLERANCE` — a quarter of the slack the ceiling already carries, so it is a real bound rather than a restatement of it). **Falsified against the state it was written for**: run over the pre-split committed manifest it reports *"the split strands capacity: the heaviest partition is budgeted 16.3 min (97% of the 16.7 min ceiling) while p12, p13 sits at 12.3 min (73%) — a spread of 24% of the ceiling against the 15% this split allows"*, and over the new manifest it is silent. `pnpm run e2e:partitions:check` is green: *"134 spec files across 13 partitions, heaviest 15.7 min"*.
  - **Closing condition, clause by clause.** The heaviest and lightest budgets are within one ceiling of each other (15.7 and 15.5 min, a 0.2 min spread against a 16.7 min ceiling); no partition is below ~70% of the ceiling while another is at 100%; the split is derived, not written; `e2e:partitions:check` is green; and every partition executes every test it collects on the gate run recorded on the roadmap item. Direction (1) was not taken, so its correctness half does not apply — **there is no sliced group left to assert about**, which is the stronger form of the same guarantee.
  - **What this did NOT do.** No test was deleted, weakened, skipped or duplicated; no journey was rewritten; `derivePartitions` is byte-for-byte the same function it was, and its slicing branch remains for the day a single spec file outgrows a partition again.
- **Related roadmap item.** [V2.4-GATE-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-v24-gate-02--honest-signals-on-a-task-row-and-one-day-on-a-phone--delivered-2026-08-25) (which shaved a spec to fit); [FOLLOW-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_4.md#-follow-01--did-the-week-hold--delivered-2026-08-26) (which raised the count and measured this); [DEBT-157](#-debt-157--the-e2e-partition-durations-can-only-be-refreshed-from-a-failing-run--p1-re-rated-2026-08-20-mechanism-closed-by-harden-06a-the-same-day-held-open-for-its-confirming-run).

## Debt raised by the V2.5 roadmap decision (2026-08-27)

Six entries from the Goal-experience audit taken on `main` at `0610c92`
(FOLLOW-02 merged) — the audit [`ROADMAP_V2_5.md`](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md)
is built on. A roadmap pass closes no debt; each entry below is raised with the
item that takes it already named, so none of them is a finding without a home.

### ☑ DEBT-206 — An Area's Goals tab draws a third Goal progress that no other surface has — P2

- **Current issue.** The Area record's Goals tab builds its Goal cards by hand
  ([`app/modules/areas/AreaOverview.tsx`](../../app/modules/areas/AreaOverview.tsx), the Goal-card builder around lines 109–172):
  each card's progress bar is the **Task roll-up** (`taskCompleted / taskTotal`
  from the spine rollup), with metadata `Projects: X of Y complete` and a target
  date. No other surface in the product presents a Goal this way — Today and
  `/goals` lead with the GOAL-02 **measurement**, and the Goal record's summary
  band draws **Project contribution** — and the Area card carries no alignment
  state, no movement sentence and no measurement at all, though all three
  derivations exist and are batched reads away.
- **Impact.** The same Goal reads *"53% · Ahead"* on Today and an unrelated
  task-count percentage on its own Area's record, with nothing on either surface
  saying they are different questions. That is the defect class V2.4-GATE-02
  closed for Task rows — a surface saying something about a record that the rest
  of the product contradicts — one level up the spine, on the two surfaces an
  owner reaches a Goal from most often.
- **Desired future state.** The Area record's Goals tab tells the same story
  every other surface tells, through `~/shared/goal-progress` and
  `~/shared/alignment`: the measurement (or its honest absence), the movement
  sentence, the alignment word. The Task roll-up remains available as a rollup
  **fact**, worded as what it is, never presented as the Goal's progress.
- **Closing condition.** The Area tab's per-Goal facts equal the `/goals` row's
  for the same Goal, asserted by machine key as equal values (the FOLLOW-02
  parity method) — and no surface in the product renders a Goal progress figure
  not derived from the shared evaluators, asserted by enumeration.
- **Related roadmap item.** [STEER-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-03--one-goal-one-story--delivered-2026-08-28);
  [ADR-111](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-111-steering--owner-judgement-is-stored-beside-derived-signals-never-merged--one-next-action-rule-one-goal-story-and-a-collection-order-that-answers-a-recorded-question) decision 6.
- **RESOLVED 2026-08-28 by V2.5 STEER-03, against this entry's own closing condition, both clauses.**
  - **The Area tab renders the SAME component `/goals` renders** — `GoalStoryRow` ([`app/shared/goal-progress/GoalStoryRow.tsx`](../../app/shared/goal-progress/GoalStoryRow.tsx)), from the SAME shared evaluators, so there is no second composition left to drift. Not a card that resembles the row: the row.
  - **Clause one, met by machine key.** Every Goal row on every surface stamps `goalStoryDataAttributes` — the story's facts as `data-goal-*`, from one projection — and [`test/kernel/goal-story.test.ts`](../../test/kernel/goal-story.test.ts) drives the REAL `/goals`, Area-record and guided-Review loaders over one seeded workspace and asserts equality for a measured Goal, an unmeasured one, a configured-but-unstarted one and a set-aside one. The FOLLOW-02 parity method, not a comparison of sentences.
  - **Clause two, met by enumeration.** [`test/unit/goals/goal-progress-renderings.test.ts`](../../test/unit/goals/goal-progress-renderings.test.ts) lists every Goal-progress rendering in the product with the shared authority it must reach the figure through, AND scans every component for the shape of one — so a new rendering that is not declared fails a build rather than an audit. `goalProgressMeter` became the ONE Goal meter in the process: the Projects page's Goal rail was assembling the same three values inline, which is how a fourth interpretation starts.
  - **The roll-up is kept and reworded, not deleted.** The Projects and Tasks counts are real structural facts and an Area record is where structure is read, so they survive on the row's context line as counts of Projects and Tasks. What they stopped being is the Goal's progress answer. `AreaOverview.test.tsx` asserts all three halves: the "Task roll-up" caption is gone, the meter reads the GOAL's 60% rather than the roll-up's 50%, and an unmeasured Goal gets no bar at all.
  - **Falsified.** Restoring the roll-up bar breaks the cross-surface parity test, the Area unit test and the enumeration's negative rule — three independent guards, which is what a defect this cheap to reintroduce needs.

### ☑ DEBT-207 — `/goals` loads three reads it never renders — P3 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-28 (V2.5 STEER-01)**

- **Current issue.** REDESIGN-04 replaced the Goals gallery card with the
  master–detail workspace, and three reads the card consumed were left in the
  loaders. The collection route still loads a **sparkline series** per page
  (`listMeasurementSeries`, [`app/modules/goals/routes/index.tsx`](../../app/modules/goals/routes/index.tsx)
  around lines 270–282, with `GOAL_CARD_SPARKLINE_POINTS` still documenting "a
  gallery card's sparkline") and each Goal's **definition of done** (same file,
  ~lines 340–342); the workspace pane's loader reads up to five **alignment
  evidence** rows ([`goal-workspace-load.ts`](../../app/modules/goals/goal-workspace-load.ts)
  ~lines 93–96). None of the three is rendered anywhere on the surface.
- **Impact.** Dead work on one of the product's most-visited collections — rows
  transferred and typed on every page and every revalidation for nothing — and a
  trap for the next author, who will reasonably assume a loaded field is shown
  somewhere and keep it in step.
- **Desired future state.** The route loads exactly what the decided
  presentation renders: each of the three reads is either consumed by
  [STEER-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-01--what-goals-answers--delivered-2026-08-28)'s decided
  surface or removed with its plumbing.
- **Closing condition.** An assertion over the loader's returned shape that
  every field it carries has a renderer, and the route's statement budget
  restated after the removal.
- **Related roadmap item.** [STEER-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-01--what-goals-answers--delivered-2026-08-28).
- **RESOLVED 2026-08-28 by STEER-01. All three reads are removed with their plumbing**, because the decided presentation renders none of them:
  - the **sparkline series** (`listMeasurementSeries`, twelve readings per Goal on every page and every revalidation) — the gallery card that drew it was deleted by REDESIGN-04; the record and the pane plot the full history from their own `listMeasurements(goalId)`, which is a DIFFERENT read, so this removal costs the surface nothing. The repository method survives with its own tests and now has **no caller at all**, raised as **DEBT-212** rather than deleted from a route change;
  - the collection item's **definition of done** — the `ProgressRow` has no room for prose;
  - the workspace pane's five **alignment-evidence** rows — the pane renders the alignment INDICATOR; the evidence panel lives on the canonical record, which makes that read there.
- **Closing condition met.** [`test/kernel/goals-outcome-route.test.ts`](../../test/kernel/goals-outcome-route.test.ts) asserts the loader's returned shape field by field against an explicit list of what renders each one, so a field added without a renderer fails a test rather than an audit.
- **The budget, restated.** The `/goals` composition made EIGHT grouped reads per page and still makes eight: the ordered page, six reads over that page's ids (contributions, alignment facts, measurement summaries, milestone summaries, details, movement) and one workspace-wide read. What changed is *which* eight — the series read removed, the workspace lens counts added in its place — and the selected Goal's detail is one read lighter. In statements the page read costs two (a bounded preliminary resolving each Goal's schedule origin in the owner's calendar, which SQLite cannot compute) and the counts cost two, both asserted flat in the number of Goals against a counting database. Every read is grouped over the page's ids or the whole workspace; none is per Goal.

### ☑ DEBT-208 — The same Goal wears two identity marks on one screen — P3 — **RESOLVED 2026-08-28 (V2.5 STEER-01)**

- **Current issue.** The `/goals` row resolves the Goal's **own** icon and
  colour first, falling back to its Area's
  ([`app/modules/goals/GoalWorkspace.tsx`](../../app/modules/goals/GoalWorkspace.tsx)
  ~lines 148–162); the detail pane beside it renders **only the Area's**
  identity ([`GoalWorkspacePane.tsx`](../../app/modules/goals/GoalWorkspacePane.tsx)
  ~lines 146–153). A Goal given its own appearance through the record's
  `EntityIdentityPicker` (IDENTITY-01, migration `0042`) therefore shows one
  mark in the list and a different mark in the pane describing the same record,
  side by side.
- **Impact.** Small and corrosive: identity is how the owner recognises a record
  at a glance, and the two-mark state quietly teaches that the mark means
  nothing.
- **Desired future state.** One identity-resolution rule — the Goal's own
  identity where set, the Area's where not — applied by every Goal surface from
  one helper.
- **Closing condition.** The row and the pane resolve the same mark for the same
  Goal, asserted on a Goal with its own identity and one that inherits its
  Area's.
- **Related roadmap item.** [STEER-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-01--what-goals-answers--delivered-2026-08-28).
- **RESOLVED 2026-08-28 by STEER-01, exactly as the desired future state describes it.** `goalIdentitySource` / `resolveGoalIdentity` ([`goal-view.ts`](../../app/modules/goals/goal-view.ts)) state what a GOAL feeds into the shared `resolveIdentity` ladder — its own choice first, its Area's otherwise, colour and glyph walked independently, `colourRank: null` because a Goal has no rank of its own — and the row, the pane and the record all consume it. The pane used to resolve only the Area's identity; it now takes the resolved source as a prop, so the two surfaces cannot resolve differently rather than merely happening to agree.
- **Closing condition met**, both cases, by reading the same machine value from both surfaces rather than comparing what was drawn: [`goals-outcome-route.test.ts`](../../test/kernel/goals-outcome-route.test.ts) asserts it for a Goal with its own `pink`/`running` identity and for one that inherits its Area's.

### ☑ DEBT-209 — The Review's Goals step is blind to measurement and movement — P3

- **Current issue.** The guided weekly Review's *Goals and Areas* step shows,

  (measurement) reach Today's glance and never reach the ritual that exists to
  ask whether action matched intention.
- **Impact.** The owner steers the week from less information in the Review than
  they get from a glance at Today — a Goal that is behind its own target date or
  that moved substantially this week reads identically to one that is neither,
  in the one sitting dedicated to noticing.
- **Desired future state.** The step states each Goal's measurement status and
  its movement beside its alignment, from the shared evaluators, inside a
  stated, asserted statement budget (the FOLLOW-01 precedent: a budget moves by
  being stated, never absorbed).
- **Closing condition.** The step renders measurement status and movement per
  Goal from the shared vocabulary; the step's statement budget is asserted and
  flat in the number of Goals; ADR-110 decision 5 holds on the new facts (a
  future window is never described as unmoved).
- **Related roadmap item.** [STEER-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-03--one-goal-one-story--delivered-2026-08-28).
- **RESOLVED 2026-08-28 by V2.5 STEER-03, against this entry's own closing condition, all three clauses.**
  - **The step states measurement status and movement per Goal from the shared vocabulary** — and, because STEER-02 shipped first, the owner's CONDITION and the target date with it, so one propagation carried the whole story. Every value comes from `loadGoalStories` ([`goal-story-load.server.ts`](../../app/shared/goal-progress/goal-story-load.server.ts)), the same composition the Area record makes; the movement read is FOLLOW-02's ONE server read, reached exactly as `/goals` reaches it, not a second path.
  - **The budget is asserted and flat.** `REVIEW_GUIDE_QUERY_BUDGET.alignment` moved from **6 to 12**, STATED rather than absorbed — the FOLLOW-01 precedent, whose own rule this entry cites. Two of the previous six moved INSIDE the shared composition rather than being added, so the arithmetic is 6 − 2 + 8. `review-guide-context.test.ts` pins the number and proves it flat over a three-Goal and a ten-Goal workspace; `goal-story.test.ts` pins it again from the other side.
  - **ADR-110 decision 5 holds by construction.** The step renders `GoalMovementLine` from `evaluateGoalMovement`'s own output, so a future window is never described as unmoved — the sentence is the evaluator's, not the step's.
  - **The step is otherwise unchanged**, deliberately: same shape, same place, same SELECTION (`listGoalsByAlignment` still decides which Goals appear, because alignment is the question this step asks), and no next action — STEER-04 left the Review's bounded scan exactly as it was. It remains a reflection surface.
  - **A set-aside Goal is now distinguishable from a neglected one IN THE RITUAL**, which is the half of STEER-02's problem that would otherwise have survived it.

### ☑ DEBT-210 — A Goal signal names no next step, and a structureless Goal offers no way to create one — P3

- **Current issue.** Every Goal surface reports and none acts. The record's
  *Recent contribution* panel lists past evidence; nothing anywhere names the
  **next** actionable Task under the Goal's contributing Projects.
  `GoalProjectChips`'s *"+ Link project"* only re-parents an **existing**
  Project ([`app/modules/goals/GoalProjectChips.tsx`](../../app/modules/goals/GoalProjectChips.tsx)),
  the Projects tab's empty state names a path that does not exist from here —
  *"Projects created for this Goal appear here."*, with no way to create one
  ([`GoalProjectsTab.tsx`](../../app/modules/goals/GoalProjectsTab.tsx), the
  `EmptyState` around line 249),
  and the `no_structure` alignment state — *"this Goal was never given a
  path"* — is a diagnosis with no remedy on the surface that makes it, though a
  Goal has been a valid, server-resolved Project parent since AREA-02.
- **Impact.** The distance from "this Goal needs me" to doing anything about it
  is a research task: open the Goal, open a Project, find a Task — or leave to
  `/projects/new` and re-find the parent. On the layer whose entire purpose is
  connecting intention to action, the last step of the connection is missing.
- **Desired future state.** A Goal's record and pane name the next step across
  its contributing Projects — through the product's ONE next-action rule
  ([DEBT-77](#-debt-77--a-project-card-cannot-say-what-the-next-action-is--p3--resolved-2026-08-28-v25-steer-04)'s
  rule, never a second one) — with REVIEW-02's honest absence where nothing is
  visible; and the no-structure state offers *"New Project for this Goal"*,
  landing on the existing `/projects/new` with the parent preselected and
  server-verified. Never a Task created on a Goal — the spine forbids it.
- **Closing condition.** From a Goal in the no-structure state, the owner
  creates a contributing Project without re-finding the Goal, and the new
  Project's first completed Task moves the Goal's movement line — proven end to
  end. A Goal with structure names its next step under the same ordering
  `/tasks` uses, asserted.
- **Related roadmap item.** [STEER-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-04--from-signal-to-step--delivered-2026-08-28);
  [ADR-111](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-111-steering--owner-judgement-is-stored-beside-derived-signals-never-merged--one-next-action-rule-one-goal-story-and-a-collection-order-that-answers-a-recorded-question) decision 4.
- **RESOLVED 2026-08-28 by V2.5 STEER-04, against this entry's own closing condition, both halves — proven end to end.**
  - **"From a Goal in the no-structure state, the owner creates a contributing Project without re-finding the Goal, and the new Project's first completed Task moves the Goal's movement line."** [`test/kernel/goal-next-action.test.ts`](../../test/kernel/goal-next-action.test.ts) does exactly that against real D1: it posts through `POST /projects/new` with the Goal as parent, reads the Goal's record loader again and finds the Project in its contributing structure with `project.advances_goal` parentage, creates a Task under it, and completes it — after which `movement.moved` is true. `steer-goal-story.spec.ts` walks the same loop through the browser, including that the door disappears once the structural absence it answered is gone.
  - **"A Goal with structure names its next step under the same ordering `/tasks` uses, asserted."** The rule is stated once in [`~/kernel/tasks/next-action`](../../app/kernel/tasks/next-action.ts) and evaluated by `TaskRepository.listProjectNextActions`; a parity test proves the repository's answer equals the FIRST row the canonical `/tasks` collection read returns for the same Project under the same view, sort and filters.
  - **The Goal level is a COMPOSITION, not a second model.** Goal → contributing Projects → each Project's canonical next action → the best of those by the same comparator, with the Task id as the final tiebreak, so a Goal with several Projects selects predictably across reloads.
  - **Never a Task on a Goal.** The creation door makes a PROJECT, which is what the spine allows (`AGENTS.md` §4). Nothing is created automatically.
  - **The door is a door, not a flow.** It opens the ONE shared `NewProjectForm` (moved to `app/shared/project-creation/`, re-exported from the Projects module so no call site changed) with the Goal as its decided parent; the server still resolves the parent's KIND from the id and re-verifies the workspace, so a cross-workspace parent fails closed — asserted.

### ☐ DEBT-212 — `listMeasurementSeries` has no caller — P3

- **Current issue.** [`listMeasurementSeries`](../../app/kernel/goals/goal-measurement-repository.ts)
  is a bounded multi-Goal read — up to *N* readings per Goal for a set of ids,
  in one statement — implemented over D1 and covered by five tests in
  [`test/kernel/goal-measurements.test.ts`](../../test/kernel/goal-measurements.test.ts).
  Its only production caller was the `/goals` collection loader, and
  [STEER-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-01--what-goals-answers--delivered-2026-08-28) removed
  that read ([DEBT-207](#-debt-207--goals-loads-three-reads-it-never-renders--p3--resolved-2026-08-28-v25-steer-01)):
  the gallery card it fed was deleted by REDESIGN-04, and the record and the
  pane plot their history from `listMeasurements(goalId)`, a different method.
- **Impact.** Small and slow-acting rather than sharp. A tested repository
  method with no caller is maintained by the type-checker and the test suite
  without being exercised by the product, and it is a standing invitation to the
  next author to reach for it because it looks like the intended way to read a
  series — which is how the dead read DEBT-207 closed got there in the first
  place.
- **Why STEER-01 did not remove it.** Its brief was to remove dead **reads from
  this route and composition**, not to prune the repository surface. Deleting a
  capability is a repository decision with its own blast radius (the kernel
  interface, the D1 implementation, five tests and the `countingDb` flatness
  proof they carry), and making it as a side effect of a route change is exactly
  the drive-by this register exists to prevent.
- **Desired future state.** A decision, taken once: either a surface genuinely
  needs a bounded per-Goal series across many Goals — a compact trend column, a
  review, an export — and the method has a caller again; or it does not, and the
  method, its interface entry and its tests are removed together.
- **Closing condition.** `listMeasurementSeries` has a production caller, or it
  no longer exists in the kernel interface, the D1 repository or the test suite.
- **V2.8 disposition — deferred to Insight, the presumptive V2.9 (2026-09-02).** Re-confirmed zero production callers (`d1-goal-measurement-repository.ts:583`; tests only). Beside it, `listSnapshotsBefore` (`d1-review-insight-repository.ts:537-557`, bounded at `MAX_TREND_PERIODS = 8`) also has none, while ≈52 `review_insight_snapshots` a year are written and only `priorReviews[0]` is ever read (`review-insights-context.ts:797-808`). The two close together with the multi-Review trend, in a programme whose rules are already ADR-079/110/111.
- **V2.9 disposition — TAKEN (2026-09-04).** Re-confirmed on `6b4d4a8`: zero callers for both. The decision is *a caller, not removal*: `listMeasurementSeries` feeds the compact per-Goal series on Insight ([INS-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_9.md#-ins-03--insight-with-a-real-range--closes-the-caller-half-of-debt-212)) and `listSnapshotsBefore` feeds the across-Reviews facts in the Review ([INS-02](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_9.md#-ins-02--across-reviews--takes-the-listsnapshotsbefore-half-of-debt-212s-disposition)) through the history kernel ([INS-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_9.md#-ins-01--the-history-kernel--closes-debt-238-debt-239)). The `/views` "since last Review" boundary read that reimplements the snapshot ordering inline (`d1-cross-view-query-repository.ts:315-339`) converges on the same kernel read in INS-01.
- **Related roadmap item.** [STEER-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-03--one-goal-one-story--delivered-2026-08-28),
  which decides what one Goal's story shows, is the natural place for the first
  half of that decision.

## Debt raised by the V2.6 roadmap decision (2026-08-28)

The [V2.6 roadmap decision](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_6.md) audited the AI platform
and the retrieval/capture evidence together. It raised **one** entry — everything
else it found was already in this register, and two entries it re-read
(DEBT-92, DEBT-93) were left as they stand rather than restated under new
numbers. It also **amended DEBT-91** with two new instances of that entry's own
defect, which is why they are not a new ID.

### ☐ DEBT-213 — The AI model and pricing registry is pinned to one dated reading with nothing scheduling its re-verification — P3

- **Current issue.** [`app/kernel/ai/ai-models.ts`](../../app/kernel/ai/ai-models.ts)
  pins six provider model ids across three tiers (`claude-haiku-4-5`,
  `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-opus-5`, `gpt-5-mini`, `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.5`) with
  their input/output prices, all carrying `PRICING_VERIFIED_AT = "2026-08-05"`.
  [ADR-073](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-073-the-controlled-ai-platform--provider-independence-proposal-only-writes-application-enforced-budgets-and-an-evidence-contract)
  decision 8 correctly **refuses** a model with no verified price for budgeted
  use, and its own consequences say the registry *"is a dated fact that will go
  stale and must be re-verified deliberately."* **Nothing schedules that
  deliberation.** No test asserts freshness, the deploy preflight
  (`scripts/deploy-production.mjs`) checks only for a half-configured Gateway,
  and the sole surfacing is one sentence in
  [`AiSettingsSection.tsx`](../../app/modules/settings/AiSettingsSection.tsx)
  reporting the date to whoever happens to open that panel.
- **Impact.** Two distinct failures, and the second is the one that bites first.
  A **price** that has drifted makes every budget reservation and every
  reconciled figure quietly wrong, in a system whose whole design (decision 9,
  reserve → run → reconcile, integer micro-USD) exists so the owner's spend
  ceiling is honest. A **retired model id** is worse and more likely: the
  provider returns `404`, which
  [`provider-transport.ts`](../../app/platform/ai/provider-transport.ts) maps to
  `model_unavailable`, so every AI feature at that tier stops working with a
  calm sentence and no indication that the cause is a registry entry rather than
  the code. Because no live call has ever been made from this repository, this
  lands on the **first** person to supply a key — the exact moment when a
  confusing failure is most expensive, because it is indistinguishable from the
  adapter bug the provider gate is looking for.
- **Why it was not fixed by the V2.6 pass.** A roadmap decision raises debt; it
  does not build. And the fix is not a code change on its own: re-verification
  means reading two providers' current model and pricing pages and recording
  what was read on a date, which is a deliberate act with an owner in it — the
  same class of work as the provider gate, and correctly done in the same pass.
- **Desired future state.** The registry's staleness is **visible without
  anybody opening Settings**, and re-verification is an act with a recorded
  date rather than a habit. Either a check that fails (or warns loudly) when
  `PRICING_VERIFIED_AT` is older than a stated interval, or the re-verification
  is made a named step of the AI provider gate and the interval is written down
  as a standing obligation — but not neither.
- **Closing condition.** `PRICING_VERIFIED_AT` reflects a reading taken on or
  after the day the first live provider call succeeds, **and** something other
  than a Settings sentence surfaces the registry going stale — a test, a
  preflight check or a recorded standing obligation with an interval. Until both
  are true, this stays open.
- **V2.8 disposition — DEFERRED, unchanged (2026-09-02).** Closes inside the AI gate's clause (e) as stated in [`ROADMAP_V2_8.md`](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#ai-decided-again-step-3-of-the-decision-pass).
- **V2.9 disposition — DEFERRED, unchanged (2026-09-04).** `PRICING_VERIFIED_AT` still `2026-08-05` (`ai-models.ts:117-124`). Closes inside the gate as [V2.14 GROUNDED AI](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_9.md#v214--grounded-ai-presumptive--gated-on-the-owner-held-key)'s first item, with DEBT-237.
- **Related roadmap item.** The AI provider gate recorded in
  [`ROADMAP_V2_6.md`](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_6.md#the-sequence-ai-takes-when-the-blocker-clears),
  item 1, which is where this closes; [ADR-073](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-073-the-controlled-ai-platform--provider-independence-proposal-only-writes-application-enforced-budgets-and-an-evidence-contract)
  decisions 8 and 9; [`AI_PLATFORM.md`](../development/AI_PLATFORM.md) §6, §21.

## Debt raised by V2.5 STEER-05 (2026-08-28)

[STEER-05](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-05--the-weeks-door--delivered-2026-08-28)
measured Today once, in its final shape, and found two pre-existing `axe`
target-size failures on the page it was adding a surface to. It fixed the one
its own acceptance criterion covered (**DEBT-214**) and recorded the one on
another item's surface rather than absorbing an unrelated repair into a feature
branch (**DEBT-215**). Both were issued as DEBT-213 / DEBT-214 on the branch and
**renumbered on merge**, because the V2.6 roadmap decision had meanwhile taken
213; see the ID rule in [How to use this register](#how-to-use-this-register).

### ☑ DEBT-214 — Today's small row links met no target-size floor on a fine pointer — P2 — raised and resolved 2026-08-28 (V2.5 STEER-05)

- **Original issue.** Two of Today's small row links met no pointer-agnostic
  target-size floor. WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8's 24×24 CSS-pixel minimum is **not**
  conditional on the input device, and `axe` measures it on a fine pointer too.
  1. [STEER-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-04--from-signal-to-step--delivered-2026-08-28)'s
     shared `NextActionLine` floored its link inside `@media (pointer: coarse)`,
     so on an ordinary desktop it was below the floor on every surface that
     draws it: Today's "Continue working" cards, and a Goal's record and
     workspace pane.
  2. `.dh-day-row__title` — the row title on Today's attention rail, its
     "Continue working" cards, its Schedule list and `/today/tomorrow` — had no
     floor at all, and failed the spacing fallback at a phone width.
- **Impact, MEASURED rather than inferred.** On `/today` at 1280 against the
  seeded workspace the next-action link is **75.7 × 16.9 px** with **18.8 px** of
  safe clickable space around it, against a 24 px minimum. At 320 the row title
  is **210 × 19.6 px** with **18.2 px** of safe clickable space. Both are
  **serious** `axe` violations, and neither was a latent risk — two existing
  tests were **failing on `main`** because of them:
  [`today-focus.spec.ts`](../../e2e/today-focus.spec.ts)'s *"passes axe on the
  banded panel in both appearances"* and
  [`goal-measurement.spec.ts`](../../e2e/goal-measurement.spec.ts)'s *"Today's
  progress sections fit a 320px phone"*. Both were reproduced on a clean tree
  with a freshly seeded database before any STEER-05 code existed. A small
  pointer target is also the accessibility defect that costs the most for the
  least: it is the difference between clicking a next action and clicking the
  row behind it.
- **Why it was fixed here rather than filed.** STEER-05's own acceptance
  criterion 5 is an axe-clean Today with the week's door present, and a red page
  cannot be scoped around without weakening the claim. `AGENTS.md` §12's
  campsite rule points the same way — the change touches Today's composition, so
  it owns what it finds there.
- **Resolved 2026-08-28.** Both links now occupy a real target on **every**
  pointer, floored at the standard's 24 px through one new named token,
  `--app-pointer-target-min`. The token sits beside `--app-touch-target-min`
  rather than replacing it: 45 px stays the product's comfortable touch target
  and stays what a *control* reaches for, and the coarse-pointer rule still
  lifts the next-action link the rest of the way on touch. The smaller floor
  exists for exactly this shape — a deliberately small link inside a dense row,
  where 45 px would make a supporting line taller than the title it supports.
  The row title takes it through `min-block-size` plus `align-content` rather
  than a flex box, because it is a single-line ellipsised link and
  `display: flex` would put its text in an anonymous box `text-overflow` cannot
  reach. **Measured after each step**: the next-action fix alone moved the row
  title's safe clickable space from 18.2 px to 21.6 px — closer and still short,
  which is why the second half was needed. Verified by re-running both failing
  tests (`1 passed`, `7 passed`), by STEER-05's own full-page scans in both
  appearances, and by the whole 128-test
  [`accessibility.spec.ts`](../../e2e/accessibility.spec.ts) sweep.
- **The lesson worth keeping.** A `@media (pointer: coarse)` guard around a
  target-size floor is a smell: the coarse-pointer query is for *comfort*
  (45 px), never for *conformance* (24 px). Anywhere the two are conflated, the
  fine-pointer case is silently unconformant.
- **Related roadmap item.** Raised by
  [STEER-05](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-05--the-weeks-door--delivered-2026-08-28)
  against [STEER-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-04--from-signal-to-step--delivered-2026-08-28)'s
  shipped component.

### ☑ DEBT-215 — Three E2E assertions still address the Area record's Goals tab as a Card — P2 — **RESOLVED 2026-09-02**

- **Current issue.** [STEER-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-03--one-goal-one-story--delivered-2026-08-28)
  replaced the Area record's Goals tab cards with the shared
  [`GoalStoryRow`](../../app/shared/goal-progress/GoalStoryRow.tsx), which
  renders a `ProgressRow` — a heading and a link inside a `ProgressRowList` —
  rather than the `role="article"` `Card` with an `Open <title>` link it drew
  before. Three assertions in two specs were not moved with it:
  - [`goals.spec.ts`](../../e2e/goals.spec.ts) `:148` — `getByRole("article", { name: goalTitle })`;
  - [`goals.spec.ts`](../../e2e/goals.spec.ts) `:286` and
    [`areas.spec.ts`](../../e2e/areas.spec.ts) `:94` — `getByRole("link", { name: "Open Launch the site" })`.

  The row's link is named by `goalStoryRowAccessibleName` — `"<title> — <alignment> — <movement>"` —
  so `Open <title>` no longer matches anything, and there is no `article` role on
  the tab at all.
- **Impact.** Three tests fail on `main`, and they are not slow or flaky: they
  time out waiting for locators that cannot resolve. MEASURED on a clean tree
  with a freshly seeded local database on 2026-08-28 —
  `goals.spec.ts` *"create, edit details, link a Project, complete/reopen, review
  Activity"* and *"has no horizontal overflow across representative desktop and
  mobile widths"*, and `areas.spec.ts` *"collection, creation, record, rename,
  hierarchy and Project navigation"*. A red gate makes every other "verified"
  claim in the repository weaker, which is [DEBT-41](#-debt-41--the-e2e-suite-is-unreliable-on-main-so-ci-is-green-claims-are-unverifiable--p1--resolved-2026-08-02)'s
  whole point.
- **Why STEER-05 did not fix it.** It is a different item's surface. STEER-05
  fixed what its own acceptance criterion required — an axe-clean Today, which
  is [DEBT-214](#-debt-214--todays-small-row-links-met-no-target-size-floor-on-a-fine-pointer--p2--raised-and-resolved-2026-08-28-v25-steer-05)
  — and recorded this rather than absorbing an unrelated repair pass into a
  feature branch. That is V2.4-GATE-01's own recorded reason for the same choice:
  *"building three more fixtures inside a pass repairing fifty-five other tests
  is how a gate branch stops being reviewable."*
- **Desired future state.** The three assertions address what the tab now
  renders. The row already carries the machine hook every cross-surface test
  uses — `[data-goal-story="<id>"]` — and `steer-goal-story.spec.ts` is the

  than on a card's role. Do not re-add an `article` wrapper or an `Open <title>`
  label to satisfy a spec; the row's contract is the one STEER-03 shipped.
- **Closing condition.** `goals.spec.ts` and `areas.spec.ts` pass on a clean
  tree with a freshly seeded database, asserting the Area Goals tab through the
  shared row's own contract.
- **CORRECTED 2026-09-02 by [the V2.8 decision pass](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md), and TAKEN by [V2.8 CONV-00](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-00--the-gate-tells-the-truth-again--delivered-2026-09-02)-B.** The claim above that *"there is no `article` role on the tab at all"* is false on `main` at `036d3da`: `ProgressRow` renders `<article aria-label={title}>` (`app/shared/card/ProgressRow.tsx:126-131`), so `goals.spec.ts:148` / `areas.spec.ts:90` DO resolve; what cannot resolve is the `Open <title>` link name (`goals.spec.ts:151, :286`, `areas.spec.ts:94`), because the row names its link `"<title> — <alignment> — <movement>"` (`GoalStoryRow.tsx:162-176`). Red on every `main` run from #779 (2026-08-28) to #815 (2026-09-01). Repair per the desired state above — `[data-goal-story]` and the row's real accessible name; no `article` wrapper or `Open <title>` label is re-added.
- **RESOLVED 2026-09-02 by [V2.8 CONV-00](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-00--the-gate-tells-the-truth-again--delivered-2026-09-02)-B.** The three assertions now address what the tab renders, through two shared helpers in `e2e/helpers.ts`: `goalStoryRow(scope, id)` finds a row by the machine key every row stamps (`[data-goal-story="<id>"]`), and `expectGoalStoryOpenLink(row, title)` asserts the open affordance by the name the product composes — the title, then one " — " segment per derived answer the row says it holds (`data-goal-alignment-state`, `data-goal-movement-available`) — and returns the link. `goals.spec.ts` locates the Goal it created by the id in its own URL and the seeded `g-launch` for the overflow journey; `areas.spec.ts` asserts `g-launch`'s link `href` is its canonical record. No `article` wrapper and no `Open <title>` label was added to the product. **Falsified** by changing the composition to `Open <title>` and to a `" · "` separator on a scratch tree: `areas.spec.ts:12` and both `goals.spec.ts` journeys fail naming the link found. All three pass on a fresh seed (23.6 s, 32.7 s and the overflow journey).
- **Related roadmap item.** [STEER-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-03--one-goal-one-story--delivered-2026-08-28),
  which made the change; [V2.8 CONV-00](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-00--the-gate-tells-the-truth-again--delivered-2026-09-02), which repaired it.

[FIND-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_6.md#-find-01--search-answers-before-you-type--delivered-2026-08-29)
ran the Search, command-palette and accessibility suites to verify its own

### ☑ DEBT-216 — A command-palette test still asserts that Goals have no creation command, which STEER-01 gave them — P2 — **RESOLVED 2026-09-02**

- **Current issue.** [`e2e/command-palette.spec.ts`](../../e2e/command-palette.spec.ts) `:603`
  — *"contributes NO create-Goal command, because there is no such surface"* —
  asserts `getByRole("option", { name: /^New Goal/ })` has count **0**. It has
  count **1**. The test is not wrong about the past: when it was written a Goal
  could only be created from an Area record, so a workspace-level command would
  have promised something the product could not do. [V2.5 STEER-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md)
  then built exactly that surface, and `app/modules/goals/commands.ts` `:50`
  registers `goals.new` → `/goals?drawer=new-goal` through the same
  Drawer-in-the-URL contract the Areas and Projects create commands use. **The
  product is right and the assertion is stale.**
- **Impact.** One E2E test fails on `main`, and it fails for the least useful
  reason a test can: it is enforcing the absence of a feature that was
  deliberately shipped. A red gate makes every other "verified" claim in the
  repository weaker, which is [DEBT-41](#-debt-41--the-e2e-suite-is-unreliable-on-main-so-ci-is-green-claims-are-unverifiable--p1--resolved-2026-08-02)'s
  whole point — and a stale negative assertion is worse than a stale positive
  one, because the obvious "fix" is to delete the command that is correct.
- **MEASURED on a clean tree**, 2026-08-29, against `main` at `df85e95` with a
  freshly seeded local database, before any FIND-01 code existed: `1 failed`,
  `Expected: 0 / Received: 1`. Re-confirmed with FIND-01's changes stashed.
- **Why FIND-01 did not fix it.** It is a different item's surface. FIND-01
  changed Search's empty-query path and touched no command, no Goal and no
  palette registration; the failure reproduces identically with its work
  removed. Repairing another item's stale assertion inside a feature branch is
  how a branch stops being reviewable — V2.4-GATE-01's own recorded reason for
  the same choice.
- **Desired future state.** The assertion says what is now true. The palette
  offers `goals.new`, and what should be asserted is that creating a Goal goes
  through the ONE shared `NewGoalForm` at `/goals?drawer=new-goal` rather than a
  second creation flow — which is the invariant the original test was really
  protecting. Do not delete `goals.new` to make the test pass.
- **Closing condition.** `command-palette.spec.ts` passes on a clean tree with a
  freshly seeded database, asserting the Goal creation command's real contract.
- **V2.8 disposition — TAKEN by [V2.8 CONV-00](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-00--the-gate-tells-the-truth-again--delivered-2026-09-02)-A (2026-09-02).** Still red on #815; the test moved to `:616` (assertion `:634`) and survived RECALL-02's edit of the same file. Repair per the desired state; `goals.new` stays and the test asserts the one-flow invariant it always meant.
- **RESOLVED 2026-09-02 by [V2.8 CONV-00](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-00--the-gate-tells-the-truth-again--delivered-2026-09-02)-A.** The test is now *"creates a Goal through the ONE shared creation Drawer, and offers no second flow"*: under the title, the verb (a registered keyword) and the noun, exactly one `New Goal` option and no `Create Goal`/`Add Goal`; running it lands on `/goals?drawer=new-goal`, closes the palette, and the Drawer that opens is the shared `NewGoalForm` (one dialog, one form named "New Goal", its "Create Goal" control) — the Areas/Projects create commands' contract, asserted the same way. `goals.new` is untouched. **Falsified**: unregistering `goals.new` fails the count and the click; pointing it at `/goals` fails the URL assertion.
- **Related roadmap item.** [STEER-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md), which made
  the change; [V2.8 CONV-00](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-00--the-gate-tells-the-truth-again--delivered-2026-09-02), which repaired the assertion.

## Debt raised by V2.6 FIND-02 + FIND-03 + FIND-04 (2026-08-29)

The tag programme drove People, Assets, Notes, Tasks and the capture line at
1440 / 393 / 320 in both appearances to verify its own change, then read the full
CI gate. **Five** findings are about surfaces it does not own: a fixture written
outside the closed relationship vocabulary the product enforces; a pre-existing
`axe` finding on a shared anchored surface; a journey that went red on the day a
seeded obligation's due date passed; an assertion that reads a title STEER-04 now
shows as a Project's next action; and a real 200%-zoom overflow on Today caused
by STEER-05's week door. Four of the five are MEASURED rather than assumed, two
of those by naming the exact element in the DOM. All five are recorded rather
than fixed, because repairing another item's surface inside a feature branch is
how a branch stops being reviewable.

### ☐ DEBT-217 — A convergence fixture seeds a Person whose relationship is outside the product's own closed vocabulary — P3

- **Current issue.** [`e2e/seed-record-convergence.sql`](../../e2e/seed-record-convergence.sql)
  seeds `p-rc-dan` with `relationship = 'Builder'`. `Builder` is not a member of
  the Person relationship vocabulary the kernel validates against, so **any**
  journey that opens that Person's contact form and saves it — without touching
  the relationship at all — is rejected with
  `{"fieldErrors":{"relationship":"Invalid relationship: is not a recognised value"}}`.
  The product is right: the closed vocabulary is the contract, and a form that
  round-trips a field must submit a value the domain accepts.
- **Impact.** Low and narrow, but it is a trap rather than a nuisance: the
  failure names `relationship` while the journey was editing something else
  entirely (tags, in the case that found it), so the next reader debugs the wrong
  surface. It also means one seeded Person is not editable through the real UI,
  which is not a state the product can reach on its own.
- **Where it was found.** V2.6 FIND-02, writing the People half of the tagging
  parity journey. The journey was switched to `p-rc-ana` — a Person the fixture
  seeds correctly — rather than the fixture being changed, because the fixture
  belongs to the record-convergence item and is asserted on by its own specs.
- **Desired future state.** The seeded relationship is a member of the
  vocabulary, or the fixture states in a comment that the row is deliberately
  invalid and which spec depends on that.
- **Closing condition.** Every Person the convergence fixture seeds can be saved
  through the contact form without editing a field the journey did not intend to
  edit.
- **Related roadmap item.** The record-convergence work that owns the fixture; a
  truth-restoration pass in the [HARDEN-05](HARDEN_05_GREEN_MAIN_2026_08.md)
  mould owns the repair.

### ☑ DEBT-219 — An Assets journey went red on 2026-08-29 because a fixture obligation's due date passed — P2 — **RESOLVED 2026-09-02**

- **Current issue.** [`e2e/assets-ownership.spec.ts`](../../e2e/assets-ownership.spec.ts)
  `:605` asserts `getByText("1 obligation overdue")` is visible — unscoped, and
  therefore strict-mode-sensitive to any second card carrying the same sentence.
  The record-convergence fixture seeds `ob-rc-inspect` ("Safety inspection (pink
  slip)") on `Hilux SR5 — work ute` with `due_date = '2026-08-28'`. **On
  2026-08-29 that date passed**, the Hilux's card began reading "1 obligation
  overdue" like the journey's own asset, and the locator resolved to two
  elements.
- **MEASURED, and the cause is the calendar, not a change.** Queried against the
  local D1 on 2026-08-29: exactly one seeded open obligation is now past due, and
  it is `ob-rc-inspect` on `as-rc-ute`. The V2.6 tag programme, which found it,
  changed **no** obligation row — `git diff` over
  `e2e/seed-record-convergence.sql`'s `asset_obligations` block is empty — and
  touches neither due dates nor the asset card's due text. The failure would have
  arrived on this date on `main`.
- **Impact.** One E2E journey red, and it will stay red: a fixed date does not
  become un-past. It is the [DEBT-173](#-debt-173--e2e-specs-assert-against-the-shared-workspaces-accumulated-state-so-re-ordering-the-suite-changes-what-they-see--p2)
  class seen from the other side — not a leak between specs, but a fixture whose
  meaning depends on the day it is run.
- **Why the tag programme did not fix it.** A different item's fixture and a
  different item's assertion, and repairing it inside a feature branch is the
  reviewability cost this register keeps recording. It is also two repairs rather
  than one, and which of them is right is the owning item's call.
- **Desired future state.** Either the assertion is scoped to the card the
  journey created (the fixture's other cards are then free to say anything), or
  the seeded obligation's date is expressed relative to the run day the way the
  Tasks fixtures already express theirs. The first is the smaller change and does
  not move a date another spec may assert on.
- **Closing condition.** `assets-ownership.spec.ts` passes on a clean tree with a
  freshly seeded database, on a day after 2026-08-28.
- **V2.8 disposition — TAKEN by [V2.8 CONV-00](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-00--the-gate-tells-the-truth-again--delivered-2026-09-02)-D (2026-09-02).** Still red on #815, five days past due. **A second bomb is armed**: `ob-rc-rego`, `due_date = '2026-09-14'` (`e2e/seed-record-convergence.sql:382`). CONV-00 scopes the assertion to the journey's own card AND makes seeded obligation dates run-relative under the fixture rule [DEBT-236](#-debt-236--two-task-date-editor-journeys-assert-the-calendar-month-they-were-written-in--p2--resolved-2026-09-02) records.
- **RESOLVED 2026-09-02 by [V2.8 CONV-00](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-00--the-gate-tells-the-truth-again--delivered-2026-09-02)-D — both repairs, in the order the entry ranked them.** (1) The assertion is scoped to the card the journey created, through the spec's own `expectCollectionSignal(page, title, signal)` — the list item carrying the asset's title, then the signal inside it — so the fixture's other cards are free to say anything. **Falsified** with the pre-repair seed (the Hilux's inspection five days overdue): the unscoped `getByText("1 obligation overdue")` fails strict mode on two elements while the scoped assertion passes. (2) Every OPEN obligation in `seed-record-convergence.sql`, and the ute's `next_service_date` / `renewal_date`, are now `date('now', '+N days')` offsets — the offsets the fixture was written with, from 2026-08-01 (`ob-rc-rego` +44, `ob-rc-inspect` +27, `ob-rc-service` +93, `ob-rc-insurance` +184) — so no seeded obligation crosses its due date because the calendar advanced; completed history keeps its real dates and the warranty stays a fixed, annotated fact. The Static check CONV-00-E added ([DEBT-236](#-debt-236--two-task-date-editor-journeys-assert-the-calendar-month-they-were-written-in--p2--resolved-2026-09-02)) fails on the next such literal.
- **Related roadmap item.** ASSET-03, which owns the journey; [V2.8 CONV-00](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-00--the-gate-tells-the-truth-again--delivered-2026-09-02), which repaired it.

### ☐ DEBT-218 — The shared anchored surface scrolls, and `axe` reports `scrollable-region-focusable` on the collection controls popover — P3

- **Current issue.** The collection controls popover renders inside the shared
  `.dh-anchored` surface, which clamps its height and scrolls. `axe` reports
  `scrollable-region-focusable` on that scroller because every row inside the
  menu is `tabIndex={-1}` — a **correct** roving-tabindex pattern, which the rule
  cannot see the arrow-key access of. The finding is therefore about a shared
  surface's interaction with a static rule, not about a keyboard user being
  stuck.
- **MEASURED, not assumed**, at 1440 by V2.6 FIND-03 before its own group
  existed: the popover's content is **6206px** against a **694px** clamp with the
  tag group hidden, and **6612px** with it. The surface already scrolled; the tag
  dimension adds ~6% and does not cause it.
- **Impact.** One `axe` violation on a shared surface, reachable from every
  collection. Real enough to keep, low enough not to justify a shared-surface
  change inside a feature branch — and it is exactly the kind of finding that
  must not be answered by disabling a rule.
- **What FIND-03 did instead.** It scoped its own scan to the popover's menu
  BODY (`.dh-collection-popover__body`, or `[data-testid='collection-sheet']`
  when compact) with the reason recorded in the spec file, and **disabled no
  rule**. Everything the item is responsible for is clean.
- **Desired future state.** The scroller carries the access the rule is looking
  for — most simply `tabIndex={0}` with an accessible name on the scrolling
  region, which is compatible with the roving tabindex inside it — or the
  surface is restructured so the menu body is the scroller.
- **Closing condition.** `expectNoAxeViolations(page)` passes unscoped on a page
  with the collection controls open, at 1440 and at 320, with no rule disabled.
- **Related roadmap item.** [DHDS-09](../design/DHDS_09_FLOATING_SURFACES_AND_CONTEXTUAL_CHOICE_2026_08.md),
  which owns the anchored surface.

### ☑ DEBT-220 — A Project-templates assertion reads a template task's TITLE, which STEER-04 now shows as a Project's next action — P2 — **RESOLVED 2026-09-02**

- **Current issue.** [`project-templates.spec.ts`](../../e2e/project-templates.spec.ts)
  `:317` asserts, on `/today`, that `getByText(<template task title>)` has count
  **0** — the surface half of *"a template's tasks are never live work"*. It has
  count **1**. The template's task titles are copied from the SOURCE Project's
  real tasks, so the assertion matches by a string the live work also carries,
  and [STEER-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md) then gave Today's Project cards a
  next-action line. **The claim is still true and the assertion is now wrong.**
- **MEASURED, and the element is named rather than guessed.** Probed on
  2026-08-29 by seeding only `seedCanonicalProject()` — no template saved, no
  tags anywhere — and walking the text nodes of `/today`. Exactly one match, at:
  `a.dh-next-action__open` ‹ `p.dh-next-action dh-day-row__next` ‹
  `li.dh-day-row dh-day-row--project` ‹ `section.dh-today__panel dh-today__continue`.
  That is [`NextActionLine`](../../app/modules/today/day/TodayScreen.tsx) — the
  Project's own next action, which is live work and is supposed to be there.
- **Impact.** One E2E journey red, and red for the least useful reason: it is
  reporting a feature that shipped. The underlying guarantee is unaffected — the
  same test asserts structurally, at the database, that a template task has no
  `entities` row at all, and that assertion passes.
- **Why the V2.6 tag programme did not fix it.** A different item's spec, and a
  different item's surface: the tag work adds no Task to Today, changes no
  next-action rule (it is explicitly forbidden from feeding one) and touches no
  template. Recorded rather than repaired inside a feature branch.
- **Desired future state.** The absence is asserted on the template's tasks by
  the identity that makes them templates — their `project_template_tasks` rows
  have no entity id — or the `/today` assertion is scoped to exclude
  `.dh-next-action`, which is the Project's next action rather than a task list.
  Do not delete the next-action line to satisfy a spec.
- **Closing condition.** `project-templates.spec.ts` passes on a clean tree with
  a freshly seeded database, with the template-vs-live-work guarantee still
  asserted at the database.
- **V2.8 disposition — TAKEN by [V2.8 CONV-00](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-00--the-gate-tells-the-truth-again--delivered-2026-09-02)-C (2026-09-02).** Still red on #815 (`:316-325`, on `/today` and again on `/plan`); the structural guarantee at `:307-313` passes. Repair per the desired state; the next-action line stays.
- **RESOLVED 2026-09-02 by [V2.8 CONV-00](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-00--the-gate-tells-the-truth-again--delivered-2026-09-02)-C.** The structural guarantee (no `entities` row joins a `project_template_tasks` row) is kept as the claim; the surface half on `/today` and `/plan` is scoped to the shared task row — `taskRows(page).filter({ hasText: title })` has count 0 — because a Task is acted on in a row and the next-action line is a reference to a Project's Task, not a Task (ADR-115 decision 3). The next-action line stays. The template fixture's source Task dates (`project-template-fixtures.ts`) were also a bomb this pass could see arming — a fixed March 2027 due/scheduled pair would have put the source Task on Today that March and failed the scoped assertion — and are now derived from the owner's day. **Falsified** by inserting a live Task entity titled "Pull the numbers" scheduled for the owner's day on a scratch tree: the scoped `/today` assertion fails on one task row; inserting an `entities` row with a template task's id fails the structural assertion.
- **Related roadmap item.** [STEER-04](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md), which added
  the line; PROJECT-02, which owns the spec; [V2.8 CONV-00](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-00--the-gate-tells-the-truth-again--delivered-2026-09-02), which repaired it.

### ☑ DEBT-221 — Today overflows sideways at 200% zoom, because the week door's date range cannot wrap — P2 — **RESOLVED 2026-09-02**

- **Current issue.** [`mobile-shell.spec.ts`](../../e2e/mobile-shell.spec.ts)
  `:502` drives `/today` at **195 × 422** — a 390px phone at 200% zoom, which is
  WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.4's own case — and requires no horizontal scrolling. The
  document scrolls to **239px** in a **195px** viewport.
- **MEASURED on 2026-08-29**, by walking every element whose right edge passes
  the client width. The offender is [STEER-05](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md)'s week
  door: `a.dh-btn.dh-btn--outlined.dh-btn--sm` — *"Start this week's Review,
  24 Aug 2026–30 Aug 2026"* — laid out **206px** wide, driven by its
  `span.dh-today__review-door-period` at **166px**. The period is a date range
  joined by an en dash (`24 Aug 2026–30 Aug 2026`) with no break opportunity in
  it, so the button cannot narrow below the range. (`a.dh-viewtabs__tab` also
  passes the edge, but it sits in a deliberately scrollable tab strip and is not
  the document overflow.)
- **Impact.** A real accessibility defect rather than a stale assertion: a
  low-vision owner at 200% zoom gets a sideways-scrolling Today. It is not
  caused by the number of records — the offending string is a fixed-width date
  range that is always there once the door is open.
- **Why the V2.6 tag programme did not fix it.** It is STEER-05's surface and a
  layout decision about how a week is worded; nothing in the tag work renders on
  Today. Reproduced on a clean `origin/main` tree at `b928fd4`, with its own dev
  server and a freshly migrated and seeded database, with the identical predicate
  timeout — so it predates this branch.
- **Desired future state.** The range gets a break opportunity (a `<wbr>` or a
  wrapping span per date), or the door states the week in a form that fits — the
  product already has a short calendar wording — or the button wraps to two
  lines at that width. Whichever is taken, it is judged by re-measuring
  `documentElement.scrollWidth` at 195px, not by looking at it.
- **Closing condition.** `mobile-shell.spec.ts`'s 200%-zoom case passes for
  `/today` on a clean tree, with the week door still reachable and still naming
  its period.
- **CORRECTED 2026-09-02 by [the V2.8 decision pass](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md), and TAKEN by [V2.8 CONV-00](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-00--the-gate-tells-the-truth-again--delivered-2026-09-02)-F.** The named offender does not hold on `main` at `036d3da`: `span.dh-today__review-door-period` sits in the panel HEAD and has carried `white-space: normal` since STEER-05 itself (`app/styles/today.css:2127-2129`); the door button's period is a `.dh-visually-hidden` span (`app/styles/base.css:563-573`) that cannot drive layout width; no code has touched the door since `bc26fd2`. **RE-MEASURED locally at 195 × 422 on a fresh seed (2026-09-02)**: `scrollWidth` **239** against `clientWidth` **195** — the defect is real and unchanged — and exactly three elements pass the right edge: `a.dh-viewtabs__tab` (the deliberately scrollable strip, not document overflow), `p.dh-today__panel-foot` at 206px, and inside it the door itself, `a.dh-btn.dh-btn--outlined.dh-btn--sm`, laid out **206px** wide. The button's VISIBLE label — *"Start this week's Review"* — is what cannot wrap, because the shared button is `white-space: nowrap`; the date range is not in the visible box at all. The fix is at the button (let the label wrap below the phone tier, or a shorter label there), judged by re-measuring `scrollWidth`, and the closing condition is unchanged.
- **RESOLVED 2026-09-02 by [V2.8 CONV-00](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-00--the-gate-tells-the-truth-again--delivered-2026-09-02)-F, at the offender the correction named.** The door's link carries one more class, `dh-today__review-door-open`, whose rule in `today.css` is the `.dh-today__reflection-write` treatment already on the same screen: `white-space: normal`, `min-inline-size: 0`, `max-inline-size: 100%`, `text-align: start`; and the door's foot may shrink once it has wrapped onto its own line (`flex: 0 1 auto; min-inline-size: 0` instead of `flex: none`). Nothing about the shared button changes — this is one label on one panel — and the button semantics, the outlined geometry, the glyph and the accessible name with its period are untouched. **RE-MEASURED after the fix with the same element walk, on a fresh seed:** at 195 × 422, `scrollWidth` **195** against `clientWidth` **195**, the door laid out **129 × 49** (two lines, `white-space: normal`, name *"Start this week’s Review, 31 Aug 2026–6 Sep 2026"*), and the only element past the right edge is `a.dh-viewtabs__tab` in the deliberately scrollable strip; at 393 px the door is **206 × 32** on one line and nothing passes the edge, so the phone appearance is unchanged. `mobile-shell.spec.ts` *"stays usable at 200% zoom: /today"* passes with no rule disabled. **Falsified** by restoring `white-space: nowrap` on the door: the 195 px assertion fails again (`scrollWidth` 239) while 393 px still passes.
- **Related roadmap item.** [STEER-05](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_5.md#-steer-05--the-weeks-door--delivered-2026-08-28),
  which owns the door; [V2.8 CONV-00](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-00--the-gate-tells-the-truth-again--delivered-2026-09-02), which repaired it.

## Debt raised by the V2.7 roadmap decision (2026-08-30)

The RECALL programme definition ([`ROADMAP_V2_7.md`](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_7.md),
[ADR-114](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-114-recall--retrieval-reaches-content-under-an-explicit-query-boundary-one-excerpt-contract-one-completion-time-authority-and-commitments-that-return-without-a-reminder-engine))
re-measured every finding of the 2026-08-29 post-V2.6 audit against `main` at
`0d08cd6` and issues here the numbers that audit deliberately withheld. Every
entry below carries the measurement that confirmed it; two of the audit's
claims did NOT survive re-measurement and became corrections rather than debt
(Review snapshots ARE compared — `review-insights.ts:608-631, 679-727,
741-768, 1183-1196` — and `/today/waiting` HAS a palette command,
`today/commands.ts:30-37`). Read this register's own warning on DEBT-200:
