### ☑ DEBT-236 — Two Task date-editor journeys assert the calendar month they were written in — P2 — **RESOLVED 2026-09-02**

- **Current issue.** Two E2E journeys walk the DalyHub date picker's month
  grid by a FIXED number of `PageUp`/`PageDown` presses from the month the
  grid opens on, then click a day named by its full spoken date — and both
  numbers were counted in August 2026.
  [`e2e/editing-consistency.spec.ts`](../../e2e/editing-consistency.spec.ts) `:253`
  clears the seeded Task's due date, reopens the picker — *"Unset, so the grid
  opens on the owner's own month; July is one back"* (`:301-303`) — presses
  `PageUp` once and clicks *"Wednesday 29 July 2026"* (`:304`).
  [`e2e/inline-editor-overlay.spec.ts`](../../e2e/inline-editor-overlay.spec.ts) `:390`
  commits "Today", reopens, presses `PageDown` four times and clicks *"Friday
  25 December 2026"* (`:450-454`). From August, one back is July and four
  ahead is December. From September, one back is August and four ahead is
  January 2027, and neither day is in the grid.
- **MEASURED.** Both went red the day the owner's calendar (the seeded
  identity's timezone) turned to September: `editing-consistency.spec.ts:253`
  is red on `main` runs #812 (`7a60fea`, 2026-08-31) and #815 (`036d3da`,
  2026-09-01); `inline-editor-overlay.spec.ts:390` is red on #815 (on #812 its
  spec file sat in a partition that was red for another reason, and the
  manifest was regenerated between the two). **Reproduced locally on
  2026-09-02** on a freshly migrated and seeded database from a clean tree:
  `locator.click: Test timeout` at `:304` (30.8 s) and at `:454` (1.5 m).
  Neither is named by any entry — DEBT-215/216/219/220/221 are the five
  recorded causes, and these two arrived while the gate was already red.
- **Impact.** Two journeys covering the due-date editor — the control DHDS-09
  built and DHDS-10 put on every row — are red and will stay red until August
  2027, and any real regression in that editor is invisible behind them. It is
  the [DEBT-219](#-debt-219--an-assets-journey-went-red-on-2026-08-29-because-a-fixture-obligations-due-date-passed--p2--resolved-2026-09-02)
  class from inside the spec rather than the seed: a test whose meaning
  depends on the day it is run. 111 absolute 2026 date literals exist in
  `e2e/*.sql` today; `ob-rc-rego` (`seed-record-convergence.sql:382`) arms on
  2026-09-14.
- **Desired future state.** The two journeys compute their target day from
  the run day through the same owner-day helper the product uses, name it
  with the same long-date formatter the grid uses for its accessible names,
  and derive the number of month presses from the difference between the
  month the grid opens on (asserted first, not assumed) and the target. A
  Static-tier check (`scripts/e2e-fixture-dates.mjs --check`, beside
  `e2e:partitions:check`) fails the build on any unannotated future date
  literal in an E2E fixture or spec, in every format that can recreate this
  defect — ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`, the long-form accessible label the picker tests
  click (`Wednesday 29 July 2026`) and the abbreviated display form the specs
  assert on (`29 Jul 2026`); an ISO-only scan would stay green on exactly the
  two literals above. A picker-action label is flagged whatever its date,
  past or future — the presses that reach it are counted from where the grid
  opens, which is the run day when the value is unset — so a label from last
  month cannot re-arm this defect either. Its first run enumerates the 111
  ISO literals and the
  long-form and abbreviated ones in the specs, and the item classifies each
  as derived, fixed historical, deliberately fixed and annotated, or a
  time-bomb to convert (the full contract is CONV-00-E, amended 2026-09-02).
- **Closing condition.** Both journeys pass on a clean tree with a freshly
  seeded database in any month; the Static check is green and would go red on
  **both** a bare future ISO literal and a bare long-form picker label of any
  date (falsified by adding one of each); no fixture date arms.
- **RESOLVED 2026-09-02 by [V2.8 CONV-00](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-00--the-gate-tells-the-truth-again--delivered-2026-09-02)-E — the class, not the instance.**
  - **The two journeys are derived end to end**, through one shared test-side module, [`e2e/calendar-dates.ts`](../../e2e/calendar-dates.ts): the target comes from the owner's day (`ownerTodayIso`, the same `ownerToday` resolution as ADR-022) or from the value the test itself set; its label is generated in the grid's own shape (`calendarDayLabel` — weekday, day, month, year, English names, no comma); the grid's opening month is **asserted** by its live heading (`expectCalendarMonth`) and the `PageUp`/`PageDown` count is the difference between that month and the target's (`pickCalendarDayByKeyboard`); the rendered form is read back through `shortCalendarDate`, which mirrors the product's `formatCalendarDate` ("Sep", where `Intl` en-AU says "Sept"). `editing-consistency.spec.ts` walks from the seeded July month to the 15th of the month after the seeded date, then — after clearing — from the owner's current month back to the seeded day; `inline-editor-overlay.spec.ts` walks from the owner's month to the 25th of the month two ahead. The seeded `2026-07-29` stays a fixed historical datum (the decision: the walk to it became run-relative, not the seed). Both pass on a fresh seed in September (16.3 s and 11.7 s) — the month in which the old assertions timed out.
  - **The Static check exists and is wired**: `scripts/e2e-fixture-dates.mjs check` (`pnpm run e2e:fixture-dates:check`, a `Static` step beside `e2e:partitions:check`). It scans every `.sql`, `.ts`, `.mts` and `.mjs` under `e2e/` (the `.mts` fixture generator included), strips comments string-aware, and reads three forms — ISO (alone or leading a timestamp), the long-form picker label, and the abbreviated display form with or without a weekday, "Sep" and "Sept" alike. A data literal is flagged when it is on or after `HEAD`'s committer date (a fixture dated *today* reads "due today" today and "overdue" tomorrow — the same class one day later, a review finding that caught one such seed row); a long-form picker label is flagged **whatever its date**; a same-line `// fixed-date: <why>` / `-- fixed-date: <why>` annotation classifies a literal as deliberately fixed in every form. `list` prints the inventory. Sixteen unit tests (`test/unit/ci/e2e-fixture-dates.test.ts`) pin the contract, including that the repository's own fixtures are clean.
  - **The first run's inventory, classified.** 1,315 literals in 42 files on `036d3da` (the entry's "111" counted date-only literals in the seeds; the check also reads the date leading every timestamp, which is why the total is larger): **1,254 fixed historical** (ignored), **57 data literals on or after the reference day** and **2 bare picker labels** to resolve, 2 already annotated. Of the 59: **43 converted to derived** — 17 `seed-tasks.sql` dataset dues/schedules (one of them dated the reference day itself) and 10 `seed-record-convergence.sql` dates as `date('now', '+N days')` with the fixture's own authoring offsets; six "far ahead" creation instants (`checklist-`, `dependency-`, `drag-`, `project-template-fixtures.ts`, `pwa-offline-tasks.spec.ts`) as `futureInstant(366)`, because a fixed 2027 instant sorts above live records only until 2027; eight typed Goal targets and picker targets (`goal-fixtures.ts`, `goal-measurement`, `goals-outcomes`, `goals`, `areas-goals-mobile`, `dhds-10-inline-manipulation`, four in `visual-convergence-screenshots`) as `ownerDayPlus` / `dayInMonthsAhead`, read back through `shortCalendarDate`; and the template fixture's source-Task dates (DEBT-220). **16 annotated as deliberately fixed**: `2099-12-31` (`t-drawer`, twice, and its "Due 31 Dec 2099" assertion), the Hilux's warranty (`2027-05-10`, a purchase fact, three places), a history event's recorded "next due", the drag fixture's milestone Goal target, and the Diary strip's two long-form day links, which are walked from a fixed seeded `?date=` rather than from the run day. After the pass: 1,263 literals, 1,247 past, 16 annotated, **0 offenders**.
  - **Falsified, both halves, on a scratch tree**: an unannotated future ISO literal in a seed and an unannotated long-form picker label whose date is already past each fail `Static`'s check with the file, line, literal and form named; each passes again once annotated. The clock could not be moved on this machine; the derivation is instead pinned by the unit tests over a fixed reference day and proven by the two journeys passing in the month that broke them.
- **Related roadmap item.** [V2.8 CONV-00](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#-conv-00--the-gate-tells-the-truth-again--delivered-2026-09-02)-E.

### ☐ DEBT-237 — The AI gate names a fake-provider path that the repository deliberately does not have — P3

- **Current issue.** [ADR-112](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-112-retrieval-and-capture-velocity--one-tag-vocabulary-a-recency-source-that-is-not-activity-and-the-ai-gate-that-is-not-yet-runnable)
  decision 2 lists, among what the AI infrastructure gate proves, *"the
  disabled and fake-provider paths"*. On `main` at `036d3da` there is no
  fake-provider path to prove: [`e2e/ai-assistance.spec.ts`](../../e2e/ai-assistance.spec.ts) `:525-529`
  records *"There is no deterministic test-provider seam in this repository —
  AI-01 shipped none on purpose"*; every adapter test injects a `fetchImpl`
  against mocked HTTP (`ai-configuration.ts:96-99`,
  `test/unit/ai/adapters.test.ts:120-291`); the evaluation corpus uses a fake
  that lives only in the test tree (`test/unit/ai/evaluation.test.ts:1-11`);
  and `scripts/ai-integration-check.mjs` is wired to no npm script and no CI
  job (`:6-7`).
- **Impact.** The gate as written cannot pass as written, even with a key. A
  future session holding the secret would have to either weaken the gate's
  clause or build the seam under the pressure of a live credential — which is
  how a gate becomes a rubber stamp. Severity P3 because nothing user-facing
  depends on it until the owner-held half exists.
- **Desired future state.** A dev-only fake provider behind the existing
  `StructuredRequest → StructuredResponse` contract, selectable only when the
  runtime is explicitly configured for it (never reachable from production
  configuration, asserted the way the SSRF boundary is), and the check script
  wired as `pnpm run ai:integration-check`. The E2E off-state journeys gain
  one fake-on path. ADR-112's gate is otherwise unchanged; its full passing
  condition is stated in [`ROADMAP_V2_8.md`](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_8.md#ai-decided-again-step-3-of-the-decision-pass).
- **Closing condition.** The gate's clause (f) — disabled path and
  fake-provider path green in E2E on the same tree — is runnable on `main`
  without any secret; the remaining clauses need one.
- **V2.9 disposition — DEFERRED, unchanged (2026-09-04).** Still its own PR on its own evidence the day the secret exists; it is the first item of the V2.14 GROUNDED AI sequence ([`ROADMAP_V2_9.md`](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_9.md#v214--grounded-ai-presumptive--gated-on-the-owner-held-key)) because every Stage A feature is E2E-proven through this seam without a key.
- **Related roadmap item.** Not taken by V2.8: the code-held half of a
  tripwire, done in its own PR the day the owner's secret exists (or before,
  by a session with nothing else to do), per V2.8's LATER.

## Debt raised by the post-V2.8 product-strategy pass (2026-09-04)

The [post-V2.8 product-strategy pass](DALYHUB_POST_V2_8_PRODUCT_STRATEGY.md)
re-measured `main` at `6b4d4a8` to define [V2.9](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_9.md)
and the sequence to V3. It raised **five** entries, each a concrete gap the
measurement produced with evidence in the code or the documents, and none a
wish. Everything else it found was already in this register and received a
dated disposition on its entry instead of a new number.

### ☐ DEBT-238 — The kernel Activity contract has no time-window read, so five adapters carry their own windowed SQL — P3

- **Current issue.** `ActivityRepository` ([`app/kernel/activity/activity-repository.ts`](../../app/kernel/activity/activity-repository.ts) `:53-113`) exposes `getById`, `listForWorkspace`, `listForEntity` and `listForEntities`, whose inputs ([`activity.ts`](../../app/kernel/activity/activity.ts) `:136-185`) carry `type?`, `limit?` and `cursor?` — **no from/to and no bucketing**. Every read that needs a window bypasses the contract with its own `occurred_at` predicate: `d1-activity-window-repository.ts:169-186, 414-417` (FOLLOW-01/02), `d1-review-insight-repository.ts:208-215, 346-347` (the Review trend and contributions), `d1-project-health-repository.ts:288-298` (`MAX(occurred_at)`), `d1-recent-records-repository.ts` and `d1-meeting-repository.ts`. The `(workspace_id, type, occurred_at, id)` index (`migrations/0004_create_activities.sql`) already serves all of them.
- **Impact.** Five hand-written window predicates over the one append-only stream is five places a timezone or half-open-interval rule can drift. Beside them, the Task completion count that reads the right authority — `countCompletedTasksInWindows` over `spine_records.completed_at` (RECALL-02, ADR-114), which `task.completed` events must never stand in for because they survive a reopen — has no bucketed form, so "completions per week for twelve weeks" has no source. Every history question Reports and grounded AI will ask is a further copy unless each read exists once.
- **Desired future state.** Two kernel Activity reads — `countByTypeInBuckets({ types, window, grain })` and `listInWindow({ window, types?, limit, cursor })` — and one Task read, `countCompletedInBuckets({ window, grain })` over `spine_records.completed_at`, each one grouped statement whatever the window, with the five callers converged on the Activity reads and enumerated by a contract test, and Task series never derived from Activity.
- **Closing condition.** The two reads exist on the kernel contract with counting-DB flatness proofs; `grep` finds no `occurred_at` window predicate in an adapter outside the Activity repository; the five named callers read through the contract with parity asserted on the same fixture before and after.
- **Related roadmap item.** [V2.9 INS-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_9.md#-ins-01--the-history-kernel--closes-debt-238-debt-239).

### ☐ DEBT-239 — Analytics' range vocabulary is three presets bucketed to fit the Review's eight-period cap, and there is no shared window, grain or series primitive — P3

- **Current issue.** `ANALYTICS_RANGES` ([`app/kernel/analytics/analytics-range.ts`](../../app/kernel/analytics/analytics-range.ts) `:44-70`) is exactly `week` (7×1 day), `month` (4×7 days) and `quarter` (6×14 days); the module header (`:20-27`) records that bucketing was chosen to fit `MAX_TREND_PERIODS = 8` (`review-insight-repository.ts:63`) because Analytics reuses the Review's grouped aggregate. `rangeBuckets` (`:157-176`) is module-private; there is no `Grain`, no `Series` type and no bound flag a second consumer could reuse. The one shared period abstraction, `ActivityWindow` (`activity-window.ts:41-52`), is good and is not the problem.
- **Impact.** "Completions per week over twelve weeks" and "per month over a year" are not askable; the quarter range buckets fortnightly, which nobody thinks in; Projects and Goals completed have no line; and Finance's month-by-category, Reports' every series and AI's fact blocks would each grow their own bucketer — the second copy of a fact the kernel already holds, which ADR-079 d2 exists to prevent.
- **Desired future state.** `Window` (the existing `ActivityWindow`), `Grain` (day / week / month / Review period), `bucket(window, grain)` with the backward-from-the-end rule and a stated maximum per grain, and `Series<Point>` carrying its bound — in one kernel slice, consumed by Analytics, the Review and every later domain.
- **Closing condition.** The primitive exists with unit tests over week-start and month-end edges in the owner's timezone; Analytics offers an explicit window and grain over it; `rangeBuckets` is gone or is a thin alias; the Review's `readSeries` keeps its asserted statement count through it.
- **Related roadmap item.** [V2.9 INS-01](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_9.md#-ins-01--the-history-kernel--closes-debt-238-debt-239) (the primitive) and [INS-03](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_9.md#-ins-03--insight-with-a-real-range--closes-the-caller-half-of-debt-212) (the range).

### ☐ DEBT-240 — An obligation cannot exist without an Asset parent and carries no amount — P3

- **Current issue.** `asset_obligations` ([`migrations/0025_asset_history_and_obligations.sql`](../../migrations/0025_asset_history_and_obligations.sql) `:97-187`) declares `asset_id TEXT NOT NULL` with a composite foreign key into `entities (workspace_id, id, type)` constrained to `'asset'`, so the database refuses an obligation with no Asset; it has no `amount_minor` or `currency_code` column — money appears only at completion, as `asset_events.cost_minor`. There is no `obligation` entity type in any module manifest, so an obligation is not linkable, not searchable and not a subject of Activity in its own right. The machinery around it — a closed category set, `lead_days`, a recurrence chain, one-batch completion with a proof event and a successor (ADR-083), the 30/7/1 notification rungs, one Today attention row deduplicated against an open linked Task — is the right shape and is measured as such in [the strategy](DALYHUB_POST_V2_8_PRODUCT_STRATEGY.md#42-life-admin--obligation-is-the-domain-not-a-pile-of-screens).
- **Impact.** A tax return, a passport renewal, a gym membership, a school fee or a subscription has nowhere to live but a recurring Task with no amount, no evidence, no renewal history and the wrong recurrence engine — or a fake Asset created to hold it. The product's answer to "what do I need to deal with?" is therefore limited to things that are Assets, and any Finance "recurring commitment" built before this is fixed would be a second due-and-recurring model.
- **Desired future state.** Obligation is an entity type with an optional subject — a nullable foreign key to `entities` (any kind) for structural reads **and** a reserved typed EntityLink written in the same transaction, on the Meeting-item → Task precedent (ADR-083), so the subject's record and timeline show it — and an optional expected amount in minor units under ADR-049; the Assets record's Obligations tab is a lens over the shared records; one kernel authority for urgency, completion and succession.
- **Closing condition.** A subject-less obligation with an amount can be created, completed with an actual amount, and appear on Today's attention row only when not tracked by an open Task; every former Asset obligation reads identically on its Asset before and after the migration, proven by moving a restored production artefact through it.
- **Related roadmap item.** [V2.10 LIFE ADMIN](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_9.md#v210--life-admin-planned) (PLANNED — defined by its own pass); [ADR-116](../decisions/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md#adr-116-the-post-v28-domain-boundaries--one-obligation-model-for-life-admin-and-finance-deterministic-facts-before-ai-explanation-saved-reports-before-dashboards-and-no-domain-without-its-export) decision 1.

### ☑ DEBT-241 — No documentation link or anchor check exists, and 447 local links are broken — P2 — **RESOLVED 2026-09-04 (V2.9 INS-00)**

- **Current issue.** There is no `docs:*` script in `package.json`, no link or anchor validation in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, and `docs/` is in `.prettierignore` — so the only gate a documentation-only change meets is a Prettier run that does not read it. **Measured 2026-09-04** with a temporary checker over every `docs/**/*.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `README.md`: **6,601 local links, 447 broken** — 254 anchors that no longer resolve (chiefly register entries whose headings gained a `— **RESOLVED …**` suffix, and ADR titles amended after they were linked; eleven of them in `ROADMAP_V2_8.md` alone, all to entries V2.8 itself resolved), 43 missing non-image files, and 150 missing screenshots under `docs/design/assets/`. The most-linked file, this register, carries 115 of the failures.
- **Impact.** The repository is the product's memory by constitution (`AGENTS.md` §0) and its documents are held together by anchors; a link that lands on the top of a 4,900-line file instead of the entry it named is a memory defect of exactly the class V2.8 refused for the test gate. The failure is silent, it compounds with every resolution, and this pass — which added a document that links into the register eighty times — could only find it by writing its own checker.
- **Desired future state.** A Static-tier check that resolves every relative link and `#anchor` with GitHub's slug rule, fails naming file, line and target, and has no allowlist; the count at zero; a recorded rule that the PR which changes a heading repairs every link to it in the same change.
- **Closing condition.** `pnpm run docs:links:check` exists, runs in CI's Static job, and reports zero findings on `main`; its slug rule is unit-tested against the register's own heading forms.
- **Resolved (V2.9 INS-00, 2026-09-04).** `scripts/docs-links.mjs check` (`pnpm run docs:links:check`) is a `Static` step beside `e2e:fixture-dates:check`, and **the count is zero**: 6,555 local links across 149 files, all resolving.
  - **Re-measured before editing, not inherited.** The checker's own first run on this branch found **422 of 6,737** broken — 233 drifted anchors, 39 missing non-image files, 150 missing screenshots. That is 25 fewer than the entry's 447 because the defining pass's own repairs had landed and because this checker reads reference definitions and nested image-links the temporary one did not. The classes are the ones this entry named.
  - **How each class was repaired.** 233 anchors were rewritten **at the link** — 213 mechanically, where exactly one heading in the target file extended the broken anchor (the `— **RESOLVED …**` drift) or shared its `DEBT-NNN`/`ADR-NNN` identifier, and 20 by hand where the target heading had been rewritten or the document retired (`THEME_ACCEPTANCE_MATRIX.md` is now a two-section stub; `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`'s `#design-tokens-ds-01` is now `#foundations--…`). No heading was renamed back. 39 missing non-image paths were code files that had been retired or renamed: `responsive.spec.ts` (split by CONV-03) and `ASSET-03`'s asset folder were re-pointed, and the rest — `theme-preference.ts`, `TodayDashboard.tsx`, `task-selection.ts`, `menu-placement.ts`, `CaptureFab.tsx`, `today/routes/plan.tsx` — were unlinked to plain code text naming the pass that removed them. **150 missing screenshots: not one image was invented.** Every referenced folder was checked against `git log --all` and had never been committed, so each reference became prose saying what the capture showed, derived from its alt text, its filename and the surrounding analysis.
  - **Falsified before it was trusted.** On a scratch tree, breaking one anchor (`AGENTS.md#12-development-workflow` → `#12-development-workflows`) and one path (`docs/README.md` → `docs/READMEE.md`) made `Static` fail naming file, line and target for both; reverting made it green. Sixteen further cases are pinned as unit tests, including that a link inside a fenced block, a code span or an HTML comment is not a reference.
  - **The rule is recorded** in [`AGENTS.md` §12](../../AGENTS.md#12-development-workflow), in [this register's "how to use"](#how-to-use-this-register) and in [`SETUP_AND_CI.md`](../development/SETUP_AND_CI.md#documentation-links-v29-ins-00): the PR that changes a heading repairs every link to it in the same change, and Static proves it. No allowlist, no annotation, no escape.
- **Related roadmap item.** [V2.9 INS-00](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_9.md#-ins-00--the-map-tells-the-truth--delivered-2026-09-04--closes-debt-241). The eleven `ROADMAP_V2_8.md` anchors were repaired by the defining pass, in the same change that raised this entry.

### ☐ DEBT-242 — No workspace or account deletion path exists — P3

- **Current issue.** Settings → Privacy & data lists it by name among things not built: *"Import from other products, file attachments, AI-provider credentials, integrations, notifications, reminders, **workspace deletion**, roles and billing are not built yet."* ([`app/modules/settings/routes/index.tsx`](../../app/modules/settings/routes/index.tsx) `:1411-1419`). Export exists in two forms and restore in one; the only permanent-deletion path anywhere is Areas' guarded purge with an audit tombstone (ADR-046); sign-out clears reproducible device data only, by design (ADR-082 decision 8).
- **Impact.** None today for a single owner who controls the Cloudflare account — deletion is `wrangler d1 delete` plus bucket removal. It becomes a stated requirement the moment Finance rows and attachments raise the sensitivity of what would be deleted, and the strategy's security section names it so it is decided rather than discovered.
- **Desired future state.** Either a guarded in-product purge on the ADR-046 pattern (typed confirmation, a verified safety backup first, an audit tombstone, the R2 objects included), or a recorded decision that deletion is the owner's infrastructure act with the exact commands documented in `BACKUP_AND_RESTORE.md`.
- **Closing condition.** One of the two, dated, with the Settings copy changed to say which.
- **Related roadmap item.** [V2.16 CONSOLIDATE](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_9.md#v216--consolidate-presumptive--the-v3-readiness-release); re-rated at [V2.12](../roadmap/ROADMAP_V2_9.md#v212--finance-core-planned--gated-on-debt-198)'s definition if Finance's pass finds it must precede money.

